top_10.title: Flaky: test_ws_bash_keeps_a_profile_appended_prompt_command and test_ws_bash_restores_an_inherited_prompt_command fail on the ubuntu-26.04 runner image
top_10.body:
## What

Two PTY integration tests fail on every run of the `kirocrew-linux-4-core` runners with `Image: ubuntu-26.04` (version `20261103.629`):

- `test/test_terminal_handler_pty_integration.py::TestTerminalWsIntegration::test_ws_bash_keeps_a_profile_appended_prompt_command`
- `test/test_terminal_handler_pty_integration.py::TestTerminalWsIntegration::test_ws_bash_restores_an_inherited_prompt_command`

Failure lines:

```
AssertionError: the profile's own PROMPT_COMMAND element did not survive the readiness hook's self-withdrawal.
AssertionError: the gateway's exported PROMPT_COMMAND was not restored after the readiness hook withdrew
```

The PTY tail shows `__systemd_osc_context_precmdline` and `OSC 3008` sequences. That image's bash profile appends its own systemd `PROMPT_COMMAND` element, which the tests do not expect.

## Why

Backend Tests (3.12, 7) goes red on unrelated PRs, and Coverage Gate fails closed behind it, so PR Readiness blocks. A rerun lands on the same image and fails again.

## Additional Context

- OS: Linux, `ubuntu-26.04` runner image.
- Seen on #36815 (heads `720eb61`, rerun included, and `689acf5`): https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/43760844876/job/132958102857
- Same two tests on another PR: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/43722317344
- Main's shard 7 passed in the same window on a different runner pool: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/43725366454
- Both tests pass locally, and neither file changed on main.
- Likely fix: have the tests tolerate (or strip) an image-supplied `PROMPT_COMMAND` element, or run them with a profile that the image cannot extend.

top_10.title: [doc-audit] 03-indexing.md BTreeDirectoryEntry shows Reserved field but source has Slot; StableId claimed as sole lookup key
top_10.body:
**Doc path:line:** `doc/in-depth-overview/03-indexing.md` lines 295–304

**Wrong sentence(s):**
Line 298 of the struct listing:
```csharp
    public short Reserved;
```
Line 304:
> `StableId` is the lookup key: `-1` is the convention for the PK index, positive values are `FieldInfo.FieldId` for secondary indexes, `0` is for standalone/test trees.

**Contradicting code:**
`src/Typhon.Engine/Indexing/internals/BTree.cs` lines 73–88 and 91–135

The second field is *not* `Reserved` — it is `Slot` with a full doc comment:
```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Component slot within the archetype, for the per-archetype index segments that several
/// component slots share; 0 on a per-ComponentTable segment, which hosts one component's trees only.
/// See <see cref="BTreeStableKey"/> for why the slot is part of the key (#657).
/// </summary>
public short Slot;
```
And lines 91–98 of `BTree.cs` explicitly state:
> `StableId` alone is NOT unique on a per-archetype index segment. Field ids restart at 0 for every component, so two components in the same archetype that each index their field #0 both register with StableId 0. Creation appends two distinct entries and works, but on reopen `FindInDirectory` returns the FIRST match for both trees — they end up sharing one root…

The actual lookup key is the *pair* `(StableId, Slot)` via `BTreeStableKey` (lines 104–135).

**Suggested fix:**
1. Replace `public short Reserved;` with `public short Slot;      // component slot within archetype; 0 on per-CT segments`
2. Change "StableId is the lookup key" to: "The lookup key is the pair `(StableId, Slot)`: `StableId` is `-1` for the PK index, `FieldInfo.FieldId` for secondary indexes, or `0` for standalone/test trees; `Slot` is the component's slot within the archetype, which disambiguates two components in the same archetype that share a `StableId` value (issue #657)."

top_10.title: [doc-audit] 02-storage.md states DatabaseFormatRevision is 4; source is 8
top_10.body:
## Finding

`doc/in-depth-overview/02-storage.md` has two places that claim format version 4:

- **Line 154** section header: `### The first eight pages of an empty file (format v4)`
- **Line 178** struct sample comment: `public int DatabaseFormatRevision; // currently 4 (CK-05 twins + directory-only root)`

## Source

`src/Typhon.Engine/Storage/internals/PagedMMF.cs:123`:
```csharp
internal const int DatabaseFormatRevision = 8;
```
Version history in that file: v5 = WorldTick entity keys, v6 = per-sector page verification, v8 = entity-level spatial index removed (#872 step 13).

## Impact

Anyone checking format compatibility against the doc will read the wrong constant. The struct sample is what readers copy when writing tooling against the file format.

## Fix

Update the section header to `(format v8)` and update the struct comment to `// currently 8` with a brief note about the version history (or simply remove the parenthetical comment).

issues.title: [doc-audit] tick-lifecycle WorkerCount default omits Math.Max(1, ...) floor
issues.body:
## Finding

`doc/feature-set/Runtime/tick-lifecycle/README.md` line 60:

```
| RuntimeOptions.WorkerCount | -1 (`ProcessorCount - 4`) | Worker threads ... |
```

## Source

`src/Typhon.Engine/Runtime/public/RuntimeOptions.cs`:
```csharp
internal int ResolveWorkerCount() => WorkerCount == -1 ? Math.Max(1, Environment.ProcessorCount - 4) : WorkerCount;
```

## Impact

On a 4-core (or fewer) machine the doc implies 0 workers, but the engine clamps to 1. Minor but factually wrong.

## Fix

Change the default description to `-1 (`Math.Max(1, ProcessorCount - 4)`)`.

issues.title: [doc-audit] 01-foundation.md claims AccessControlSmall has no promoter logic but TryPromoteToExclusiveAccess exists
issues.body:
**Doc path:line:** `doc/in-depth-overview/01-foundation.md` line 70

**Wrong sentence:**
> No re-entrancy. No promoter logic. Same `WaitContext` integration.

**Contradicting code:**
`src/Typhon.Engine/Foundation/Concurrency/internals/AccessControlSmall.cs` lines 366–430

The struct provides a full Shared→Exclusive promotion API:
```csharp
// line 370
public bool TryPromoteToExclusiveAccess(ref WaitContext ctx)

// line 419
public void DemoteFromExclusiveAccess()
```

The dedicated feature page (`doc/feature-set/Foundation/access-control-lock-family/access-control-small.md` line 48) already correctly notes: "continuous shared acquisitions can starve a pending exclusive/promote", so the overview and the feature page contradict each other.

The distinction worth preserving is that `AccessControlSmall` lacks *waiter preference counters* (the per-promoter-waiter tracking that the full `AccessControl` has in its high bits), so promotion can be starved — it's not that promotion is absent.

**Suggested fix:**
Replace "No promoter logic." with "Promotion is supported (`TryPromoteToExclusiveAccess`/`DemoteFromExclusiveAccess`) but has no waiter-preference counter — continuous shared acquisitions can starve a pending promote."

issues.title: Check required inputs before long agent runs
issues.body:
## Problem

Long agent runs can start without all required inputs. Text may arrive while images or other attachments do not.

The run can then complete against incomplete evidence.

Katie Parrott’s [early-access Fable 5.2 review](https://every.to/vibe-check/fable-5-2) reports an overnight agent run that analyzed slide text but missed deck screenshots. This is an observation, not an independently verified benchmark.

## Change

Add a preflight that inventories required inputs before a long EGM run begins.

The preflight must confirm that the agent can read each required input. It must distinguish text, images, and other attachments.

Stop the run with an actionable error when a required input is absent or unreadable.

## Acceptance criteria

- The run defines its required inputs before execution.
- The preflight confirms the count, type, and identity of each input.
- The preflight verifies that the agent can read each input.
- The run stops before execution when a required input is absent or unreadable.
- The run records the preflight result.
- Automated tests cover text-only input, mixed text and images, a missing image, and an unreadable attachment.

issues.title: Flaky: test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt (fixed 60 ms sleep before reading flushed frame)
issues.body:
`test/test_subagent_scale_batch.py::TestCoalescer::test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt` failed on an unrelated PR.

- Run: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/41797479802/job/126467561880 (PR #29490, head 712e6f822c65)
- OS: ubuntu, Python 3.12, Backend Tests shard 3
- Failing line: `((etype, data),) = all_frames` -> `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)`

The test waits a fixed `await asyncio.sleep(0.06)` past the 20 ms flush tick and then expects one frame. On a slow runner the flush has not happened yet, so the list is empty. It passes 8/8 locally (alone and with the whole file under -n 4). PR #29490 does not touch the coalescer or this test.

Likely fix: wait for the frame (poll with a deadline) instead of a fixed sleep.

issues.title: Church name text hidden in sidebar but still shown on login page when a custom logo is uploaded
issues.body:
## Description When a custom church logo is uploaded (Admin → System → Church Information), the church-name text is hidden in the sidebar but still shown on the login page — inconsistent behavior across the two surfaces that both render the logo. - **Sidebar** (`src/Include/Header.php`, lines ~186-199): the `navbar-brand-text` span is wrapped in `if (ChurchLogoService::hasCustomLogo())` — it only renders when there's **no** custom logo: ```php 'navbar-brand-image crm-brand-logo']) ?> ... ``` - **Login page** (`src/session/templates/begin-session.php`, lines 30-37): `ChurchLogo::img()` and `ChurchMetaData::getChurchName()` render unconditionally as separate elements, with no `hasCustomLogo()` check at all: ```php

``` Confirmed identical on both `master` and the `7.8.1` tag (same blob SHA on `begin-session.php` across both refs). The sidebar's hide-on-custom-logo behavior was intentional per #9719 ("The uploaded logo replaces the ChurchCRM branding in the sidebar (where it also hides the church-name text)") on the assumption that an uploaded logo already contains the church name as artwork. The login page not following the same rule means that assumption isn't applied consistently — admins who want the name visible lose it in the sidebar but keep it on login, with no way to choose. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Admin → System → Church Information → upload a custom logo. 2. Visit the dashboard — sidebar shows only the logo, no church name. 3. Log out and view the login page — logo **and** church name are both shown. ## Expected Consistent behavior between the sidebar and the login page — either both hide the name when a custom logo is present, or neither does. ## Reported by maestrovivo, in the project's Discord #support-chat.

The chat-ui test campaign (PR #741) found these while checking what the docs say against the code. Line numbers are at the campaign's merge base.

Today it is a `role="meter"` labelled "Memory" with a "… % full (about 6.4k of 8k tokens)" tooltip (`ContextMeter.tsx`). (PR #776: both now describe the `role="meter"` "Memory" meter and its bands)
- [ ] **architecture.md ~:2377** (Voice dictation) says the "not installed" mic deep-links with `onNavigate('models')`; since #527 it is `models:voice` (`ChatScreen.tsx` ~:2681).

Findings that were refuted, already decided in `docs/design-decisions.md`, or already filed are left out. The severity is the second reviewer's. The reproduction and suggested fix for each one are in the audit record (ask on this issue to have one posted).

issues.title: fix(ci): migrate reusable eval workflows to the Go CLI and require real automatic-run artifacts
issues.body:
## Summary

<!-- 2-4 sentences: describe the bug, feature request, documentation gap, or task. -->

The reusable `waza.yaml` workflow still installs a Python package and uses obsolete CLI/result contracts, while automatic `waza-eval.yml` runs do not resolve output defaults before execution. A successful current-main automatic evaluation run uploaded no result artifact. Migrate retained consumer workflows and examples to one tested Go CLI contract; proposed target v0.41.0.

## Type of issue

- [x] Bug
- [ ] Feature request
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Maintenance
- [ ] Question or investigation

## Agent instructions

<!-- Make this actionable for a coding agent. Include constraints, likely files, and what not to change. -->

- Goal: Every advertised reusable workflow invokes the actual Go Waza contract, preserves meaningful failures, and produces usable evidence on push/PR/dispatch/call events.
- In scope: Installation/source-version strategy, supported arguments, effective input defaults, result/output mapping, artifact verification, and corresponding CI guide/site examples.
- Out of scope: Reintroducing Python Waza, altering product exit/reporting policies to accommodate stale examples, silently changing callers' output names, or using mutable latest installs as exact-source regression evidence.
- Likely files or areas: `.github/workflows/waza.yaml`, `waza-eval.yml`, `skills-ci-example.yml`, `docs/CI-CD-GUIDE.md`, site CI documentation and workflow contract tests.
- Dependencies or related issues: Coordinate final enforcement with [#900](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/issues/900). Keep reporter product bug [#892](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/issues/892) separate; this issue fixes workflow consumption and result evidence, not the reporter implementation.

## Current behavior

<!-- What happens today? For bugs, include the actual result and error output if available. -->

[`waza.yaml`](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c/.github/workflows/waza.yaml#L48-L81) runs `pip install waza`, `--format json`, `--fail-threshold`, `waza report`, and reads `.summary.pass_rate` / `.summary.composite_score`. Current Go run accepts `default` or `github-comment` output format and writes native summary fields such as `success_rate`; there is no corresponding `cmd_report.go` command. In [`waza-eval.yml`](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c/.github/workflows/waza-eval.yml#L154-L197), `OUTPUT_FILE` reads a raw input that is empty on automatic events, but upload falls back to `results.json`. [Current-main run 41918346222](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/actions/runs/41918346222) succeeded, warned `No files were found with the provided path: results.json`, and its artifacts API returned an empty list. The CI guide repeats obsolete summary keys/actions, so documentation can propagate the mismatch.

## Expected behavior

<!-- What should happen instead? For feature requests, describe the desired outcome. -->

Resolve effective defaults once for all event types and use the same values for execution, parsing, summary, and upload. Use a reviewed Go installation/build strategy with genuine embedded dashboard assets where source builds require them. Validate result shape, completeness, and availability instead of interpreting null/missing values as zero or success. Preserve documented reusable inputs/outputs through migration or explicitly document reviewed breaking changes.

## Steps to reproduce

<!-- For bugs, provide the smallest reproducible example. Delete if not applicable. -->

1. Inspect the historical Python workflow against `cmd/waza/cmd_run.go` and `internal/models/outcome.go` at the cited SHA.
2. Read the current-main automatic run log's artifact warning.
3. Query `GET /repos/microsoft/waza/actions/runs/41918346222/artifacts` and compare the empty list with the workflow's stated result-artifact contract.

## Environment

<!-- Fill in what you know. Delete fields that are not relevant. -->

- OS: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu.
- Waza version or commit: `f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c`.
- Go version: CI specifies 1.26; stale reusable workflow provisions Python 3.11.
- Command run: Read-only `gh run view 41918346222 --log`, artifacts API, and local CLI/model source reads.

## Acceptance criteria

<!-- Use checkboxes so an agent can verify completion directly. -->

- [ ] Retained reusable workflows install/build the intended Go version and invoke supported commands and flags.
- [ ] Push, PR, workflow_dispatch, and workflow_call paths resolve identical defaults; explicit custom output/context inputs remain intact.
- [ ] Actual CLI fixtures cover passing grading, completed failing grading, task/runtime errors, missing/malformed artifacts, zero scores, and absent values without success-shaped fallbacks.
- [ ] Automatic successful runs must upload a fresh, complete result artifact; missing evidence fails rather than only warning.
- [ ] Workflow outputs and thresholds use validated current producer fields and preserve failure exit policy.
- [ ] Copied CI guide/site workflows are exercised by contract tests against actual CLI help and saved JSON; unsupported legacy actions/installation examples are migrated or explicitly retired.

## Validation expectations

<!-- List expected automated or manual checks, or say why validation is not applicable. -->

- [ ] Applicable `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `golangci-lint run`.
- [ ] `NO_COLOR=1 make test-compat` for behavior-affecting workflow/CLI contracts.
- [ ] Docs site checked, if docs changed: build and Chromium e2e; documentation example controls execute copied commands.
- [ ] Web/dashboard checks run, if `web/` changes.
- [ ] Other: event/default mutation controls and production-CLI fixture runs with a rejecting offline runtime; verify actual uploaded artifact content on current-head CI.

## Additional context

<!-- Add links, screenshots, logs, related issues, or implementation notes. -->

Research date: 2026-11-06. The Python workflow was identified statically; no third-party Python package was installed or executed. The missing automatic-run artifact is directly observed, not inferred.

issues.title: [Request] 文档：Secure Boot 开启下的自签流程（db 自签 / MOK+shim）与三个已知坑
issues.body:
> 起草说明：本文由 AI 辅助整理，事实来自仓库现状与 #145 的讨论；**没有做真机验证**（我这台没有可切 Secure Boot 的独显机位），凡未实测之处都已标注。若与现场不符，以现场为准。

### 建议类型 / Request type

文档修正 / Documentation change

### 当前问题与需求 / Current problem and need

**要解决的是文档缺口，不是功能缺口。** 想让 Secure Boot 保持开启的用户，现在在文档里只能读到一句：

- `docs/faq.md:272` / `docs/faq.en.md:263`：`替换 U 盘启动文件前先备份。Secure Boot 关闭或使用受信任的自签 EFI。`

这句话承认了自签这条路存在，但没有过程。而 [#145](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/145)（已关闭）里三条路只写全了一条：

| #145 里的方案 | 文档状态 |
|---|---|
| 方案一 休眠切换法（SB 开/关来回切） | 评论里有完整流程，未入 FAQ |
| 方案二 固件内置 FFS（PR #100） | `docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162` 有可行性，标注【待实证】 |
| 方案三 MOK + shim | 评论里有六步，未入 FAQ |
| 方案三 db 自签 | **只有"简版"一句**：每台机器手动导证书、每次更新重签 |

而现场反馈指向的恰恰是最后这条：#145 里有一条西语报告——"Conseguí firmar con un certificado propio el Efi, de modo que ha sido posible iniciar con el secure boot activado"（用自己的证书签了 EFI，因此可以在 Secure Boot 开启下启动）。这是 db 自签路线**可用**的现场证据，但它现在埋在一条已关闭的 issue 的评论区里，既没进 FAQ，也没进兼容性记录。

现实需求面也不小：#145 的原始动机是打 LoL/Vanguard（反作弊要求 SB 开启），而 `docs/community-reports.md` 里的实测行几乎每条都写着 "Secure Boot off"——SB-on 场景目前是文档空白区。

补充一点定位：这**不是**在申请"绕过 Secure Boot"。自签属 `SECURITY.md:53` 威胁模型里"已开启 Secure Boot 且已导入自签证书"的合法配置，与方案一、方案二并列，只是缺文档。

### 期望改进 / Desired improvement

新增 `docs/faq.md#secureboot`（EN 同步 `docs/faq.en.md`）一节，建议内容：

1. **两条路线对比表**：db 自签（固件直接验你的签名，代价是每台导证 + 每次重签）vs MOK+shim（不动 db，走发行版 shim）。shim 那条直接链接 #145 现有六步，不重复写。
2. **db 自签五步**：
   - 生成密钥/证书（`openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -addext "extendedKeyUsage=codeSigning"`——这个 EKU 不能省，Windows 侧 `signtool` 会校验）；
   - 签名与验证（`sbsign --key ... --cert ... --output ...`；`sbverify --cert ...`；Windows 等价物 `signtool sign /fd SHA256` + `signtool verify /pa`）；
   - 把 **DER 证书追加**进 db 的三种方式：固件 Key Management（`db → Append / Append from file`）、`efitools` 的 `efi-updatevar -a -c cert.crt -k KEK.key db`、`sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft`（`--microsoft` 才会把微软证书一并写回）；
   - 新版 maker 直接吃签名后的件：`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284`（`-BootEfi`）、`:488`（盘根）、`:494`（`EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI`），即
     ```powershell
     .\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family ad102 -Out G:\ -BootEfi .\BOOTX64.signed.efi
     ```
   - 验证：`mokutil --sb-state` 应为 `SecureBoot enabled`；固件层真正放行的铁证是盘上出现新的 `loader.log` 且含 `TX BUILD` banner。
3. **三条硬纪律**（这部分比签名本身更容易出事）：
   - **只能追加，不能替换 db 里的微软证书**——`bootmgfw.efi` 靠 *Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011* 签名，删了 Windows 起不来；
   - **动 PK 前先导出 PK/KEK/db 备份**；若板子要求清 PK 进 Setup Mode 才能 Append，事后必须把原厂证书恢复并重新 enroll PK；
   - **私钥只留本机**：db 里一旦有你的证书，这把私钥就能给这台机器签任何引导组件。
4. **三个已知坑**：
   - **SB 开着时 `ssdiag` 仍然不可用**：它临时加载的 `pmxdrv.sys` 是 Intel/COMODO 2018 交叉签名、无微软根，SB-ON 必然被 DSE 拒（`tools/ssdiag/README.md` 的 "Secure Boot — the gate that actually refuses this driver"、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`）。所以 SB 常开的机器上，系统内读回只能走 `loader.log` 的 `HANDOFF-OUT`（EFI 阶段零驱动读回）或 Linux 侧 `tools/diag-unlock.py`；要 `ssdiag --reapply` 修回锁，仍须临时关一次 SB。
   - **BitLocker / PCR[7]**：SB 或 db 状态变化会改 PCR[7]，可能弹恢复密钥，操作前先挂起保护。
   - **换版本必须重签**，签名后再改一个字节即失效；资产 `*.bin` 不需要签名（SB 只验 PE 引导链）。
5. **反作弊边界**（与 #145 的警告保持一致）：db 自签不改 SB 状态位，Vanguard（LoL）通常可过；ACE 系（腾讯）会校验 TPM/PCR[7] 链式启动记录，自签链的度量与原厂引导不同，**不保证过检**——打 ACE 系游戏请回到方案一。

顺带把 `docs/faq.md:272` / `.en.md:263` 那句改成带锚点的链接。

### 相关版本、文档与参考资料 / Versions, documentation and references

- 文档现状：`docs/faq.md:272`、`docs/faq.en.md:263`（自签仅一句）
- 讨论：#145（休眠切换法、FFS 方案、MOK+shim 六步、db 自签简版）；西语现场反馈在该 issue 评论中
- 固件形态可行性：`docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162`（SB 只验 OS 引导链）
- maker 的 boot 路径改动：`5684752`（打印可执行 copy 步骤）、`c0f3518`（输出不再纯平铺）、`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284/488/494/500/505-511`
- ssdiag 的 SB 门：`tools/ssdiag/README.md`、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`
- 威胁模型定位：`SECURITY.md:53`
- FAQ 判据/回锁值（本 issue 不涉及，仅说明读回路径不同）：`docs/faq.md:189`、`docs/cold-values.md:139`

### 替代方案与补充信息 / Alternatives and additional context

- **替代**：维持现状，让每个 SB-on 用户自己在 Discussions 问一遍。现状的代价是 #145 已经被关掉，新来的人搜不到过程。
- **更小的一步**：只把这份内容作为 #145 的补充评论贴回去——但该单已关闭，不解决"下次还能找到吗"。
- **我愿意直接出 patch**：如果维护者认可，可以照 #141 / #144 的方式提 docs PR，中英同步、只动 `docs/faq*.md`。
- **缺一个现场字段**：能否请 #145 那位西语报告者补 **主板型号** 与 **`ssdiag` 是否被拒**（第 4 条里"必然被拒"还是"通常被拒"取决于此），以及 **BitLocker 是否弹过恢复密钥**。这三项决定文档该写成硬性结论还是保守表述。

issues.title: [Report] RTX 4060 Laptop (28A0) / MECHREVO Yaoshi15Pro 2024 (GM5IX0A, i7-14650HX) - v2.1.9 TX success, matched A/B FP16 +81%, 15-inch thin laptop @ 140 W
issues.body:
## 摘要 / Summary

`10de:28a0`（AD107 · 24 SM · 8 GB）在机械革命 **耀世15Pro 2024**（i7-14650HX / 32 GB）上完成 **v2.1.9 Ada 事务**，EFI 侧读回全绿（`HANDOFF-OUT: ss0=0x88888888 ss1=0x8 readout1=0x00000000 feat_plm=0xffffffff`），Windows 正常进入。

**平台定位需要先说明**：这是一台 **15 寸轻薄游戏本**，不是同 TGP 的厚砖机。140 W 塞进这个厚度的机身，散热余量本来就是这个形态的短板——下面的 87 ℃ / 2.5 GHz 持续数据要放在这个前提下看，不代表其他 140 W 机型的水平。

同一脚本、同一 GPU 设置（140 W / 核心 +105 MHz / 显存 +200 MHz）的前后对照：

| 路径 | 解锁前 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.26 / 21.27 | **38.45** | **+81%** |
| BF16 | 21.25 / 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 / 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3 | 40.79 / 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（对照） | 6.41 / 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

绝对值比 [#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0）和 [#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882）低 13–15%，实测受 **140 W 功耗墙 + 87 ℃ 温度墙**限制（持续负载下核心 2625 → 2430 MHz），与这台 15 寸轻薄机身的散热包络相符。新增信息：28a0 的首份**同脚本匹配 A/B**，以及解锁态下的持续功耗/时钟/温度采样。

---

## 工具版本 / Tool version

- **nv-uefi-unlocker v2.1.9** 官方发布包，未做任何本地修改
- `BOOTX64.EFI` 335,872 B，SHA-256 `9D2C41F90B290AD0DA3ECF294016A7EA67638E2625D8E1B1735028298943BB5C`（与 [#35](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/35) 记录的官方 v2.1.9 同一文件）
- 资产：`-Family 40` 生成的 `ad102` family 共 8 个文件，`loader.log` 中逐个 `TX-ASSET-DIAG: ... loaded N/N bytes` 全量校验通过
- 未使用 `i_know_what_i_am_doing.txt` / `tx-quiet.txt` / `tx-select-bdf.txt` / `tx-require-d0.txt` 等任何 marker（日志中均为 `absent`）

## GPU 与平台 / GPU and platform

- **GPU**：NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU，AD107，24 SM，8192 MiB
- **PCI ID**：`10DE:28A0`，子系统 `139A:1D05`（机械革命），地址 `0000:01:00.0`；音频功能 `10de:22be @ 01:00.1`
- **VBIOS**：`95.07.3f.00.26`　**驱动**：596.49（WDDM）
- **整机**：MECHREVO **耀世15Pro 2024**（Yaoshi15Pro Series GM5IX0A），**15 寸轻薄游戏本**；Intel Core i7-14650HX；内存 32 GB
- **BIOS**：American Megatrends International `N.1.05MRO06`（2024-01-30）
- **OS**：Windows 11 Pro build 26200
- **显示拓扑**：**独显直连**，内屏由 dGPU 驱动，2560×1440 @ 240 Hz；Intel UHD Graphics 存在于系统中但无显示输出（`CM_PROB_PHANTOM`），无 eGPU、无第二块独立显卡

## 操作过程 / Procedure

1. 在目标机（本机）解压 v2.1.9 发布包，管理员 PowerShell 运行 `.\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family 40`，自动识别本机为 40 系并只生成 `ad102` 资产；`NVIDIA-kernel-module-source-610.43.03` 与 `nvidia-utils-610.43.03` 两个钉版输入按脚本校验通过
2. 把脚本列出的 7 个 `.bin` 复制到 U 盘根目录，`BOOTX64.EFI` 放入 `EFI/BOOT/`
3. BIOS 中关闭 Secure Boot；从系统「重启」→ F7 一次性菜单选 `UEFI: VendorCo ProductCode 1.00, Partition 1`
4. 版本屏按 **空格** 确认（无 armed marker，走 30 秒超时语义）
5. 事务完成后自动链回 Windows，未修改 NVRAM 永久启动顺序
6. 全程只尝试了这一次事务，无重试、无断电恢复过程

## 性能对比 / Performance comparison

**口径**：`make-usbroot.ps1` 自带前的自写脚本 `gemm_bench.py`（`torch.mm`，8192 系尺寸扫，`cudaEvent` 计时，每尺寸 5 次预热 + 3 窗口 × 20 次取中位），**解锁前后同脚本、同 GPU 设置**；解锁前为上一次启动（stock），解锁后为事务后同一次启动，两次测量间隔约 40 分钟，期间未改任何 GPU 设置。

**A/B（N=4096，TF/s）**

| 路径 | stock 第1次 | stock 第2次 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.27 | 21.26 | **38.45** | +81% |
| BF16 | 21.25 | 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 | 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3（`_scaled_mm`） | 40.79 | 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（TF32 off，对照） | 6.41 | 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 153.0 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

`FP16 / FP8` 比值：stock 0.52 → 解锁后 0.51；`FP16 / FP32` 比值：stock 3.1× → 解锁后 5.9×。三条对照（FP32、显存带宽、以及时钟本身）都持平，说明增益不是时钟或散热瞬态造成的。

**其他尺寸（解锁后，同一脚本）**：FP16 1024 → 42.51，4096 → 38.45，8192 → 35.46。

**第二套独立基准交叉验证**：用 [#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119) 附件里的 `baseline-gemm-v1.py` 原样跑（N=4096、`torch.mm(a,b,out=c)`、7 组 × 30 次、每组一个 event 窗口）：**FP16 37.587 TF/s，BF16 38.227 TF/s**，与本机自写脚本的 38.45 / 38.66 一致（差 2%）。

**持续负载（解锁后，FP16 GEMM 4096，连续 40 s）**

| 指标 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 吞吐 | 36.06 TF/s（40 s 平均） |
| 核心时钟 | 2625 → 2430 MHz，均值 **2545 MHz** |
| 功耗 | 均值 132 W，峰值 **139.8 W**（顶死 140 W TGP） |
| 温度 | 79 → **87 ℃**（控制台 `TargetTemperature` 即为 87） |

**与现有报告的对比（仅供维护者参考，不作结论）**：[#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0）stock 29.51 → 44.24；[#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882 桌面）n=4096 FP16 26.98 → 42.44。本机 stock 21.26 明显更低但增益更大（+81% vs +49% / +57%）。解锁后绝对值低 13–15%，而 **每 MHz 效率与 #119 接近**（本机 36.06 / 2545 MHz ≈ 14.2 GFLOPS/MHz；按其 44.24 反推约 3.0 GHz 得 ~14.7），因此**我倾向于认为这是 140 W 笔记本散热包络下的频率差异，而非解锁不完整**——这一条是假设，没有 ssdiag 读回佐证。

issues.title: First time contributing? Start here.
issues.body:
Welcome 👋

If you've never contributed to AiSOC before, here's the shortest path from "interesting repo" to "merged PR".

## Step 1 — See AiSOC actually running

```bash
git clone https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC && cd AiSOC
make up      # the CORE profile — the real pipeline
make smoke   # prove it: one real event in, a retrievable alert out
```

`make up` creates `.env`, generates every secret in it, creates an administrator and **prints its password once** — copy it. Then sign in at <http://localhost:3000> (API docs at <http://localhost:8000/api/docs>). `make smoke` reports PASS or FAIL for each stage, so you know the pipeline works rather than assuming it:

```
[PASS] raw telemetry accepted by ingest
[PASS] event traversed the spine and became an alert
[PASS] alert is retrievable by id from the API
```

Needs Docker Compose v2 with 8 GB memory and 20 GB free disk in the Docker VM, plus `python3` and `bash`. `make doctor` checks all of it and diagnoses a stack that won't come up. [Installation](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/installation) says what each number was measured against.

**Zero install:** [open in GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/beenuar/AiSOC?quickstart=1) and run the same commands, then click the forwarded port 3000 in the **Ports** panel.

Once it's up, `make demo` loads labelled synthetic data on top — including `/cases/INC-RT-001?tab=ledger`, a LockBit 3.0 ransomware case the agent has investigated. Click through the **Investigation Ledger** so you've seen what AiSOC does. Every seeded row carries `is_synthetic=true` and the console labels it as such.

> One thing to avoid: `pnpm aisoc:demo` brings up `infra/compose/docker-compose.demo.yml`, which is a **UI preview only** — no ingest service, no fusion service, and Kafka disabled. The file says so in its own header. It's fine for looking at the interface, but it can't tell you whether AiSOC works. Use `make up` for that.

## Step 2 — Pick a small, scoped task

The [`good first issue`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) list is the first place to look — comment on one saying you'd like to take it. It's often thin, so these standing tasks are always open:

- **Add a detection.** New rules go under [`detections/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections) with positive *and* negative fixtures in [`detections/fixtures/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections/fixtures). Read [`detections/README.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/detections/README.md) first — it explains the four tiers and what "executable" means here (a rule replayed through the real engine and watched to fire, which is not the same as a rule that detects an attack).
- **Add a connector.** One Python class per source under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors). [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md) is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real one against a free no-auth API, so you can follow it without a vendor account. Requests and votes live in the [connector wishlist (#356)](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues/356).
- **Write a hunt.** Hunt-as-Code YAML hypotheses under [`hunts/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/hunts); [Hello, hunt](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/detections/hello-hunt.md) walks through one.
- **Add a playbook** under [`playbooks/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/playbooks).
- **Fix a typo or improve a doc page** under [`apps/docs/docs/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/apps/docs/docs).

## Step 3 — Make the change, open a PR

Commits need a sign-off (`git commit -s`); `git commit --amend -s --no-edit` fixes the last one and `git rebase --signoff main` fixes a branch.

The default [pull-request template](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md) walks you through what we need. The eval-harness section is required for substrate, playbook and detection changes — tick "Not applicable" otherwise.

Two things worth knowing before your first PR, because they're enforced and they surprise people:

- **Every published claim has to be true.** If you add a link it must resolve, and if you state a number it has to come from the tree rather than from memory. CI checks a lot of this.
- **No mock or fabricated data in the authenticated product.** Seeded and synthetic data is gated behind demo mode and labelled; honest empty and error states are the default everywhere else.

If you get stuck, [open a Q&A discussion](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/discussions/new?category=q-a) — don't suffer in silence.

The full contributor guide is [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and **Your first 30 minutes** near the top of it is a four-step version of this page.

Looking forward to your first PR. 🛡️

issues.title: Connector wishlist — what should AiSOC ingest next?
issues.body:
This is the rolling wishlist for **new connectors** the community would like to see ingested by AiSOC.

## How to vote / request

- 👍 the top comment for a connector you want.
- Reply with the *exact* product name + source format (REST? JSONL? syslog? S3 export?) + a link to the vendor's API docs. A signal score helps prioritisation: how many enterprises already rely on this in their SOC?
- If you've already shipped a custom connector for AiSOC, drop it here — even unmerged forks help.

## How to *build* one

**Start with [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md)** ([on the docs site](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors/hello-connector)). It is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real, runnable connector against a free no-auth HTTP service, so you can walk every line of the contract — `schema()`, `test_connection()`, `fetch_alerts()`, `normalize()` and a smoke test — without a vendor account or an API key. [Connectors overview](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/index.md) is the companion reference.

Connectors live under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors), one Python class per source. The shape:

1. Subclass `BaseConnector` ([`base.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/base.py)) and declare a `schema()` returning a `ConnectorSchema` with the config fields your connector needs.
2. Pick a category. There are **nine**: `ai`, `cloud`, `edr`, `iam`, `ndr`, `network`, `saas`, `siem`, `vcs`.
3. Mark sensitive fields `secret=True` so the credential vault encrypts them at rest.
4. Register the class in `_CONNECTOR_CLASSES` **and `__all__`** in [`__init__.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py). Discovery is registry-based, so there is no other wiring — but two artefacts are derived from that tuple and both are `--check`-gated in CI, so regenerate and commit them or the build reds:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py   # the "N connectors" claims
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_types.py   # the console's ConnectorType union
   ```
5. Add a marketplace manifest at `plugins/<connector-id>/plugin.yaml` mirroring `schema()`, then run `pnpm marketplace:sync`.
6. Preserve all five severity tiers in `normalize()` — `info | low | medium | high | critical`. If the vendor publishes a distinct `critical`, map it to `critical`; do not collapse it into `high`.
7. Nest the vendor payload under `raw_event` (not `raw`). The ingest normalizer's canonical-envelope check keys on that, and a connector that gets it wrong falls through to the generic profile, which is how events end up archived but never promoted to alerts.

Per-connector documentation pages under `apps/docs/docs/connectors/` are **generated** by [`scripts/generate_connector_docs.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/scripts/generate_connector_docs.py), which also owns the `Connectors` list in [`apps/docs/sidebars.ts`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/sidebars.ts) between its `GENERATED CONNECTOR LIST` markers — so run the generator rather than hand-editing the sidebar. A hand-written page wins over the generated one, but it still has to mention every required and secret field; the generator appends a marker-wrapped field reference to enforce that.

## Currently most-requested (auto-curated from comments)

_Maintainers will edit this list as votes pile up. PRs always welcome — the issue tracker is just the queue._

| Source | Category | Status |
|--------|----------|--------|
| _comments below feed this table_ |        |        |

## What already ships

**87 connectors** out of the box: 22 SaaS, 18 cloud, 17 SIEM, 10 EDR, 7 IAM, 7 network, 3 VCS, 2 NDR, 1 AI. The count is derived from the registry by `python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py` and gated in CI, so check it there rather than trusting this paragraph.

The authoritative list is [`_CONNECTOR_CLASSES`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py) or the [connectors overview](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors). Not the marketplace — [`marketplace/index.json`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/marketplace/index.json) carries **77** plugin manifests against those 84 registered connectors, so it undercounts. (A missing manifest for your connector is itself a reasonable first PR.)

If your tool isn't in the catalog and you don't want to write code, **universal capture** may already cover it — webhook URLs, an email relay, CEF syslog and Splunk HEC let any vendor that can POST or send mail land events in the same OCSF stream.

issues.title: [Bug] Subtitle import silently truncates overlong end-timestamp milliseconds
issues.body:
## Reproduction

On main at 8f6c113, import this subtitle through the dubbing subtitle importer:

```srt
1
00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,1234
Hello.
```

The shared `services.srt_parser.parse_srt` returns a cue ending at 2.123 seconds and reports zero skipped cues. The fourth digit is silently discarded. With an overlong start field instead, the timing line is not recognized and the malformed cue is not counted.

## Expected

Skip and count timestamps with more than three millisecond digits, preserving subsequent valid cues. Existing one- and two-digit millisecond support should remain intact.

## Cause and validation

`_TS` captures only 1–3 digits while the timing-line suffix accepts the remaining digits as trailing style hints. Eight regression cases reproduce incorrect skipping/counting for both endpoints and both accepted separators. The end-timestamp case changes the timing instead of exposing the malformed input.

Could you assign this issue to @isnaenihidayat? I have reproduced it and am preparing the regression test and fix.

issues.title: fit.py --fit crop: crop_content_off_centre fires on evenly spread, centred motion and suggests the anchor already in use
issues.body:
Found while reviewing main at 828efbb (crop_check came in with #585).

## What happens

`fit.py --fit crop` on a frame whose motion is spread evenly and centred reports `crop_content_off_centre`, and the remedy it names is the value already in use.

```
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=1280x720:r=30:d=12 -f lavfi -i sine=f=440:d=12 \
  -c:v libx264 -g 60 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -shortest src.mp4
python3 scripts/fit.py src.mp4 --aspect 9:16 --fit crop -o out.mp4 --json
```

Result (FFmpeg 6.1.1):

```
"crop_check": {"axis": "x", "discarded_fraction": 0.6833, "motion_outside": 0.5547,
               "detail_outside": 0.587, "centroid": 0.5026, "suggested_anchor": 0.5,
               "samples": 9, "verdict": "review"}
warning crop_content_off_centre: "55% of the sampled luma motion lies in the 68% of the frame
(x axis) the crop cuts away. ... --crop-x 0.5 centres the kept window on it"
```

The centroid is 0.50, the run used the default `--crop-x 0.5`, and the suggested anchor is 0.5.

## Why

In `crop_loss()` the motion branch is `motion_outside >= CROP_MOTION_OUTSIDE_WARN` (0.5) with no allowance for how much of the frame is cut. A 16:9 to 9:16 crop discards 68% of the width, so motion spread over the whole frame (a pan, handheld footage, a busy scene) always has more than half of it outside. The detail branch already compares against the discarded share (`detail_outside - discarded_fraction >= CROP_DETAIL_EXCESS_WARN`); the motion branch does not.

## Class

An advisory fires on input that gives it nothing to act on, and suggests the setting already in use. Callers that route on the warning code will re-run or ask the user for no reason, and the warning stops meaning anything on ordinary handheld footage.

## Suggested direction

- Motion branch: require an excess over the discarded share, as the detail branch does (the existing test's box at the left edge still gives about 1.0 against 0.68), and/or
- do not name `--crop-x V` / `--crop-y V` as the remedy when V equals the anchor the run used; say that only pad or blur keeps it.
- A regression test with evenly spread, centred motion (testsrc2) expecting verdict `ok`.

#613 rewrites the same function (per-sample review points). The same rule would apply to each sample there, so this is best fixed in or right after #613 rather than in a third branch.

issues.title: After 4.0: ways to make the 42 tools efficient to use
issues.body:
Ideas for after 4.0 (#632), recorded so they are not lost. None of this starts before the 4.0 numbers have come down. Each idea names what it would save a caller.

## 1. One front door: goal, project, preview, approval, run, check

Today an agent picks among 42 tools and about 1,100 flags, and the routing evals show that choosing the tool is where runs go wrong more often than the tool itself. A single entry point takes a goal in a few fields (source, platform, what to keep, captions or not), writes a `render.py` project, shows the plan and a low-resolution preview, waits for a yes, runs, and ends with `check.py`. The 42 tools become what the project is made of, not what the caller has to choose between.

Saves: tool choice, flag choice, the forgotten final check.

## 2. One encode for a chain of steps

After the rebuild each tool declares what it reads, writes and applies, so a chain (cut, reframe, captions, loudness, delivery preset) can be checked end to end before anything runs and, where the steps allow it, folded into one ffmpeg command. Today a chain is several encodes: slower, and each generation costs quality. Related: #357.

Saves: time (roughly one encode per step removed) and generation loss.

## 3. Fewer verbs on the surface

Present about eight verbs to a caller (trim, frame, sound, text, look, check, deliver, assemble) and keep the 42 tools as their modes. MCP already advertises a core set of 12; this goes one step further and makes the grouping the documented way in. `SKILL.md` gets shorter, which is also a standing constraint (its size budget).

Saves: routing mistakes, context spent on tool lists.

## 4. Deliver as one step

`deliver --platform X` = export preset, loudness to spec, content checks (black, frozen, silence, dropouts), size limit, and a contact sheet, with one result document. Related: #575, #579.

Saves: the three or four follow-up calls every delivery needs today.

## 5. Edit on a proxy, conform at the end

Long or 4K sources: do every decision (cuts, crops, caption placement) on a small proxy with fast encodes, record the decisions in the project, and apply them once to the original. `proxy.py` and plans exist; the missing part is carrying the decisions across.

Saves: most of the waiting on long sources.

## 6. The project file as the memory of an edit

Every step appends to one project file: what was asked, what ran, what was measured. Re-running, undoing one step, or handing the edit to a person or another agent starts from that file instead of from a chat history.

Saves: redoing work after a context loss; makes review possible (#581).

## 7. Show, do not describe

After each step that changes the picture, attach a frame or a contact sheet and the before/after numbers automatically, so the caller checks the result instead of trusting `verified`. Related: #581, #570.

Saves: the errors nobody sees until the upload.

## 8. Learn which tools are used

An opt-in local log of which tools and flags a machine actually runs (no network). The first use is deciding what to prune or stop guaranteeing.

Saves: maintaining what nobody uses.

## Order suggested

1 and 4 first (largest effect for a caller, built from parts that exist), then 2 (needs the rebuilt engine), then 3 and 6. 5, 7 and 8 as they fit.

issues.title: neko-plugin check: missing support file fix suggests setup-repo <id>, which fails outside the plugins root
issues.body:
## Problem

When `neko-plugin check` finds a missing repository support file (`README.md`, `tests/test_smoke.py`, `.vscode/*`, `.github/workflows/*`, `.gitignore`), it suggests:

```text
fix: neko-plugin setup-repo <plugin_id> --github-actions
```

`setup-repo` resolves a bare plugin id only under the plugins root (`plugin/plugins` by default). For a plugin that lives anywhere else, which is the usual layout for a plugin with its own Git repository, the suggested command fails:

```text
[FAIL] plugin.toml not found for plugin '<plugin_id>': <checkout>/plugin/plugins/<plugin_id>/plugin.toml
```

## Where

[`release_cmd._suggest_fix`](https://github.com/Project-N-E-K-O/N.E.K.O/blob/69d8b5e52bd49b3e7db8f87c0a3be07c4031d3e3/plugin/neko_plugin_cli/commands/release_cmd.py#L606) returns `f"neko-plugin setup-repo {label} --github-actions"`, where `label` is the plugin id.

## Suggested fix

When `plugin_dir` is known, suggest the plugin path instead of the id, quoted so that paths with spaces work in bash, PowerShell and cmd:

```python
target = f'"{plugin_dir}"' if plugin_dir is not None else label
return f"neko-plugin setup-repo {target} --github-actions"
```

#3808 uses the same form for its new stale agent-kit hint. Extend a `check` test with a plugin outside the plugins root and assert that the suggested command succeeds.

Impact: only the suggested command text; `check` results and exit codes are unaffected.

Context: found while working on #3808, which leaves this for a separate change.

— DevNeko (assisted by Claude Opus 5.5)

issues.title: neko-plugin skill text guards: code-fence tracking ignores nested fences
issues.body:
## Context

`plugin/tests/unit/test_neko_plugin_agent_guides.py` (added in #3806) guards the neko-plugin skill text with simple regexes. Its `_FENCE` pattern toggles "inside a code fence" on any line starting with ``` or ~~~, regardless of the opening fence's character or length.

## Limitation

If a skill document nests fences (a four-backtick or `~~~` block wrapping a three-backtick example), the inner fence line closes the outer block early. Two checks share `_FENCE` and are affected:

- the `[checkout only]` section detection (a `#` comment inside the outer block could be read as a heading);
- the scan for bare `neko-plugin <subcommand>` lines inside code fences, so an unregistered subcommand after the inner fence would not be reported.

No skill file or agent-guide template uses nested fences today, so nothing is missed now. This was raised in review of #3806 and deliberately left out to keep the guard simple.

## Suggested fix (when a nested example is first added)

Track the opening fence's character and length, and close only on a line with the same character, at least that length, and nothing but whitespace after it (CommonMark rule). Add a nested-fence regression case for both checks.

issues.title: Telegram bot webhook mode cannot start: run_webhook is awaited but synchronous; webhook_port ignored
issues.body:
## What happens

Telegram bots in webhook mode (`webhook_url` set) cannot start.

`TelegramBot.start()` in `src/praisonai-bot/praisonai_bot/bots/telegram.py` (~L1508) does:

```python
await self._application.run_webhook(listen="0.0.0.0", port=8443, ...)
```

In python-telegram-bot 20+ (`>=20.0` is the declared floor; 22.5 checked), `Application.run_webhook` is a **synchronous** call that starts and owns its own event loop. Calling it from inside the bot's running loop fails, and its `None` return cannot be awaited.

## Second defect

The port is hardcoded to `8443`, so `BotConfig.webhook_port` (default `8080`) and the YAML `webhook_port` field are ignored.

## Fix

Inside the existing loop, use the async pieces instead: `await app.initialize()`, `await app.updater.start_webhook(listen=..., port=config.webhook_port or 8443, url_path=..., webhook_url=...)`, `await app.start()`, and the matching stop calls in `stop()`. Add a test that starts webhook mode against a mocked `Updater` and checks the configured port is used.

issues.title: Qwen3.8 campaign: separate recipe from load path for the loadpath-333 concept arm
issues.body:
The `loadpath-333` stage of `scripts/qwen38_a100_campaign.py` qualified the Qwen3.8-27B composite (ImageTextToText) load path on one 80 GB A100 at main `b9252dc`. The runner's overall verdict was **FAIL**, and the only cause was the concept arm's quality gates.

## What passed
- Pristine text-backbone logit parity between CausalLM and ImageTextToText was exact (max abs error 0.0, top-token agreement 1.0).
- Memory admission with the vision weights passed (+0.92 GB).
- The refusal edit on the composite path passed every gate.
- Edited checkpoints of both arms reload under both auto classes.
- GSQ resolves the text backbone (496/496).

## What failed
The concept arm `user/campaign-pain-pilot` (diff_means) used `layer_select: preset all`, so it excised the direction at all 64 layers, including 0–3 and the last layers. Its controls were underpowered (n=20) and validation returned `fail`. The edited model degenerated:
- perplexity 3.15 → about 3.0e5;
- coherence 0 and capability 0/6;
- invalid outputs 0% → 83%;
- refusal 94.5% → 0%.

This looks like a recipe effect, since all-layer removal of a weak pilot direction is expected to be destructive. But the run had no causal-path control for this arm, so path-independence is not demonstrated.

## Proposal
Add a way to separate the two. Either:
- rerun the concept arm with data-driven layer selection (`cv_auc`); or
- run the concept arm once on the CausalLM path with the same recipe.

Record which variant ran in the stage evidence. Quality gates should keep reporting without vetoing the operator's edit.

issues.title: Phase memory admission cannot model the qwen3_5_text recurrent scan workspace
issues.body:
On Qwen3.8-27B (`qwen3_5_text`, hybrid linear-attention), every concept and edit phase logs this warning and then proceeds in default mode:

PHASE MEMORY ADMISSION WARNING: phase '<baseline|probe|validate|excise|verify>' on cuda:0; estimated shortfall 0 bytes (0.00 GiB) plus unknown demand; ... unmodelled demand: Cannot model phase demand: ValueError: unmodelled qwen3_5_text recurrent scan backend: only the installed Transformers torch fallback workspace is bounded; set OBLITERATUS_PHASE_ADMISSION=off to explicitly bypass admission.
```

## Evidence
From one bf16 run on a single 80 GB A100 (main `b9252dc`, torch 2.13.0+cu130, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2, causal-conv1d 1.7.0):

issues.title: [PERF] #4989 (fix of #4955) incomplete: EXL3 BF16 native path is launch-bound - ~12 eager ops per linear for the per-row pre-scale make bf16 decode 2x slower than fp16 (8.7 vs 4.4 ms/step, 96 vs 33 us per linear on sm_120)
issues.body:
Found on `main` @ 7b8f12785, RTX 5090 (sm_120), torch 2.15 + CUDA 13.2. GPU otherwise idle.

### What is wrong
#4989 (fix of #4955) removed the host sync from the EXL3 BF16 path. Decode in BF16 (the default load dtype for Llama-3/Qwen EXL3 checkpoints) is still **2x slower than the same checkpoint in fp16**, and 2.4x slower than the dense bf16 model. The cause is now CPU launch overhead. `ExllamaV3Linear._native_bf16_input` + `_rescale_native_output` (`gptqmodel/nn_modules/exllamav3.py:411-449`) run about 10 eager tensor ops per linear per forward:
`vector_norm(inf)`, `.float()`, `div`, `frexp`, `ones_like` x2, `ldexp`, `where`, `x / scale`, `.to(fp16)`, then `result.to(fp32)`, `* scale`, `.to(bf16)`.

At decode (M=1) each of these is a microsecond-scale kernel, but each costs a full dispatch + launch on the host. `torch.profiler` over 20 calls of one `gate_proj` (4096 -> 14336): GPU time is 46 us/call (EXL3 GEMM 30 us + elementwise ~16 us), while host time is **209 us/call**. The per-call wall clock is GPU-starved.

### Numbers
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct truncated to 8 decoder layers, `EXL3Config(bits=4)` quantized with GPTQModel, AUTO -> `ExllamaV3Linear`. Batch 1, manual `DynamicCache` decode loop, CUDA-event medians:

| | decode step bs1 | decode step bs8 | prefill 2048 | `generate()` 128 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dense HF bf16 | 3.60 ms | 4.10 ms | 39.3 ms | 242 tok/s |
| EXL3 fp16 | 4.38 ms | 4.40 ms | 35.7 ms | 209 tok/s |
| **EXL3 bf16** | **8.67 ms** | 8.55 ms | 46.4 ms | **111 tok/s** |

Single `mlp.gate_proj`, M=1, wall clock per call (200 calls, synchronized at the end): bf16 **96.2 us**, fp16 33.0 us. Wrapping the two helpers in `torch.compile` only reaches 86 us (still dispatch-bound) and is bit-identical to the current output. CUDA-event per-module times: q/o/gate/down at M=1 are 112/106/115/119 us in bf16 vs 42/42/57/59 us in fp16 (dense bf16: 23/23/80/83 us).

### Repro
```python
m = GPTQModel.load("<EXL3 4-bit Llama-3.1-8B ckpt>", backend=BACKEND.AUTO, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
lin = m.model.model.layers[0].mlp.gate_proj            # ExllamaV3Linear
x = torch.randn(1, 1, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
import time
with torch.inference_mode():
    for xx in (x, x.half()):
        for _ in range(10): lin(xx)
        torch.cuda.synchronize(); t = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(200): lin(xx)
        torch.cuda.synchronize(); print(xx.dtype, (time.perf_counter() - t) / 200 * 1e6, "us")
# torch.bfloat16 96.2 us / torch.float16 33.0 us
```

### Suggested fix
Do the pre-scale in one launch: a small fused CUDA/Triton op computing the row amax, the power-of-two scale and the fp16 cast, writing `x_fp16` and `scale`. Do the rescale in one more fused op, or fold it into the EXL3 GEMM epilogue (it is a per-row multiply). That brings bf16 down to two extra launches per linear instead of about 12. The math stays bit-identical: power-of-two scaling, then one rounding.

### Test that should have caught it
#4989's test asserts there is no host sync. Nothing compares bf16 vs fp16 EXL3 decode latency. An M=1 bound such as "bf16 <= 1.3x fp16 per linear" would catch the launch overhead.

### Severity
Medium [PERF]: the default dtype of EXL3 Llama/Qwen checkpoints decodes at half the speed of fp16.

issues.title: [DocDB] yb-master never starts again after the fd limit is restored, once a start hit Too many open files in sys catalog bootstrap: WAL files missing
issues.body:
Jira Link: [DB-26572](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-26572)
## Description

A yb-master that runs out of file descriptors once during sys catalog bootstrap can be left unable to start again, even after the fd limit is back to normal. Running out of fds is only the trigger, and that start failing is expected. The bug is what follows. Every later start, with the normal fd limit restored, fails WAL replay with `WAL files missing`, so the master needs manual recovery. There is no power loss and no crash, only one start that hit EMFILE.

Seen on 2024.2.12.0-b52 (aarch64, Linux), with `durable_wal_write` on.

### Observed

The start that runs out of fds dies with:

```
F master_main.cc:144] IO error (yb/util/env_posix.cc:1125): Unable to initialize catalog manager: Failed to initialize sys tables async: <fs_data_dir>/yb-data/master/wals/table-sys.catalog.uuid/tablet-00000000000000000000000000000000: Too many open files (system error 24)
```

Earlier in that same start the log shows, in this order:

```
Bootstrap replayed 1/1 log segments. Read operations: 573, ... Last read committed op id: 1.573, last entry metadata: { ... offset: 259550 ... }
ReplayState: Previous OpId: 1.573, Committed OpId: 1.573, ... Flushed Regular: 1.573, ...
.../wal-000000001: Truncating file from size: 258048 to size: 258048. Preallocated size: 0. Size on disk: 1048576
Successfully rebuilt footer for segment: .../wal-000000001 (valid entries through byte offset 259708)
```

Every start after that, with the normal fd limit, fails:

```
F master_main.cc:144] Illegal state (yb/tablet/tablet_bootstrap.cc:1703): Unable to initialize catalog manager: Failed to initialize sys tables async: Failed log replay. Reason: WAL files missing, or committed op id is incorrect. Expected both term and index of prev_op_id to be greater than or equal to the corresponding components of committed_op_id. prev_op_id=1.566, committed_op_id=1.573
```

The EMFILE start had replayed the WAL through op 1.573, so the WAL was complete before that start. After it, the segment ends at op 1.566.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start 3 yb-masters (RF=3) and 1 yb-tserver on one host with `--durable_wal_write=true --log_segment_size_mb=1`.
2. Keep sys catalog writes going with a CREATE TABLE / DROP TABLE loop in ysqlsh.
3. Run `yb-admin flush_sys_catalog`, then stop one follower master.
4. Start it again. When its open fd count reaches N during startup (N=37 in the run that reproduced), run `prlimit --pid <pid> --nofile=<N+8>:`.
5. After it dies with `Too many open files`, start it again with the normal fd limit.

The window is narrow. It reproduced in 1 of 11 such starts on RF=3. Most EMFILE starts die at other points and restart fine.

Controls on the same setup:
- kill -9 at the same startup points: 15 restarts, none failed to start.
- Restarts with no fault: 4, none failed to start.

In a longer run the same thing happened during a rolling upgrade. A master lost about 40 sys catalog ops (`prev_op_id=32.4264, committed_op_id=33.4304`) and never started again.

### Expected

A start that fails with EMFILE should not change the WAL so that later starts cannot replay it. The next start with a normal fd limit should come up.

### Related

#34197 has the same replay error, but after power loss.

issues.title: CLI exposes raw traceback when a DeepSeek connection fails
issues.body:
## Summary

When the DeepSeek provider connection fails, the terminal CLI prints a full Python traceback and exits instead of showing a concise actionable error.

## Environment

- `waku-agent 0.1.12`
- Python 3.14 on Linux
- `WAKU_PROVIDER=deepseek`
- Waku Memory disabled

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a valid DeepSeek API key.
2. Start Waku with `WAKU_PROVIDER=deepseek waku`.
3. Send a prompt when the provider connection encounters a transport/TLS failure.

## Actual behavior

The retrieval gate reports a fail-open event such as:

```
gate · retrieve — gate failed open (APIConnectionError)
```

The main model request then raises `openai.APIConnectionError`, and the CLI prints the complete Python traceback, including HTTP client internals.

## Expected behavior

- Keep the retrieval gate's fail-open behavior if that is intentional.
- Catch the main provider connection error at the CLI boundary.
- Print a short actionable message, for example:

```
error: model connection failed; check network or proxy settings and retry
```

- Exit non-zero.
- Preserve technical details in the local trace or an explicit debug mode rather than printing them by default.

## Scope

The underlying TLS EOF may be environmental or upstream-related. This report is specifically about graceful CLI handling of an expected provider connection failure, not an attribution of the transport failure itself.

issues.title: [FEA]: Configurable extra HTTP headers for the openai-compatible provider
issues.body:
## Problem to solve

Some OpenAI-compatible gateways reject requests that lack a routing header. OpenCode Go is one: a request from SkillEvaluator's chat client (`rubric-eval`, Tier 1 LLM checks, the judge) returns

```
HTTP 400  MissingSessionID: Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently.
```

even for a minimal chat completion, so `SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` cannot be used with that gateway. SkillEvaluator already supports OpenCode as a Tier 3 agent (see #763), but the evaluator's own LLM client has no way to send custom headers; the only `extra_headers` use in `inference/client.py` is an Anthropic beta flag.

## Proposed approach

Add `SKILL_EVAL_LLM_EXTRA_HEADERS`: a JSON object of header names to string values, sent as `default_headers` by the `openai-compatible` chat client.

- A `{uuid}` placeholder in a value is replaced with one random UUID per client, so session-routed gateways get a stable id.
- Other providers (`openai`, `nv_build`, ...) ignore the variable, so headers are never sent to native endpoints.
- Invalid JSON or non-string values fail with a clear error.

Example:

```bash
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_API_KEY=...
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_EXTRA_HEADERS='{"x-opencode-session": "{uuid}"}'
```

Alternatives considered: a dedicated `x-opencode-session` option (too gateway-specific), or a Python-only hook (not usable from CI). A prototype is ready on a branch and I will open a PR referencing this issue.

## Additional context

Out of scope: the embedding client and the Tier 3 in-container agents, which build their own clients. With the prototype, `rubric-eval` against OpenCode Go with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` completed all nine criteria. No credentials or private data are included.

issues.title: [embedding] Point integrators and coding agents at the supported surface (AGENTS.md, llms.txt, non-contract notices)
issues.body:
When a developer asks an AI coding agent to "embed GAIA in my app", nothing at the repository root points it at the supported integration surface, so it reads the code and patches the most visible hooks — `Agent`, `_execute_tool`, `process_query`. Those are internals with no stability promise, and integrations built on them break on routine releases.

**Proposal:** make the supported path the first thing both people and coding agents see.

- **`AGENTS.md`:** add an "Integrating GAIA into another application" section that names, in order, the sidecar contract, `openapi.gaia.json`, the embed guide, and the `@amd-gaia/gaia` npm client.
- **`llms.txt`** (and optionally `llms-full.txt`) on the docs site, listing those same pages.
- **Non-contract notices:** mark `Agent._execute_tool`, `process_query` and similar internals as "not a stable surface for embedding applications" in their docstrings, and add a matching banner to extension docs that use them — with a pointer to the supported alternative where one exists or is planned (e.g. #4590 for tool policy).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A coding agent asked to embed GAIA in an app is directed to the sidecar contract by files at the repository root.
- [ ] Internals commonly patched by integrators carry a visible non-contract notice.
- [ ] `llms.txt` is served from the docs site and lists the integration pages.

Part of #4589. Depends on #5173 (the embed guide) for a page to point at.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Technical details</summary>

State at `5e23720`:
- No `llms.txt` at the repo root or under `docs/`.
- `AGENTS.md` has no section on embedding GAIA; it covers contributing only.
- `.claude/skills/integrate-hub-agent/SKILL.md` is already agent-agnostic, and `hub/agents/gaia/npm/SKILL.md` covers the flagship sidecar — but both are only discoverable from inside a Claude Code session in this repo, not by an agent working in the integrator's own project.
- `_execute_tool` (`src/gaia/agents/base/agent.py`) is a private method whose docstring describes internal contracts (the `NOT_EXECUTED` sentinel, stand-ins copying it by attribute assignment) with no warning against external use.
</details>

issues.title: Middleware edits are dropped when a tool returns a CallToolResult
issues.body:
### What happened?

An `on_call_tool` middleware that edits the result after `call_next` works for ordinary tools. For a tool that returns an `mcp_types.CallToolResult`, the middleware sees its edits, but the client still receives the tool's original content and structured content. So a redaction middleware like the one below leaks whatever those tools return. Returning `result.model_copy(update=...)` instead of editing in place loses the edits too. This also happens on the 4.2.0 release.

I expected both tools to print `redacted`. The script prints:

```
plain redacted {'token': 'redacted'}
protocol s3cr3t {'token': 's3cr3t'}
```

### Example Code

```Python
import asyncio

from mcp_types import CallToolResult, TextContent

from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
from fastmcp.server.middleware import Middleware


class Redact(Middleware):
    async def on_call_tool(self, context, call_next):
        result = await call_next(context)
        result.content = [TextContent(type="text", text="redacted")]
        result.structured_content = {"token": "redacted"}
        return result


mcp = FastMCP(middleware=[Redact()])


@mcp.tool
def plain() -> dict:
    return {"token": "s3cr3t"}


@mcp.tool
def protocol() -> CallToolResult:
    return CallToolResult(
        content=[TextContent(type="text", text="s3cr3t")],
        structured_content={"token": "s3cr3t"},
    )


async def main():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        for name in ("plain", "protocol"):
            result = await client.call_tool(name)
            print(name, result.content[0].text, result.structured_content)


asyncio.run(main())
```

### Version Information

```Text
FastMCP version:                                 4.2.1.dev5+8c0e10ff
MCP version:                                                   2.3.0
Python version:                                              3.12.16
Platform:                               macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit
```

issues.title: Delegate route guard rejects valid YAML 1.1 directive and indentless block sequences
issues.body:
OMH 4.0.6 and current main (6906258099fda4065c98fa13addca6663af06c13) reject valid Hermes configuration with config_unreadable before any delegate dispatch. Two independent minimal inputs:

```yaml
%YAML 1.1
---
delegation:
  model: example
```

```yaml
fallback_providers:
- model: example
  provider: custom
delegation:
  model: example
```

Installed Hermes 0.23.0 hermes_yaml.safe_load accepts both. scan_config in src/plugin_bundle/omh/route_endpoint_guard.py treats the directive and the indentless sequence entry as unexpected root keys. Removing only one form from a document containing both still refuses. Formatting both away in memory preserves parsed values and passes the guard.

Proposed fix: recognize a single leading YAML 1.1 directive followed by document start, and indentless sequences under untracked empty root keys. Continue refusing multiple documents, duplicate keys, sequence-valued model/delegation, unsupported directives and endpoint ambiguity. A local patch passes 11 new regression cases plus the existing routing/endpoint suites; carried as a hash-guarded Nix compatibility patch rather than rewriting user configuration.

issues.title: [BUG]: Script lint skips valid UTF-8-BOM Python scripts and reports them as passed
issues.body:
### What happened?

The advisory script linter silently skips a valid Python file when it begins with a UTF-8 byte-order mark. On SkillEvaluator `96f03c1abf0e801a1d062d67737f35465c6df219` (version 0.9.0), the same `import sys\nprint(sys.argv)\n` source produces `flat_script`, `missing_shebang`, and `no_input_validation` findings without the BOM. With `EF BB BF` prefixed, the CLI produces no findings and says `All 1 script(s) passed lint checks`. Both runs exit 0 because this lint is advisory.

### Reproduction steps

Create a temporary valid skill with `scripts/example.py` containing `import sys\nprint(sys.argv)\n`, then run:

```bash
skillevaluator lint-scripts /tmp/plain-skill -r json -o /tmp/plain-report
```

Write the same source bytes prefixed by `EF BB BF` into a second skill and run the command with a different output directory:

```bash
skillevaluator lint-scripts /tmp/bom-skill -r json -o /tmp/bom-report
```

Inspect `results[0].findings` and `results[0].success_details` in the JSON reports. The plain file has three advisory findings; the BOM file has none and is reported as passed. Both commands return 0. The behavior was reproduced through the public CLI on the commit above using a temporary synthetic fixture.

Expected: a single initial UTF-8 BOM does not prevent AST checks from running; the advisory severity and exit behavior stay unchanged.

### SkillEvaluator version or commit

`96f03c1abf0e801a1d062d67737f35465c6df219` (`0.9.0`)

### Environment

- macOS arm64
- Python 3.13.15
- uv development environment (`uv sync --frozen --python 3.13 --all-extras`)
- Synthetic local skill; no provider or credentials

### Before submitting

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct.
- [x] I searched open issues for a duplicate. Related historical BOM reports concern `SKILL.md` frontmatter, not Python script lint.

issues.title: [BUG]: Task-list helper loses task text and changes saved status when descriptions contain status words
issues.body:
### What happened?

The bundled task-list helper accepts a task description containing status-shaped parenthetical text, but `list` interprets a matching word inside the description as the serialized status. For example, adding `Investigate (completed) labels after merge` creates a pending task with the full description. The next `list` reports it as completed with description `Investigate`, then rewrites the Markdown state file with that corrupted task.

Expected: only the final serialized status suffix should determine status; the full description should remain unchanged after listing and reloading.

### Reproduction steps

On commit `abac7c5f575d646cd0d8fe1c5fb7edcc3a46af70`, use a fresh temporary state path:

```sh
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
export TASK_LIST_STATE_PATH="$tmpdir/todo.md"
uv run --no-sync python src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/task-list/scripts/tasks.py add --content 'Investigate (completed) labels after merge'
uv run --no-sync python src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/task-list/scripts/tasks.py list
cat "$TASK_LIST_STATE_PATH"
```

Observed: `list` prints `Completed` and truncates the description to `Investigate`; the saved file moves the task to the Completed section. The commands use only a synthetic local task and require no credentials or provider access.

### SkillEvaluator version or commit

`0.9.0`, commit `abac7c5f575d646cd0d8fe1c5fb7edcc3a46af70` (upstream `main` at reproduction).

### Environment

macOS 26, arm64, Python 3.13.15; source checkout, run with the repository's `uv` environment.

### Before submitting

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have searched the [open issues](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Abug) and found no duplicate of this report

issues.title: [BUG]: Packaged API caller builds invalid URLs for scalar path values containing spaces or reserved characters
issues.body:
### What happened?

The packaged API caller substitutes an OpenAPI path parameter with its raw string value. A plain `id=plain-id` works, but `id=red blue` produces `/items/red blue`; the CLI fails with `URL can't contain control characters` before the loopback endpoint receives the request. Reserved characters in scalar identifiers can also become URL syntax instead of remaining path data.

Expected: each scalar path value is encoded as one path segment while the authored path separators and query parameters remain unchanged.

### Reproduction steps

Using a synthetic OpenAPI fixture served only on loopback, define `GET /items/{id}` with operation ID `getItem` and a server URL of `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Then run from the repository root:

```sh
uv run --no-sync python src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/api-caller/scripts/call_api.py \
  --spec http://127.0.0.1:<port>/openapi.json --operation getItem --params '{"id":"plain-id"}'
uv run --no-sync python src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/api-caller/scripts/call_api.py \
  --spec http://127.0.0.1:<port>/openapi.json --operation getItem --params '{"id":"red blue"}'
```

Observed on the current checkout: the plain control exits 0 and the loopback server receives `/items/plain-id`; the space value exits 1 with an invalid-URL control-character error and never reaches the endpoint. The fixture and requests are local and require no credentials or external API access.

### SkillEvaluator version or commit

`0.9.0`, commit `64808e9b01073643e76da212ff3a7781a1a514ec` (upstream `main` at reproduction).

### Environment

macOS 27.0.1, arm64, Python 3.13.15; source checkout, run with the repository's `uv` environment.
