issues.title: consolidate --resume refuses with COORD_LATE_PROJECTION_REFUSED after following COORD_TEARDOWN_KEPT_ONLY_COPY's own remedy
issues.body:
# Bug: consolidate --resume refuses with COORD_LATE_PROJECTION_REFUSED after following COORD_TEARDOWN_KEPT_ONLY_COPY's own remedy

## Summary

On a coord-topology mission, consolidate lands the mission and then stops at teardown because review-cycle files are untracked in the coordination worktree. Doing what the error says, committing them on the coordination branch and resuming, projects those files and then refuses permanently, naming 14 planning files the operator did not change in that commit. Teardown cannot finish without hand-merging planning files on the target, and all lane and coordination worktrees stay in place.

## Reproduction

Prerequisites: a coord-topology mission where planning artifacts were amended and re-finalized on the target branch after an earlier finalize-tasks, for example to fold analysis findings, and at least one WP review cycle.

1. `spec-kitty consolidate --mission <m> --yes`. The squash lands and all WPs reach done, then it exits 76 with `COORD_TEARDOWN_KEPT_ONLY_COPY`, listing `tasks/WPnn-*/review-cycle-N.md` as untracked in the coordination worktree.
2. As the message instructs, commit those files on the coordination branch.
3. `spec-kitty consolidate --mission <m> --resume --yes`.

Expected: the review-cycle files are projected and teardown completes.

Actual: the commit is projected, then exit 1 with `COORD_LATE_PROJECTION_REFUSED`: "14 record(s) the coordination branch changed after the merge captured the coordination tip are not landed on the target". It lists spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, the contract, quickstart, analysis-report.md, lanes.json and every WP prompt. The only commit added after the merge held review-cycle files.

## Root Cause

Not established. The listed paths differ between the coordination branch and the target because the target carries the later planning amendments, so the check appears to be treating a pre-existing branch difference as a late coordination change.

## Workaround Applied

None. The landing is complete and the mission shows all WPs done, so the worktrees were left in place. The message's remedy would mean hand-merging 14 planning files or reverting coordination commits.

## Environment

spec-kitty-cli 4.0.0rc8 from PyPI via uv tool (tag v4.0.0rc8, commit 1d1a0c04c; the index artifact records no commit, so the installed SHA is unresolved), Linux.

Related: #6791 and #6871, both closed, covered late coordination commits being lost at teardown.

issues.title: ElementTriN1 on different length-scales
issues.body:
The ElementTriN1()*ElementTriP1() works fine for me as long as the lengthscale of the system is ~1, if I change it to the order of ~ 1e-6 the results become unprecise. This seems especially for solutions which have non-zero values in both subspaces.
I've had a look on the assembly:

```python
from skfem import *

@BilinearForm
def test_form(u_n, u_p, v_n, v_p, w):
    print(u_n.max(), u_p.max())
    return u_p * v_p

mesh = MeshTri().refined(2)
basis = Basis(mesh, ElementTriN1()*ElementTriP1())
test_form.assemble(basis)

print('-' * 80)

mesh = MeshTri().refined(2).scaled((1e-6,1e-6))
basis = Basis(mesh, ElementTriN1()*ElementTriP1())
test_form.assemble(basis)
```

The first assembly has values like 
```
0.0 0.816847572980459
3.6336951459609206 0.0
```
while the second one is like
```
0.0 0.816847572980459
3633695.1459609214 0.0
```

Could this be the problem, that there are orders of magnitude between the values and eigs cannot solve the system precisely?

issues.title: Factorize the COO to CSR conversion in assemblies
issues.body:
The COO to CSR conversion in `BilinearForm.assembly` quickly becomes a bottleneck as the number of threads is increased and limits the asymptotic speedup as `nthreads` is increased. It could be interesting to investigate avenues of bypassing this conversion by building some COO data to CSR data map for the sparsity pattern of a given form+basis. 

Maybe something like (in pseudo-code, and here assuming the basis used for assembly remains the same)
```py
# Get coo_data
coo_data = self._assemble(*args, **kwargs)

# Does the COO to CSR map exist?
if self.coo_to_csr is None:
    # ... if no, use the lengthy process to calculate the matrix
    mat = COOData._assemble_scipy_csr(*coo_data)
    
    # Map (ix, jx) in DOF numbering to index in CSR data 
    global_to_csr = csr_matrix((np.arange(mat.data.shape[0]), mat.indices, mat.indptr))
     
    # Create coo_to_csr map such that `csr.data[:] = coo_to_csr @ coo.data`
    jx = np.arange(coo_data[1].shape[0])
    data = np.ones(coo_data[1].shape[0], dtype=int)
    ix = np.ravel(global_to_csr[coo_data[0][0], coo_data[0][1]])
    
    self.coo_to_csr = csr_matrix((data, (ix, jx)), shape=(mat.nnz, coo_data[1].shape[0]))
    self.csr_indices = mat.indices
    self.csr_indptr = mat.indptr
else:
    # ... if yes, use it to quickly evaluate the CSR matrix data
    mat = csr_matrix((self.coo_to_csr @ coo_data[1], self.csr_indices, self.csr_indptr))
```
The scheme above may not be the most robust because the initial assembly has to be performed on a form which is not zero on some parts of the domain. From a preliminary implementation of it however, the evaluation of `csr_matrix((self.coo_to_csr @ coo_data[1], self.indices, self.indptr))` seems to be significantly faster than the default scipy COO to CSR conversion used currently in the library, which makes subsequent assemblies faster and also increases the asymptotic speedup. In addition, the `coo_to_csr @ coo_data[1]` product could be in turn parallelized, increasing again the asymptotic speedup.

issues.title: Plugin API: a public, read-only compaction preview for a profile and model route
issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Plugins can't ask Hermes when compaction will fire for a given profile and model route. The trigger depends on the window lookup, the substring and provider-scoped `model_thresholds` ranking, the small-window floor, the output reservation, the `threshold_tokens` cap, the Codex automatic raise and the summariser ceiling, and none of that is on the public plugin surface.

That leaves two options, and both are poor:

- Re-implement the maths in the plugin. It drifts on the next release and users get wrong numbers.
- Import the internals: `agent.agent_init._parse_compression_config`, `agent.context_compressor.ContextCompressor` (and `preview_threshold_tokens`), `agent.model_metadata.get_model_context_length`, `hermes_cli.profiles` and `hermes_cli.config_effective`. The answer is exact, but every import is a catalogue rule 9 warning and can break on any release.

I maintain [hermes-tuneup](https://github.com/GodsBoy/hermes-tuneup), a plugin that tells users when each route really compacts and flags settings that waste quota or break prompt caching. It takes the second option today, with every internal import kept in one adapter file behind a drift guard that reports a route as unresolved rather than guess. The catalogue docs ask for a seam request in this situation, so here it is.

Hermes already has the right internal shape: `ContextCompressor.preview_threshold_tokens`, which `hermes_cli/context_switch_guard.py` uses to quote the real trigger before a model switch.

### Proposed Solution

A small, documented, read-only module on the public plugin allowlist, for example `hermes_cli.compaction_preview`:

```python
def preview_route(config: dict, *, model: str, provider: str, role: str = "main") -> RoutePreview: ...
def list_profiles() -> list[ProfileRef]: ...        # name and home path, default first
def load_profile_config(home: Path) -> dict: ...     # effective config, no side effects
```

`RoutePreview` would carry the window and where it came from (config pin, custom provider, catalogue, fallback), the trigger in tokens, and the factors behind it: the matched rule, the base and effective percentage, whether the small-window floor applied, the output reservation, the cap and the summariser ceiling.

Three properties matter:

- Side-effect free: no backups, no cache writes into the profile, no network. Today a read through `load_config` writes a backup into the home it reads, so a plugin has to copy files into a temporary home first.
- Offline: window resolution without a base URL or key, with the source reported so callers can mark a fallback window as assumed.
- Covered by the plugin API's compatibility promise, so a plugin's `requires_hermes` floor means something.

Hermes' own `/model` switch warning and `hermes config show` could use the same function to print the real trigger instead of the raw percentage.

### Alternatives Considered

- Keep the internal imports. Works today, but every release is a risk for users and the plugin carries rule 9 warnings.
- Expose only `preview_threshold_tokens`. Helpful, but plugins would still need the profile list, a side-effect-free config load and the factor breakdown to explain a number to a user.

### Feature Type

Developer experience (plugin API)

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

issues.title: pi backend: git over SSH fails with "Host key verification failed" because ~/.ssh (known_hosts included) is masked
issues.body:
## What

With `agent.acp_backend = "pi"`, every agent session fails git over SSH before authentication:

```
$ git ls-remote origin refs/heads/mainline
Host key verification failed.
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
```

The same command from a `kas` session on the same host and tier (`standard`) succeeds. Tools that push a git snapshot over the same SSH (for example a code-review CLI) fail too, so agents hand the operator git commands to run by hand.

Seen on 0.12.0.9, pi 1.5.0, pi-acp 0.0.34, Linux.

## Cause

- Pi is an enforced harness, so `adapter_hidden_credential_dirs` (`agent_sdk/tool_gate.py`) masks `~/.ssh` from its process tree. `acp/harness/pi.py` passes it as `extra_hidden_dirs`.
- Only the `strict` tier restores `known_hosts` into the masked `~/.ssh` (`mask_ssh_keys` in `sandbox_launcher_parts/mask_stages.py`). On `standard`, `~/.ssh` is empty for Pi.
- `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` still points `UserKnownHostsFile` at `~/.ssh/known_hosts`, which no longer exists, so ssh refuses the host.
- `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is forwarded only with `ssh_auth_sock_consent.json` (#18223). Even with consent, the missing `known_hosts` fails the check first.

## Proposal

Keep private keys hidden and host-key checking on:

1. Re-expose `~/.ssh/known_hosts` read-only inside the mask for enforced harnesses, as the strict tier already does. It holds only public host keys.
2. Then either forward the ssh-agent socket under the existing consent, or extend the gateway-side git proxy (`remote_session/git_gateway.py`) to SSH remotes.
3. Say why it failed: tell the session that `~/.ssh` is masked for this harness and name the fix.

## Workaround

A pooled MCP server runs outside the Pi mask. On our host, a pooled `builder-mcp` and its `CRRevisionCreator` tool pushed the snapshot and created a two-package draft code review from a Pi worker session (verified 2026-11-09). Plain `git fetch`/`git push` from the Pi shell still fail. The other workaround is a per-agent `agents.<name>.acp_backend = "kas"` override, which takes those agents off Pi.

## Related

- #13266 (closed): `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=-F /dev/null` broke remotes that rely on `~/.ssh/config`. Different cause, same symptom family.
- #29529 (closed): same `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `~/.ssh` visible case.
- #18223: no UI for the `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` consent.
- #11988: other Crew leaves masked from enforced harnesses.

issues.title: pi backend: amazon-bedrock models (GPT-6 Astra) fail with "Could not load credentials from any providers"
issues.body:
## What

A Pi session on `amazon-bedrock/global.openai.gpt-6-astra` fails on its first turn with an empty reply:

```
stopReason: error
errorMessage: Could not load credentials from any providers
```

The same session on a model from a provider extension with its own credential helper (Sol, via a Codex credential process) works. Switching an existing session to Astra fails the same way.

Seen on 0.12.0.9, pi 1.5.0, pi-acp 0.0.34, Linux.

## Cause

- Astra is only offered by Pi's built-in `amazon-bedrock` provider, which uses the AWS SDK's default chain.
- Under Kiro Crew every agent process gets `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`/`AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` pointed at a per-process broker directory (`kirocrew_amazon/creds_broker.py`). Its `creds` file is empty until the agent calls creds-agent `get_aws_creds`, and `credential_process` is stripped. A turn that starts on Astra fails before it can call that tool.
- Found 2026-11-09: each resumed Pi run gets a new broker directory with an empty `creds` file. A grant made in one run does not reach the next. Granting on Sol, then switching models with a follow-up run, failed again in 14 ms.

## What works today

The grant and the Astra call in the same run. On Sol, call `get_aws_creds` with a session policy limited to `bedrock:InvokeModel`/`InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on the Astra ARNs plus `sts:GetCallerIdentity` (900 s), then in the same run:

```
AWS_REGION=us-west-2 pi -p --no-session --no-tools --no-mcp --provider amazon-bedrock --model global.openai.gpt-6-astra "Reply exactly ASTRA_OK"
```

This returned `ASTRA_OK`, exit 0. It does not make a live Astra chat work, and the only role that could vend for the Bedrock account was an admin role, scoped down per call.

## Proposal

1. Give a harness's own model provider credentials without an agent-initiated `get_aws_creds` call: an operator-configured grant scoped to Bedrock invoke on the configured model ARNs, applied at spawn and not exposed to the agent's shell.
2. Or keep a session's broker grant across resumed runs of the same conversation until it expires.
3. When a Pi model call fails this way, say which credential source is missing instead of returning an empty reply.

Related: #9467 (closed, Astra in the model picker), #11988.

issues.title: record-analysis --report-only in an owned checkout records the repository-root charter digest, so `next` sees the fresh report as stale
issues.body:
## Symptom

In a validated owned checkout, `spec-kitty agent mission record-analysis --report-only` writes `input_artifacts.charter` with the hash of the **repository-root** charter. The full recorder (no `--report-only`) writes the hash of the **owned** charter.

`next` checks freshness against the owned charter (`next_cmd.py:118`, `charter_root=owned.owned_root`). When the two charters differ, a report-only report that was just recorded is classified as stale.

## Where

- `#6846` (commit 88ca02dbd, "bind owned analysis inputs and currency to validated roots") threaded `charter_root` through `write_analysis_report` (`mission_record_analysis.py:503`) and `next`. Its engineering note (`docs/plans/engineering-notes/2026-10-30-owned-analysis-currency.md`) says "Report-only transactional analysis is outside this qualification".
- `src/specify_cli/git/report_transaction.py` still calls `collect_input_artifact_hashes(feature_dir, repo_root)` (lines ~255, ~263) and `render_analysis_report` with no `charter_root`, although it receives `owned`.

## Reproduction

`tests/integration/test_owned_analysis_recording.py::test_analysis_records_in_owned_write_branch`. Its assertions now expect the owned charter (the intended #6846 contract). The `report_only=True` parameters (ids `[True-*-*]`) fail:

```
assert {'sha256': 'c55eaf…'(repository-root charter)} == {'sha256': 'ce1d6e…'(owned charter)}
```

The `report_only=False` parameters pass. Before the re-pin, the test expected the repository-root charter, so the `report_only=False` half went red in the nightly. That re-pin lands with the nightly slice D PR (#6787 / #7110). This issue tracks the remaining report-only half.

## Expected

A report-only recording in a validated owned checkout binds and checks the owned charter, as the full recorder does.

issues.title: `is_holiday` does not pass the requested date to `get_holiday_list_for_employee`
issues.body:
### Information about bug

The [`is_holiday`](https://github.com/frappe/erpnext/blob/v16.54.0/erpnext/setup/doctype/employee/employee.py#L441) function in **ERPNext** does not pass its `date` parameter to [`get_holiday_list_for_employee`](https://github.com/frappe/erpnext/blob/v16.54.0/erpnext/setup/doctype/employee/employee.py#L419).

When **HRMS** overrides this function through the `employee_holiday_list` hook, the HRMS implementation uses `as_on` to resolve the applicable Holiday List.

Since `as_on` is not passed, it defaults to today's date, potentially causing incorrect holiday checks for past or future dates.

**Expected behavior:**

`is_holiday` should pass the requested date to `get_holiday_list_for_employee`:

```python
holiday_list = get_holiday_list_for_employee(
    employee, raise_exception, as_on=date
)
```

This ensures the correct Holiday List is selected based on the requested date.


### Module

HR

### Version

_frappe: 16.55.2
erpnext: 16.54.0_

issues.title: skills_guard: redirected named-variable existence check falsely flagged as dump_all_env
issues.body:
## Summary

`scan_skill` reports a named-variable existence check with all output redirected to `/dev/null` as `dump_all_env` / high-severity exfiltration. For a community source, that caution verdict makes `should_allow_install` return false.

This is a narrow likely false positive, not a request to trust Superpowers wholesale or weaken installation gates.

## Environment and affected upstream

- Reproduced with installed Hermes Agent v0.23.0, git revision `2bd378ed1b8d6bf2192cb26e0a55ff3091e6bd19`, Linux, Python 3.14.9.
- Actual example: [obra/superpowers systematic-debugging/SKILL.md at reviewed revision](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/22f0b463e7a5e579904dd6211a520321035526f7/skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md#L95).
- This report does not establish behavior on a newer Hermes main revision.

## Minimal reproduction

Run from a Hermes checkout with its Python environment. This writes and scans a Markdown fixture; it does not execute the shell example or read environment values.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from tools.skills_guard import scan_skill, should_allow_install

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    root = Path(directory)
    (root / "SKILL.md").write_text(
        "---\nname: named-env-check-repro\n"
        "description: Minimal named environment existence check.\n---\n"
        "```sh\n"
        'printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" '
        '|| echo "IDENTITY not in environment"\n'
        "```\n"
    )
    result = scan_skill(root, source="https://github.com/obra/superpowers")
    print(result.verdict)
    for finding in result.findings:
        print(finding.pattern_id, finding.severity,
              finding.category, finding.description)
    print(should_allow_install(result))
```

Observed in this minimal fixture:

```text
caution
dump_all_env high exfiltration dumps all environment variables
(False, 'Blocked (community source + caution verdict, 1 findings). Use --force to override.')
```

The same finding occurs at line 95 in the reviewed upstream skill.

## Expected behavior and regression scope

`printenv IDENTITY` requests one named variable, not the entire environment. Both stdout and stderr are discarded, and the subsequent `echo` statements reveal only existence. This example does not dump environment values into the transcript or send them elsewhere.

Please distinguish this specific existence-check form from actual environment disclosure. A fix should retain detection for bare `printenv`, unredirected value exposure where relevant, piping/uploading values to an external destination, and redirection combinations that do **not** actually suppress output. Blanket allowlisting `printenv`, a repository, or all shell redirections would not be appropriate.

## Impact and limits

The finding blocks admission of this community skill under the normal policy. No scanner bypass or default-profile installation was performed. This report is not a full plugin security assessment, compatibility claim, or demonstrated runtime benefit.

Related but different mechanisms:
- #143864: plugin scan scope includes repository files a client does not load.
- #132155: credential-pattern collision inside base64 data.

Opened by Daksh with Hermes assistance, based on a local synthetic reproduction and the pinned upstream source.

issues.title: [Bug] GitHub trong chat: bộ kiểm tra trước khi đẩy bỏ qua "Lệnh kiểm tra" đã lưu vì lệch khoá brain (mã `brain` và đường dẫn `/brains/...`)
issues.body:
**Phiên bản:** Javis 0.487.2 (Docker trên VPS Linux), bộ não Claude Code.

### Triệu chứng

1. Danh sách **Lệnh kiểm tra** tuỳ chỉnh đã lưu cho một repo không được bộ kiểm tra sau lượt chat (`github_work.after_turn`) dùng. Gate vẫn chạy danh sách tự đọc từ CI, nên lần nào cũng đỏ cùng một lệnh và PR không bao giờ được đẩy.
2. Thẻ GitHub ở trang Kết nối không hiện hàng "N repo · N cuộc trò chuyện", dù repo đã gắn vào chat và đang có worktree.

### Cách tái hiện

1. Gắn một repo có app Node nằm trong thư mục con vào một chat web. Ví dụ CI có `defaults.run.working-directory: web` hoặc `working-directory: web` ở từng step, còn thư mục gốc không có `package.json`.
2. Lưu Lệnh kiểm tra tuỳ chỉnh cho repo (vd `cd web && npm ci`). Bản ghi được lưu với `brain = "/brains/Brain Default"`.
3. Sửa một file trong worktree rồi kết thúc lượt chat.
4. Gate báo `Kiểm tra ở máy: 0/6 đạt ... Đỏ: npm ci`, kèm lỗi `EUSAGE ... can only install with an existing package-lock.json`. Báo cáo có 6 lệnh, trong khi danh sách đã lưu có 9.

### Nguyên nhân

Chat truyền **mã brain** (`"brain"`) vào `github_work.after_turn(sid, brain, ...)` (`main.py`, `_persist_turn`). Còn bản ghi repo trong `github_repos` lưu `brain` là **đường dẫn** (`"/brains/Brain Default"`).

- `github_work.py:172` trong `gate_repo`:
  ```python
  rec = github_repos.find(brain, repo["full_name"]) or {}
  ```
  `find("brain", ...)` trả `None` nên `rec = {}`. Khi đó `checks_for(rec, wt)` không thấy `rec["checks"]` và rơi về `github_gate.suggest_checks(wt)`.
- `session_repos(sid, "brain")` vẫn tìm ra repo vì `_rec_for_folder` (`github_repos.py:619`) có đường dự phòng theo `folder_id`. Vì vậy repo vẫn được gate, chỉ là gate bằng danh sách sai.
- `local_view` (`github_repos.py:780`) gọi `list_local(brain)` với mã brain thì ra danh sách rỗng. Đây nhiều khả năng là lý do thẻ GitHub không hiện hàng repo.

Kiểm trực tiếp trên máy:

```text
github_repos.find("/brains/Brain Default", "owner/repo")  -> có bản ghi, checks = 9 lệnh
github_repos.find("brain", "owner/repo")                  -> None
github_repos.session_repos(sid, "brain")                  -> repo_id = 0f3f90b278e5 (tìm qua folder_id)
github_repos.list_local("brain")                          -> []
```

### Lỗi phụ (làm lỗi chính lộ ra)

`github_gate.commands_from_workflow` chỉ lấy `run:` của từng step, **bỏ qua `working-directory`** (cả ở step lẫn `defaults.run` của job hoặc workflow). Repo đặt app trong thư mục con vì thế luôn đỏ ở danh sách tự đọc. Tính năng "Lệnh kiểm tra" vốn sinh ra để vá chỗ này, nhưng lại bị lỗi chính ở trên vô hiệu hoá.

### Đề xuất sửa

1. Chuẩn hoá khoá brain ở một chỗ, ví dụ `find`/`list_local` nhận cả mã lẫn đường dẫn qua `_brain_root(...)`. Hoặc trong `gate_repo` tìm bản ghi giống `session_repos`:
   ```python
   rec = (github_repos.find(brain, repo["full_name"])
          or next((r for r in github_repos.list_local() if r.get("id") == repo.get("repo_id")), None)
          or {})
   ```
2. Trong `commands_from_workflow`, ghép `working-directory` của step, rồi đến `defaults.run.working-directory` của job, rồi của workflow, thành `cd <dir> && <run>`.
3. Thêm test: lưu checks với brain dạng đường dẫn, gọi `gate_repo` với brain dạng mã, rồi khẳng định gate dùng checks đã lưu. Thêm một test cho `working-directory`.

### Ảnh hưởng

Mọi repo đặt app trong thư mục con không thể đẩy PR từ chat, kể cả khi người dùng đã tự sửa Lệnh kiểm tra. Ba vòng sửa tự động đều đỏ cùng một lỗi, không do code của nhánh.

issues.title: Windows: việc nền Codex mức auto bị hạ xuống read-only, cần đặt windows.sandbox
issues.body:
## Tóm tắt
Trên Windows, mọi việc nền chạy bằng Codex ở mức `auto` thực tế chỉ có quyền **read-only**, dù Javis đã truyền `--sandbox workspace-write`. Worker không ghi được file, dừng lại, và Javis hiểu nhầm thành "đang chờ chủ trả lời" thay vì báo lỗi quyền.

## Môi trường
- Windows 11 (bản cài Javis native, không Docker)
- codex-cli 0.162.1
- Javis server commit `a94fe8e4`

## Cách tái hiện
1. Trên Windows, dùng cấu hình Codex mặc định (không có mục `[windows]` trong `config.toml`).
2. Giao một việc nền mức `auto` cho engine Codex, yêu cầu ghi một file.
3. `claude_cli.CodexCLI._build_args` dựng lệnh `codex --sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval never ... exec ...`.
4. Mở file rollout của phiên Codex: `sandbox_policy` là `read-only`. Lệnh ghi file thất bại, worker báo không ghi được đầu ra.

Trên một máy, 100% phiên Codex chạy việc nền trong 2 ngày đều ra `read-only`, không phiên nào ra `workspace-write`.

## Nguyên nhân
Trên Windows, khi sandbox Windows của Codex chưa được bật trong config, Codex hạ `workspace-write` xuống `read-only` mà không báo lỗi. Cờ `--sandbox workspace-write` của Javis vì vậy không có tác dụng.

## Cách khắc phục đã thử và chạy được
Thêm vào `config.toml` của CODEX_HOME:
```toml
[windows]
sandbox = "unelevated"
```
Sau đó chạy lại cùng lệnh thì phiên nhận đúng `workspace-write` và ghi file được. Truyền qua dòng lệnh `-c windows.sandbox="unelevated"` cũng cho kết quả tương tự.

## Đề xuất sửa trong mã
- Trong `CodexCLI._build_args` (hoặc `codex_sandbox_cho_mode`): khi `sys.platform == "win32"` và có đặt `--sandbox`, tự thêm `-c windows.sandbox="unelevated"`. Cách này áp dụng cho mọi CODEX_HOME, kể cả tài khoản ChatGPT thêm sau, và không phụ thuộc người dùng sửa config tay.
- Khi worker Codex báo không ghi được do sandbox read-only, nên phân loại thành lỗi môi trường/quyền (giống thông báo "rào sandbox riêng của Codex không khởi động được" đang có cho Docker), không chuyển việc sang trạng thái chờ chủ trả lời.

issues.title: Tự gắn source cho ký ức làm hỏng frontmatter (memory_control._join không đặt dấu nháy); lượt sau có thể xoá hết các khoá khác
issues.body:
## Lỗi
Bản 0.500.5. Sau mỗi lượt chat, `server/main.py:18070` gọi `memory_control.stamp_new_facts()` để gắn `source` cho ký ức trong `memory/facts/` được sửa trong lượt mà chưa có `source`. Hàm đọc frontmatter bằng `_split()` (`memory_control.py:53`) rồi ghi lại cả frontmatter bằng `_join()` (`memory_control.py:64`):

```python
lines = [f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in meta.items() if v is not None and str(v) != ""]
```

`_join` in thẳng giá trị Python, không bao giờ đặt dấu nháy, nên:
- chuỗi có `: ` (vd `description: "Ghi chú: ví dụ"`) thành `description: Ghi chú: ví dụ`, YAML không đọc được nữa;
- list `[vi-du]` thành `['vi-du']`;
- mọi chuỗi khác cần dấu nháy trong YAML cũng bị ghi trần.

## Tái hiện (mã lõi 0.500.5, thư mục nháp)
File `mem/facts/vi-du.md`:
```
---
type: preference
description: "Ghi chú: ví dụ có dấu hai chấm"
tags: [vi-du]
created: 2026-11-08
---
Nội dung ký ức.
```
Gọi `memory_control.stamp_new_facts("mem", source="chat 2026-11-08 (abc12345)", since=0)`, file thành:
```
---
type: preference
description: Ghi chú: ví dụ có dấu hai chấm
tags: ['vi-du']
created: 2026-11-08
source: chat 2026-11-08 (abc12345)
---
Nội dung ký ức.
```
`yaml.safe_load` báo `ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here`, `_split()` trả `{}`.

Gọi `stamp_new_facts` thêm một lần trên file đó: vì `_split()` trả `{}` nên hàm tưởng file chưa có `source` và ghi lại chỉ còn:
```
---
source: chat 2026-11-09 (def67890)
---
Nội dung ký ức.
```
`type`, `description`, `tags`, `created` mất hết, không báo gì.

## Lần thứ hai xảy ra thật khi nào
- `main.py:19597` truyền `turn_started=(_mem_snap or {}).get("t0") or 0`, khi đó `since = time.time() - 1800`: file vừa được gắn source trong 30 phút trước bị xét lại ở lượt kế tiếp.
- Hoặc file được sửa lại ở một lượt sau trong lúc frontmatter vẫn hỏng.

Đọc mã thì `edit_memory()` (`memory_control.py:189`, sửa ký ức trong app) cũng ghi bằng `_join` sau `_split`, nên có cùng hai vấn đề (bỏ dấu nháy; frontmatter đã hỏng thì ghi lại chỉ còn các khoá hàm tự đặt). Phần này tôi chưa chạy thử.

## Ảnh hưởng
- Lỗi âm thầm: mọi chỗ đọc qua `_split()`/fastyaml coi ký ức như không có frontmatter (mất type, description và các khoá riêng của người dùng).
- Đã gặp thật trên brain của tôi ngày 08/11/2026: một ký ức có `description` chứa dấu hai chấm bị hỏng frontmatter sau một lượt chat. Tôi đã sửa tay và tạm dùng hook Claude Code tự thêm dòng `source:` có dấu nháy trước khi lõi chạm vào, nhưng engine khác không có hook đó.

## Đề xuất sửa
1. `stamp_new_facts`: chèn đúng một dòng `source: <json.dumps(source, ensure_ascii=False)>` vào trước dấu `---` đóng của frontmatter gốc, không dựng lại cả frontmatter, để giữ nguyên các khoá khác.
2. `_join`: dump bằng `yaml.safe_dump(meta, allow_unicode=True, sort_keys=False)` như `learn.py:196` đang làm.
3. Frontmatter không đọc được thì bỏ qua file (hoặc ghi log), không coi là `{}` rồi ghi đè, ở cả `stamp_new_facts` và `edit_memory`.

Ghi chú nhỏ: `stamp_new_facts` gắn source cho mọi file có mtime trong lượt, kể cả file do việc nền chạy cùng lúc sửa, nên nguồn có thể gán nhầm sang cuộc chat đang mở.

issues.title: Spec hooks that Kiro Crew fires itself ignore max_output_size and cache_ttl_seconds
issues.body:
### Existing issues

- [x] I searched open issues and this is not already reported.

### KiroCrew version

0.13.0 (source checkout, not a release build), main at 81f78c71c1

### Release channel

Not sure

### How is it installed?

From source

### Platform

Not platform-specific

### What happened

Kiro Crew runs an agent spec's own hooks itself on KAS (the default backend), goose, opencode and strands, and on claude for every event but `preToolUse`. There, an object-form hook entry's `max_output_size` and `cache_ttl_seconds` are dropped without a word.

A `userPromptSubmit` or `agentSpawn` hook whose author set `max_output_size: 20000` can put up to 64 KiB of stdout into the model's context, which is Kiro Crew's own stream cap, instead of the 20000 bytes the author allowed. `cache_ttl_seconds` is ignored too, so the hook runs on every event, and nothing in the log or the docs says so.

Expected: the stdout that reaches the model is cut at `max_output_size` UTF-8 bytes, as kiro-cli counts it, and a `cache_ttl_seconds` that Kiro Crew does not honour is at least named in the log and the docs.

Root cause: `agent_sdk/spec_hooks._from_object_form` reads only `command`, `matcher` and `timeout_ms` from each entry, and `_hook` builds a `ScriptHook` that has no output-limit field. `hook_runtime/script_hooks.run_script_hook` caps stdout only at `_HOOK_STREAM_CAP_BYTES` (64 KiB), and the turn loop appends that whole stdout to the `[Hook context]` block.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Write a user-level agent spec named `capped` with `hooks.userPromptSubmit: [{"command": "<a script that prints 40000 bytes>", "timeout_ms": 10000, "max_output_size": 20000, "cache_ttl_seconds": 1}]`.
2. Start the gateway with `kirocrew gateway` on the default KAS backend.
3. Open a chat on `capped` and send one message.
4. Observe: the prompt Kiro Crew sends the engine carries all 40000 bytes of the hook's stdout in its `[Hook context]` block, with no truncation marker, and no gateway log line names `cache_ttl_seconds`.

The same thing in code: `spec_hooks.spec_script_hooks("capped", spec)` for that spec returns hooks that carry the event, matcher and timeout only.

### Relevant log output

```shell
[Hook context] block in the prompt sent to the engine: hook stdout bytes = 40000 (limit 20000), truncation marker = False
gateway log lines naming cache_ttl_seconds: 0
```

### Anything else

Proposed fix: carry `max_output_size` onto the in-memory hook (never saved to `hooks.json`), clamp it to the 64 KiB stream cap, and cut stdout to that many UTF-8 bytes in `run_script_hook` after redaction, so the cut cannot split a secret before redaction sees it whole. Leave `cache_ttl_seconds` unhonoured, because a result cache would be new per-session state and without one the hook only runs more often; log it once per hook and document it.

Workaround today: keep the hook's output small in the hook script itself.

issues.title: Brick: PortMaster and all ports fail because `/bin/bash` is BusyBox, and `device_init` only copies bash when it's missing
issues.body:
## Bug description
On my TrimUI Brick, the PortMaster app and every PortMaster port stopped launching around late September 2026. Updating to spruceOS 4.5.6 didn't fix it.

## Logs
With the bundled PortMaster 2026.10.01-0433, `Saves/spruce/portmaster.log` ended with:

    sh: setterm: not found
    .../PortMaster/device_info.txt: line 915: syntax error: unexpected "("

Line 915 is `CAPS=()`, a bash array.

After updating PortMaster to 2026.11.02-0433 (which includes upstream fix b90aee7 for device_info.txt), the next bash-only line failed instead:

    .../PortMaster/utils/pm_launch.txt: line 122: syntax error: unexpected "("

Stardew Valley's `port.log` showed the error format of BusyBox's shell:

    StardewValley.sh: source: line 169: can't open '/roms/ports/PortMaster/device_info.txt'

## Cause
The scripts start with `#!/bin/bash`, but `/bin/bash` on this Brick is not a real bash. Most likely it's a BusyBox link from the stock firmware. In `spruce/scripts/platform/device_functions/Brick.sh`, `device_init()` only copies `spruce/smartpro/bin/bash` when `/bin/bash` is missing:

    if [ ! -x /bin/bash ]; then
        cp /mnt/SDCARD/spruce/smartpro/bin/bash /bin/bash
        chmod +x /bin/bash
    fi

So the existing BusyBox bash is never replaced, and PortMaster's newer scripts, which use bash arrays, fail.

## Working fix (tested on my Brick)
    if [ ! -x /bin/bash ] || ! /bin/bash -c 'a=(1); [ "${a[0]}" = 1 ]' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        rm -f /bin/bash
        cp /mnt/SDCARD/spruce/smartpro/bin/bash /bin/bash
        chmod +x /bin/bash
    fi

The `rm -f` comes first so that `cp` can't write through a symlink into busybox. After a reboot, PortMaster and Stardew Valley launch normally. SmartPro.sh, BrickPro.sh and AnbernicXXCommon.sh use the same missing-only check and may need the same change.

It would also help to ship the 2026.11.02 PortMaster bundle that's already on main in a release.

## Environment
- Device: TrimUI Brick
- spruceOS: 4.5.6
- PortMaster: 2026.10.01-0433 (bundled), then 2026.11.02-0433

issues.title: Feature Request: Fallback or source compilation for pedalboard on older CPUs (AVX2 Missing / Illegal Instruction Error)
issues.body:
### Before filing

- [x] I searched [existing issues](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and [discussions](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/discussions) for this idea.

### What problem does this solve?

It solves the `Fatal Python error: Illegal instruction` crash that occurs during audio generation on older but still powerful CPUs (like Intel Core i5-3570K). The application crashes because the pre-compiled `pedalboard` package requires AVX2 instructions, which are missing on these processors (they only support up to AVX). Implementing this will allow VoiceStudio to run out-of-the-box on older hardware without requiring users to manually compile dependencies from source.


### Proposed solution

1. Detect CPU flags during runtime/setup. If AVX2 is missing, force source compilation for pedalboard using:
   pip install pedalboard --no-binary :all:
2. Provide a built-in fallback script or installer toggle that automatically rebuilds hardware-specific audio dependencies targeting the native host architecture (e.g., using CFLAGS="-march=native").


### Alternatives considered

1. Manually downloading pre-compiled wheels, but they still require AVX2.
2. Installing via system package manager, but pedalboard is not available in official Arch Linux repositories.
3. Completely removing or replacing the pedalboard library, which is impossible because it's a core dependency for the backend's audio processing chain.


### Area

Voice cloning

issues.body:
### Before filing

- [x] I'm on the latest release (or `main`) — older builds may already be fixed.

### What happened?

In the desktop app, I drop a 665 MB video (14 min, 1080p) into the Dub tab. It sits on "Preparing..." for several
minutes. During that time the backend does nothing, and the app's main process is at 100% of one CPU core, reading
the file at only 1-3 MB/s.

The same file uploaded through Chrome at http://127.0.0.1:3900 is done in about 2 seconds. So the slow part is how
the desktop window sends the file to the backend (the app:// proxy, proxyToBackend in main/index.js), not the
backend itself.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the desktop app (Windows 11).
2. Go to Dub and drop a large video (I used 665 MB, 14 min, 1080p).
3. Watch the status stay on "Preparing..." for minutes; the main process CPU is at 100% of one core.
4. Open http://127.0.0.1:3900 in Chrome, go to Dub, upload the same file: it is done in ~2 s.

### What did you expect instead?

Upload speed in the desktop app similar to the browser UI (the 665 MB file takes ~2 s in Chrome at 127.0.0.1:3900).

### Operating system

Windows (x64)

### How did you install it?

Desktop app (installer / AppImage)

### Version

0.5.7

### Compute device

NVIDIA GPU (CUDA)

### Active TTS/ASR engine

omnivoice

### Logs / diagnostic bundle

```text

```

### Anything else?

Environment: Electron 44.3.0, RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, i5-14500, Windows 11. Test file: 14:21 1080p AV1 mp4, 665 MB.

Workaround that fixed it for me: in the renderer, when location.protocol is "app:", POST /dub/upload straight to
http://127.0.0.1:3900/dub/upload, and fall back to the normal call on any failure. The backend already allows the
origin app://voicestudio (CORS and browser guard both pass; a foreign origin still gets 403) and the CSP connect-src
already allows http://127.0.0.1:*. With that change the same file uploads in ~2 s in the desktop app.

Also: the "make video browser-playable" re-encode uses CPU libx264 (~5 min for this file). Trying h264_nvenc with
-hwaccel cuda first (falling back to x264) brought it to under a minute (60 s test clip: x264 32 s, NVENC 23 s,
NVENC+NVDEC 5.6 s).

issues.title: [Bug] OmniVoice catalogue licence dialog omits the Higgs tokenizer licence, so generation still fails after accepting
issues.body:
### Before filing

- [x] I searched [existing issues](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and this isn't a duplicate. (#3837 is about the tokenizer's licence *terms*; this is about the acceptance UI.)
- [x] I'm on the latest release (or `main`) — older builds may already be fixed.

### What happened?

Accepting OmniVoice's licence from its Model Catalogue row does not make OmniVoice usable. The row's "Accept licence to use" dialog lists only `k2-fsa/OmniVoice`, but generation also requires `eustlb/higgs-audio-v2-tokenizer`. After accepting from the catalogue, `POST /generate` with `engine=omnivoice` still returns 403:

```
{"detail":{"code":"model_licence_required","message":"Licence not accepted for eustlb/higgs-audio-v2-tokenizer. Review and accept it in Model Catalogue.", ...}}
```

The tokenizer has no catalogue row of its own, so "accept it in Model Catalogue" has no target. It can only be accepted through the app-level dialog that appears after a generation attempt fails. I accepted in the catalogue, believed setup was done, and only found out on first use.

**Cause (from reading `main` @ aaabec19e):**
- Backend gate: `ensure_engine_accepted("omnivoice")` → `repos_for_engine` requires every registry row whose `engines` includes `omnivoice`. In `backend/config/model_licenses.json`, that is both `k2-fsa/OmniVoice` and `eustlb/higgs-audio-v2-tokenizer`.
- Catalogue dialog: `electron/src/renderer/src/features/settings/model-license.tsx:318` passes only the row's own acceptance: `models={currentAcceptance ? [toAcceptable(label, currentAcceptance)] : []}`.

The "Accept licence to use" badge in `model-list/model-actions.tsx` also only checks the row's own `license_acceptance`, so the row shows as usable while the engine is still gated.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh install. Download `k2-fsa/OmniVoice` (the default TTS) from the Model Catalogue.
2. On the OmniVoice row, click **Accept licence to use**, tick the box, and accept. The row now shows Installed.
3. Generate any clip with OmniVoice (UI, or `POST /generate -F engine=omnivoice -F text=hi`).
4. You get a 403 `model_licence_required` for `eustlb/higgs-audio-v2-tokenizer`.

### What did you expect instead?

The OmniVoice row's licence dialog should list every licence the engine needs (OmniVoice and the Higgs tokenizer), so one acceptance makes the engine usable. Likewise, the "Accept licence to use" badge should stay until all of them are accepted. One option is for `/models` to return the engine's full `repos_for_engine` set (or the row's dependent gated repos) in `license_acceptance`, and for the dialog to render all of them.

### Operating system

macOS (Apple Silicon)

### How did you install it?

From source (uv sync) — `bun run dev`

### Version

0.5.7 (main @ aaabec19e)

### Compute device

Apple Silicon (MPS)

issues.title: parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 emits lowercase, unpunctuated output, because decoder context prompt never injected
issues.body:
`parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`, served as a multilingual model, produces all-lowercase output with no punctuation. I've tried both `mlx_audio.stt` and the `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint and they were all the same. The NeMo reference and the HF model card produce normally punctuated, cased output on the same audio.

## Root cause

The v3 tokenizer vocabulary contains decoder context-conditioning tokens:

- `<|startofcontext|>` — id **7**
- `<|pnc|>` — id **5** (punctuation)
- `<|nopnc|>` — id 4
- `<|itn|>` — id **8** (inverse text normalization)
- `<|noitn|>` — id 6

Parakeet v3 was trained with the prediction network warmed by a context prompt, such as `<|startofcontext|> <|pnc|> <|itn|>` for punctuated output. NeMo injects this sequence at the start of RNNT decoding. The mlx-audio TDT decode loop in `mlx_audio/stt/models/parakeet/parakeet.py` **never** injects it, so the model falls back to an unconditioned regime that drops punctuation and casing entirely.

## Reproduction

I use the same weights, same 45s English interview clip, only difference is warming the decoder with token ids `[7, 5, 8]` before the decode loop:

```text
# without context prompt (current behavior):
when we design it its always a perfectly straight line straight line perfect
and its not just the software its the hardware too

# with [startofcontext, pnc, itn] injected:
When we design it, it's always a perfectly straight line. Straight line. Perfect.
And it's not just the software, it's the hardware, too.
```

## Suggested fix

Warm the decoder hidden state by stepping each context token through the TDT step before the greedy loop (I have verified locally, `tokenizer.py` lookup guards models lacking the tokens):

```python
_lt, _gt = chr(60) + chr(124), chr(124) + chr(62)
ctx_names = [_lt + n + _gt for n in ("startofcontext", "pnc", "itn")]
context_ids = [vocabulary.index(t) for t in ctx_names if t in vocabulary]
for ctx in context_ids:
    _, _, h, c = tdt_step(features[:, :1],
                          mx.array([[ctx]], dtype=mx.int32),
                          decoder_hidden[0], decoder_hidden[1])
    decoder_hidden = (h, c)
    last_token = ctx
```

Models whose vocab lacks these tokens (e.g. `parakeet-tdt_ctc-0.6b-ja`, v2) skip the warmup and are unaffected — the lookup is by token name at runtime, not by hardcoded id.

## Notes

- The same defect exists in `senstella/parakeet-mlx` (its `decode(last_token, hidden_state)` has the injection interface but nothing injects by default). Cross-linking for visibility: see senstella/parakeet-mlx#44 — the same mechanism would also enable user-supplied text prompts.
- Happy to PR the patch if the approach looks right.

*Investigated with AI assistance; reproduction verified locally on M5 Max, macOS 26.7.1, mlx-audio 0.6.0.*

issues.title: [Bug]: One unavailable connector blanks the app when searching Settings > Connectors
issues.body:
If the backend can't build the summary for one connector, typing a single letter in the Settings > Connectors search box turns the whole app window blank.

**Steps**
1. Have a connector whose summary fails on the backend. It then returns a row like `{"id": "microsoft", "error": "unavailable"}` (for example when the OS keychain/keyring read fails).
2. Open Settings > Connectors.
3. Type `g` in the search box.

**Expected:** the list filters, and the broken connector shows as unavailable.

**Actual:** the window goes white with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')`. Before searching, the broken row is also counted as a nameless entry under "MCP servers".

GAIA version: `main` at dad0ed13f. Reproduced with Playwright against the built Agent UI.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Technical details</summary>

`routers/connectors.py` (~L565-570) emits `{id, error}` rows with no `display_name` or `type` when a connector's summary throws. `ConnectorsSection.tsx` (~L162-167) calls `c.display_name.toLowerCase()` and groups by `c.type` with no guard, and the app has no error boundary around Settings, so the render error unmounts everything.
</details>

issues.title: [Bug]: A render error on any Agent UI screen blanks the whole app
issues.body:
When any screen in the Agent UI throws while rendering, the whole window goes blank. The user sees an empty window with no message and no way back except restarting the app.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Trigger any render error outside a chat card. #6952 is one real case: one connector the backend can't read, then a search in Settings > Connectors.
2. The entire window goes blank, including the sidebar and the chat.

**Expected:** the broken screen shows a short "Something went wrong" message with a way to reload or go back. The rest of the app keeps working.

**Actual:** React unmounts the whole tree and the window is empty.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Technical details</summary>

- The only error boundary in `src/gaia/apps/webui/src` is `CardErrorBoundary`, which wraps rendered chat cards. `main.tsx` mounts `<App />` with no boundary, so any other render error unmounts the root.
- Suggested shape: one boundary at the root, plus one per main area (chat view, settings panels), so a crash in Settings doesn't take down an open chat. Log the error with context, and don't swallow it.
- #6955 fixes the connector crash itself. This issue is about the safety net for the next one.
</details>

issues.title: [问题] 桌面诊断把「借用同品牌参考脚本」写成「版本不一致」
issues.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## 现象

桌面版「复制完整诊断」里的「机型脚本」一行，把**借用同品牌参考脚本**和**系统版本对不上**说成同一句话。

三张票的正文里都有这句，实际版本都匹配：

```
#645  魅族 21 Note   → 机型脚本：recipes\meizu-MEIZU 21 Pro\recipe.py（录制版本 Flyme 12.6.0.0A，不一致）
#704  真我 GT7       → 机型脚本：recipes\oppo-PLP120\recipe.py（录制版本 PLP120_16.0.9，不一致）
#469  小米 14 Ultra  → 机型脚本：recipes\xiaomi-M154FF\recipe.py（录制版本 OS4.0，不一致）
```

## 根因

`tool/run.py` 的 `cmd_status_json` 里：

```python
ok = (not ref) and build_ok(i, rb)
```

`ref` 是「借的是同品牌参考脚本」。只要借用，`recipe_ok` 恒为 `false`，与版本对不对无关。声明 `recipe_ok` 的两个消费者都先判 `recipe_ref`：

- `gui/web/index.html` 的检测页：`recipe_ref` 显示「有同品牌参考」，版本比较只在自身脚本上做；
- `aac_android/view.py` 的 `_recipe()`：`if recipe and not ref and not ok` 才提「脚本按 X 录，这台是 Y」。

只有桌面诊断 `gui/app.py` 的 `Api.diagnostics()` 直接拿 `recipe_ok` 出「一致 / 不一致」，没有先看 `recipe_ref`。

用 #645 的实际值复核过：

```
$ .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'tool');import run;
i={'brand':'meizu','model':'MEIZU 21 Note','build':'Flyme 12.6.0.0A','os':''}
print(run.build_ok(i,'Flyme 12.6.0.0A'))"
True
```

`build_ok` 为真、`recipe_ok` 为假，两者只差 `not ref` 这一项 —— 诊断的「不一致」是纯措辞错误。

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** 桌面诊断区分「借用同品牌参考脚本」与「系统版本不同」，不再把前者报成版本不一致

**Current behavior:**
`Api.diagnostics()` 的「机型脚本」行按 `recipe_ok` 输出「一致 / 不一致」。`recipe_ok` 在 `cmd_status_json` 里由 `(not ref) and build_ok(...)` 得出，只要脚本来自同品牌参考就恒为 false，于是每台没有专用脚本的机型都被写成「不一致」，即使录制版本与实机版本完全相同。

**Desired behavior:**
「机型脚本」行分三档，与检测页、手机版的口径一致：

1. 没有机型脚本 → `机型脚本：无`（现状，不变）
2. 借用同品牌参考脚本 → 标明这是参考脚本，并给出它按什么版本录制；**不出现「不一致」**
3. 本机型专用脚本 → 保留现有的「录制版本 X，一致 / 不一致」

**Key interfaces:**

- `Api.diagnostics()` 的输出行（`- 机型脚本：…`）是唯一要改的落点。`status` 字典里 `recipe`、`recipe_ref`、`recipe_build`、`recipe_ok` 四个字段都在，`recipe_ref` 为真时 `recipe` 必不为空。
- **不要改** `tool/run.py` 的 `recipe_ok` 语义：检测页与手机版都靠「借用时 ok 为假」来进安全模式分支，改成「借用也算对」会连带改掉那两处的判断。

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] 借同品牌参考脚本时，诊断行不再出现「不一致」，并写明是同品牌参考及其录制版本
- [ ] 本机型专用脚本、版本一致时仍显示「一致」，不一致时仍显示「不一致」
- [ ] 没有机型脚本时仍为 `机型脚本：无`
- [ ] 新增用例覆盖这三种状态，经 `Api.diagnostics()` 断言；用 `tests/fixtures.py` 的 `FakeRunner` 注入 `status-json` 回包，不 patch `api._run`
- [ ] `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 全绿，`uvx ruff@0.17.3 check --select F,E9 tool tests gui android/app/src/main/python` 干净
- [ ] CHANGELOG `## 未发布` 的 `### 修复` 加一条 ≤ 80 字、挂本票编号

**Out of scope:**

- 手机版 `aac_android/view.py`（`_recipe()` 已先判 `recipe_ref`，无需改）
- `gui/web/index.html` 的检测页标签（已是三档）
- `recipe_ok` 的语义本身，以及 `tool/run.py` 里挑脚本的逻辑
- 在这行里补「命中率 / 哪些段会跳过」一类信息

issues.title: 段内静默跳过（二）：有兜底的段落在兜底也不通时仍标「成功」
issues.body:
拆自 #776 的三轴审查结论。#776 只修了「返回值被直接丢掉」的 8 处，票面把下面几处归为 C 类「返回值被消费且按失败处理——不用改」。审查逐个跑过，这几处在兜底失败时仍然是裸 `return` / `break`，段内一项没做，`FAILED_STEPS` 为空、退出码 0、结果页标「成功」——正是 #776 要消灭的形态。

## 现象

| 位置 | 现状 | 触发 |
|---|---|---|
| `recipes/honor-PNM-AN10/recipe.py`「广告跟踪」段 | `if not p.setting("广告", "广告与隐私"):` 之后走菜单（隐私和安全 → 其他隐私和安全功能 → 广告与隐私），三步任一失败就裸 `return` | 设置搜索框打不开（`recipe.py` 记着 #88 / #99 的 MagicOS 10 机型）且菜单入口改名 / 不在当前页 |
| `recipes/vivo-V2303A/recipe.py`「全局搜索」段 | `if not p.setting("全局搜索"): break`，跳出三个子页的循环，本段直接结束 | 设置搜索不可用 |
| `recipes/redmi-25060RK16C/recipe.py`「系统广告」段 | 搜索失败后走菜单，全程 `maybe()` 守卫，都点不通时什么也没做就结束 | HyperOS 菜单路径变化 |

第一条尤其要紧：`honor-PNM-AN10` 是 HONOR 家族的参考脚本（`tool/run.py` 的 `REFERENCE["honor"]`），没有专用脚本的荣耀机都借它跑；#639 的报告日志里出现的正是这一段。

## 根因

`Phone.setting()` 只返回 `False`、不抛异常，`@step` 装饰器只认异常。返回值被消费了不等于失败被记录了——兜底那一支如果也只是 `return`，段内结局照样是「成功」。

#776 的 AST 守卫按票面的形状判据只检查「返回值有没有被拿去判」，`if not p.setting(...):` 里写 `raise` 还是 `return` 它分不出（`tests/test_recipe_setting_checked.py` 的 `TheGuardItself` 里有一条用例把这条边界钉住了）。

## 建议方案

脚本侧同样的修法：兜底也走不通时 `raise`，让本段进 `FAILED_STEPS`。

- `honor-PNM-AN10` 广告跟踪：菜单三步任一失败 → `raise RuntimeError("没找到「广告与隐私」入口")`。
- `vivo-V2303A` 全局搜索：`break` 改成 `raise`。注意段序上它紧跟「系统广告」，用户会看到「系统广告 失败 / 全局搜索 成功」并存的结论。
- `redmi-25060RK16C` 系统广告：菜单路径没点进「广告服务」→ `raise`。

要一并决定的两件事：

1. 是否把 AST 守卫收紧成「`if not p.setting(...)` 的分支体必须能 raise」——三处 B 类的兜底都靠带 raise 的 helper（`row()` / `close_named()`）收尾，静态看不出来，需要另想判据。
2. #776 的票面把 `honor-PNM-AN10` 广告跟踪归为「按失败处理」，但代码里是裸 `return`；这条分类当时就写错了。

## 验收

- 三处兜底也失败时，日志出现 `未完成步骤：<段名>`，退出码非 0，结果页该段标「失败」。
- 兜底走通时仍 `rc == 0`，行为与现在一致。
- `vivo-V2303A` 的 `tests/test_vivo_v2303a_recipe.py` 里钉住 `break` 静默行为的用例一并改。
- 单测覆盖三处「搜索失败 + 兜底也失败」，以及 `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 全绿。

## 关联

- #776 / PR #818：只覆盖没有兜底的 8 处。
- #639 / PR #799：YOYO 段当时明确写成「不算失败步」，已被 #776 推翻。

issues.title: preview: page_title and inject_base_href count tags inside comments and scripts
issues.body:
`page_title` and `inject_base_href` in `turnstone/core/preview.py` find a page's ``, `<head>`, `<html>`, doctype and `<base>` by searching the first 64 KB for their opening text. They don't skip comments or script text, so tags inside them count, and two title edges go wrong: ```python page_title("<!-- <title>Old -->New") # 'Old': a title inside a comment wins over the real one page_title("a

b

c") # 'a

b

c': an end tag with a space doesn't end the title page_title("<titlebar>x</titlebar><title>Real") # 'xReal': a longer tag name counts as a title inject_base_href("<head><script>s='<base href=x>'</script></head>", "https://a.example/") # returned unchanged: a <base in a script counts as the page's own base inject_base_href("<!-- <head> --><body>x", "https://a.example/") # '<!-- <head><base href="https://a.example/"> --><body>x': the base lands inside the comment ``` **Effect.** The title shows in the preview pane and in `open_preview`'s tool result, so the model reads a wrong title too. A page that gets no base, or gets it inside a comment, has its relative links (and, with remote assets allowed, its images and styles) resolve against turnstone's address instead of the page's, where they 404. **Possible fix.** A forward scan that skips comments and script and style text, takes a tag name only when whitespace, `/` or `>` follows it, and ends a title at `</title` followed by whitespace, `/` or `>`. `web_fetch`'s reader in `turnstone/core/web.py` already does this, but only inside its text conversion; sharing it would need a way to walk tags outside that conversion. The fix for #1568 makes these lookups linear and keeps their results on purpose, so this would be the first change to what they find.

issues.title: Output guard reads a wait_for_workstream result's JSON encoding, not the children's text
issues.body:
The fix for #1522 marks an `inspect_workstream` result as a JSON document the framework encoded
(`ControllerJSON` in `turnstone/core/output_guard.py`), and the output guard evaluates each string
it holds as text on its own. A `wait_for_workstream` result is framework-encoded JSON too, and it
carries each finished child's final message: the child model's own words, which no guard has read
before the coordinator's does.

The guard still reads a wait result through the encoding, which escapes quotes, newlines and
backslashes, so a child's report that holds role JSON (`{"role": "system", ...}`), an override
phrase split across lines or hex shellcode draws no finding. Compact JSON also has no whitespace
between values, so a redaction that ends at whitespace (an env line's value) can run on past the
child's message and delete the entries after it. A wait result has no role keys, so it has no
false positive of the kind #1522 reported.

Adopting the mark needs two details the inspect path didn't:

- A wait result can carry an `Error: ` prefix before its JSON (`_WAIT_ERROR_PREFIX`), which
  doesn't parse as a document.
- Admission fits a wait result before the guard runs (`_refit_wait_result`), and the post-guard
  re-cut fits it again when redaction lengthens it. A re-encoded result has to keep each cut
  message's `truncated` and `message_chars`.

The mark's precondition holds: a wait result's keys are the framework's (field names and child
workstream ids).

issues.title: MCP: let an admin exclude individual tools from a server's catalog
issues.body:
A model provider can refuse a whole request because of one MCP tool's input schema even when that schema is valid JSON Schema: some providers add rules of their own, such as refusing an array schema that has no `items`. The pending fix for tools whose input schema is not valid JSON Schema (they are left out of the server's catalog and listed in its status as `skipped_tools`) deliberately checks only JSON Schema's own rules, because a table of each provider's extra rules is not something we want to maintain. A tool that breaks only a provider's rule is still offered, so every request that offers it fails; with tool search, that is every request after a search loads it, for the rest of the conversation. Today an operator can only fix the server or remove it, and removing it drops the server's good tools along with the bad one.

Proposal: **a per-server list of tool names that the server's catalog leaves out, set by an admin.**

- Stored with the server: a field on console-managed servers (a column and a migration), and a key for servers from a node's configuration file.
- Applied where the catalog is built (`_catalog_tools` in `turnstone/core/mcp_client.py`), next to the schema check, so an excluded tool reaches no model on any lane and tool search never offers it.
- Shown in the server's status, so the admin console's MCP Servers tab shows which tools are excluded next to the ones left out for their schema.
- Set through the admin MCP API, with the SDK types and docs updated, and from the console, for example with an exclude control next to each tool in the server's details.

Out of scope for a first version: detecting a provider's refusal or reading provider errors, exclusion per provider, model or user, name patterns instead of exact names, and repairing schemas.

Open questions: whether excluded tools are reported in `skipped_tools` with a reason of their own or in a separate field, and whether a name the server no longer lists should be flagged as stale.

issues.title: [Bug]: delegate_task output_schema: a failed first run (failed=True) still triggers the schema retry, which then starts with no history
issues.body:
### Summary

`_validate_child_output_schema` (`tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`) runs the output_schema retry turn even when the child's first run **failed**: `result["failed"] is True`, for example a provider 429 that outlasted the API retries.

The failure text in `final_response` is validated as if it were the child's answer. It fails the schema, so the retry fires. Because the retry is a new `run_conversation` with no `conversation_history` (#135252), the child restarts from the system prompt plus the retry message. The goal and its earlier tool work are gone.

The only guards today are `_schema_valid`, an empty `final_response`, and `interrupted`. There is no check on `failed`.

### Impact

- A transient provider failure turns into a context-less extra run. In our case it made 14 more API calls, on a task the child had already partly done.
- Context engines and memory providers see only the retry run's messages at session end. `close()` forwards `_session_messages`, which the retry run replaced. So the first run's rows (goal, tool call, tool result) never reach `on_session_end`, although they are in the session DB.
  - In our case a context engine that stores delegated children at session end stored 35 of the child's 38 rows. The missing 3 were the head: the goal, the first tool call and its result.
  - A failed run does not fire `post_llm_call`, so nothing stored those rows per turn either.

### Reproduction

Minimal. It was run on a tree from shortly before `main`; the early-return guard and the retry call are unchanged on `main` at bcc04fce (main also wraps the retry in `child_profile_scope`):

```python
from tools.delegate_tool_child_run import _validate_child_output_schema

class FakeChild:
    session_id = "child-1"
    _delegate_output_schema = {"type": "object", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["answer"]}
    def __init__(self): self.calls = []
    def run_conversation(self, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append(kwargs)
        return {"final_response": '{"answer": 55}', "messages": [], "api_calls": 1}

child = FakeChild()
failed_first_run = {"final_response": "API call failed after 3 retries: HTTP 429 rate limit", "failed": True,
                    "completed": False, "error": "HTTP 429", "messages": [], "api_calls": 3}
outcome = _validate_child_output_schema(child, failed_first_run, 0, "task-1", None)
print(outcome.retries, len(child.calls), ["conversation_history" in c for c in child.calls])
# prints: 1 1 [False]   -- expected: 0 0 []  (no schema retry after a failed run)
```

Observed live on a delegated child with an output_schema while the provider returned 429s. The log shows the first run ending with "API call failed after 3 retries", then the next turn for the same child session logged with `history=0` and the "Your previous final response was rejected by the output contract validator" message.

### Suggested fix

- Skip the schema retry when the first run failed: add `or result.get("failed", False)` to the early return. A failed run has no answer to correct; its error should surface as the child's failure.
- The empty-history half is #135252, with fix PR #135354. With that fix, a retry that does run continues the child's conversation, so `_session_messages` at close also keeps the first run's rows.

issues.title: Gateway fails to start on macOS when an env var contains control characters (plistlib ValueError reported as "invalid_invocation")
issues.body:
## Summary
Desktop boots but loops on:
`Desktop boot failed: Gateway inaccessible (invalid_invocation). Use hermes gateway status for recovery.`

`hermes gateway ensure --json` prints `{"endpoint":null,"reason_code":"invalid_invocation","state":"inaccessible"}` (exit 2),
even with valid arguments.

## Root cause
`hermes_cli/gateway_launchd_runtime.py` (`start_gateway_job`, ~L113) writes the full launch environment into a
launchd plist via `plistlib.dump({... "EnvironmentVariables": dict(env) ...})`. If any env value contains a control
character, plistlib raises:

```
ValueError: strings can't contain control characters; use bytes instead
```

`hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_cli.py` (~L34) catches `(ValueError, TypeError)` and reports it as `invalid_invocation`,
which hides the real cause.

In my case the offending variables were `LESS_TERMCAP_mb/md/me/se/so/ue/us`. Prezto's `environment` module
exports these by default with ESC (`\x1b`) bytes, and they are common in zsh setups (oh-my-zsh plugins and others set them too).
They reach the gateway env through the login-shell environment Desktop merges in.

Call path: `ensure_gateway_runtime` (gateway_runtime.py:482) → `spawn_unmanaged_gateway` (gateway_runtime_start.py:86)
→ `start_gateway_job` (gateway_launchd_runtime.py:113) → `plistlib.dump`.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.23.0, git install, `main @ 90d6b98fd86`
- macOS (Darwin 27.0.0) arm64, zsh + prezto

## Repro
```sh
export LESS_TERMCAP_md=$'\E[01;31m'
hermes gateway ensure --json   # → {"reason_code":"invalid_invocation","state":"inaccessible",...}, exit 2
```

## Workaround
Stop exporting the variables, e.g. for prezto add to `.zpreztorc`:
```
zstyle ':prezto:environment:termcap' color 'no'
```
then launch Hermes.app from Dock/Finder (not from a shell that still has the old env).

## Suggested fix
- Drop (or encode) env entries containing control characters before writing the plist, and log a warning that names the keys.
- Don't map unexpected `ValueError`/`TypeError` from inside `ensure_gateway_runtime` to `invalid_invocation`.
  Report a distinct reason code (e.g. `launch_failed`) and log the traceback.

Related (different code path): #48164

issues.title: [Feature][Runner] Preserve incremental token usage on non-terminal exits
issues.body:
## Problem

Runner token usage is effectively persisted only when the Host receives a terminal `run.completed` or `run.failed` result with a `usage` payload. Usage attached to earlier result events is kept as event data but is not promoted to the run-level record.

If a run is cancelled, times out, the plugin process disconnects, or the result stream ends with a transport error after model calls have already completed, the run can lose the token usage observed before the non-terminal exit. This makes monitoring and cost reporting undercount partial runs.

The current path is centered in `src/langbot/pkg/agent/runner/orchestrator.py`, where `terminal_usage` is updated from terminal results before `finalize_run`.

## Desired behavior

- Accept cumulative usage snapshots during a run.
- Preserve the latest known usage when a run ends by cancellation, timeout, plugin failure, or transport failure.
- Keep per-model/provider slices and any provider metadata intact.
- Make repeated snapshots idempotent and avoid double-counting.
- Distinguish unknown usage from zero usage.

## Acceptance criteria

- A run that emits usage before cancellation retains that usage in its final run record.
- A failed or timed-out run retains the last valid snapshot.
- Replayed snapshots do not double-count.
- Existing terminal usage behavior remains compatible.
- Add unit/integration coverage for completed, failed, cancelled, timeout, and disconnected-stream paths.

issues.title: [Bug] Dub turns unlisted language tags into another language (fil becomes Finnish, estonian becomes Spanish)
issues.body:
### Before filing

- [x] I searched existing issues and this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I'm on `main` (fc154e76).

### What happened?

Dub sets the wrong source language when a downloaded caption track or the remote ASR server reports a language code or name that is not in the dub allow-list. `detected_source_language` in `backend/services/dub_language.py` falls back to the first two letters of the value, and those letters are often a different language:

| Source | Value | Becomes | Language |
|---|---|---|---|
| YouTube caption track | `fil`, `fil-orig` | `fi` | Finnish instead of Filipino |
| YouTube caption track | `new` | `ne` | Nepali instead of Newari |
| YouTube caption track | `pam` | `pa` | Punjabi instead of Kapampangan |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `estonian` | `es` | Spanish |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `swedish` | `sw` | Swahili |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `kannada`, `kazakh` | `ka` | Georgian |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `armenian` | `ar` | Arabic |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `bengali` | `be` | Belarusian |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `tagalog` | `ta` | Tamil |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `latvian` | `la` | Latin |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `slovak` | `sl` | Slovenian |

Translation then runs from that wrong language, with no warning.

Supported languages get dropped too. They come back as "source language missing":

- YouTube's `iw` (Hebrew), `jv` (Javanese) and `yue-HK` (Cantonese).
- OpenAI names such as `spanish`, `german` and `portuguese`.

The OpenAI transcription API returns language names, for example `"language": "english"` in its `verbose_json` reference example. YouTube labels Filipino captions `fil` and Hebrew captions `iw`. I listed the codes from `yt-dlp -J` on a public video.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
cd backend && ../.venv/bin/python -c 'from services.dub_language import detected_source_language as d; [print(v, d(v)) for v in ["fil-orig", "estonian", "swedish", "yue-HK", "iw"]]'
```

Output on `main`:

```
fil-orig fi
estonian es
swedish sw
yue-HK None
iw None
```

In the app, the same thing happens when you dub a Filipino YouTube video and choose **Use downloaded captions**. `POST /dub/use-downloaded-captions/{job_id}` stores `source_lang = "fi"`, and translation treats the Filipino text as Finnish.

### What did you expect instead?

Each value should keep its own language (`fil` is `tl`, `estonian` is `et`, `yue-HK` is `yue`, `iw` is `he`) or come back as unknown. It should never become a different language. `services/pronunciation.py` fixed the same kind of two-letter cut in #2542.

### Operating system

All. The bug is in platform-independent backend code.

### How did you install it?

From source.

### Version

`main` at fc154e76.

### Compute device

Any. This is not related to the device.

### Active TTS/ASR engine

YouTube caption path: any engine. Remote path: OpenAI-compatible ASR.

issues.title: Local only can't be seen or turned off in the app, and its message tells users to run a command
issues.body:
With Local only on, the Agent UI blocks cloud models correctly, but the person can't see or change the setting in the app, and the message they get tells them to run a command: "Pick a local model. To allow cloud models again, run `gaia config set network_policy cloud_allowed`." The composer keeps offering the cloud model they can't use. In the Arabic UI the message is English.

Done when Local only is shown and switchable in Settings (with the same effects as the CLI), cloud models are marked as blocked in the pickers while it's on, and the refusal points to that setting in plain words, in English and Arabic.

**Steps (v0.25.4-rc8):** turn on Local only (`gaia config set network_policy local_ai_only`), open the Agent UI on a chat that used a Fireworks model, send a message.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Technical details</summary>

- The refusal is built in the backend (`local_only` message used by the agent's model-call error path) and shown verbatim.
- There is no Settings control for `network_policy`; the providers router and pickers don't read it.
- #5956 shipped the policy as CLI-first. Found in v0.25.4-rc8 release testing.
</details>

issues.title: Errors shown in the Agent UI still tell users to run gaia commands (and nothing checks for it)
issues.body:
Error messages that reach the Agent UI still tell desktop users to run GAIA commands: "Run `gaia init` to install it, then re-run the scheduled task", "run `gaia daemon status`", "Run `gaia gateway auth`", "run `gaia config set default_model <id>`" and about 20 more. A desktop user has no terminal habit and often no `gaia` on PATH, so these messages leave them stuck. #6686 removed the cases added since rc4; this covers the rest, and the check that stops new ones.

Done when:
- no message that can reach the Agent UI names a `gaia …` command (CLI-only paths may keep theirs);
- the UI shows a plain explanation with an in-app way forward;
- a test fails CI when such text is added.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Technical details</summary>

Examples on main: `src/gaia/ui/server.py` (scheduled task needs init), `src/gaia/llm/gateway.py` (`gaia gateway auth` ×6, `gaia config set default_model`), `src/gaia/llm/lemonade_client.py` (`gaia init` ×6, `gaia daemon status`), `src/gaia/llm/lemonade_launcher.py`, `lemonade_choice.SWITCH_BACK_HINT`.

Approach:
- Give errors a CLI remedy and a UI remedy, or attach a structured action code the UI maps to a button.
- Add a unit test that scans UI-reachable message builders and the webui locale files for `gaia <subcommand>` and fails outside an explicit CLI-only allowlist.

CLAUDE.md "No CLI remedies" has no automated check today, which is how F5/#6673 slipped in. Found in v0.25.4-rc8 release testing.
</details>

issues.title: Search page shows "No records found" despite backend returning matching cases
issues.body:
## Description

The Cases search page (`/cases/search/`) does not display any results in the UI, even though the backend successfully returns the data. The same records are visible and searchable through the Django admin panel (`/admin/`), confirming the data exists and is accessible.

This bug has been reproduced on **two independent Kiwi TCMS deployments** with the same migrated dataset, ruling out local environment issues.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to **Cases → Search** (`/cases/search/`)
2. Apply any filter (e.g. select a Product) or leave filters empty
3. Click **Search**

## Expected Behavior

The results table renders the matching test cases.

## Actual Behavior

- UI shows "No records found" / empty table / loading spinner
- Network tab in DevTools confirms the server **does return the matching records** in the response payload
- The same records are fully visible and searchable in Django admin at `/admin/testcases/testcase/`
- Reproduced consistently with and without filters, on multiple browsers

This indicates the issue is on the frontend rendering layer (likely DataTables), not the backend or database.

## Environment

Reproduced on **two separate deployments**:

**Deployment 1** — Local Docker
- Kiwi TCMS version: <!-- popuni -->
- Containers: `kiwi_web` + `kiwi_db` (MariaDB)
- OS: <!-- macOS / Linux -->

**Deployment 2** — Azure (fresh deploy)
- URL: `https://kiwi-vog7lvqxtaiok.eastus.cloudapp.azure.com/`
- Same Kiwi version, fresh database populated via the same API migration
- Confirms the bug is not environment-specific

**Common factors:**
- ~9,935 test cases in database
- Database populated via API migration from another test management system
- Browser: <!-- Chrome / Firefox / Safari + version -->

## Additional Context

- Server response time is fast (~500ms); response payload is large (~12MB when no filter is applied)
- Restarting the `kiwi_web` container does not resolve the issue
- Searching with narrow filters (specific Product) produces the same UI failure — records present in response, not displayed in UI
- No visible JavaScript error in Console; rendering simply never completes

## Workaround

Users must access cases via the Django admin panel, which is not viable for non-admin testers and defeats the purpose of the search feature.

## Possible Cause

The DataTables frontend appears to fail silently when processing larger JSON payloads. Possibly related to client-side rendering limits or a parsing error that does not surface as a console error.

## Suggested Fix

- Enforce server-side pagination on `/cases/search/` regardless of filter state
- Or surface a clear error message when client-side rendering fails
- Consider a hard cap on result-set size returned to the frontend, with a UI warning to refine filters

issues.title: Execution matrix shows green for parameterized tests even if an execution failed in the run
issues.body:
### Description of problem

When a parameterized test is run multiple times during a test run (i.e. multiple test executions), the color assigned to the test in the test matrix (/telemetry/testing/execution/matrix/) appears to be the first execution of the test. This can lead casual observers to believe that all is good (or all is not good) when that is not actually the case.

### Version or commit hash (if applicable)

V16.1 

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a parameterized test case using a single parameter containing two possible values. (for example https://public.tenant.kiwitcms.org/case/46084/)
2. Create a test plan, and add the case created in step 1 to it.
3. Execute the test plan. Mark one of the test case executions as "passed" the other as "failed". (For an example, see https://public.tenant.kiwitcms.org/runs/14902/)
4. View the test execution matrix (https://public.tenant.kiwitcms.org/telemetry/testing/execution/matrix/)

### Actual results

On the public site, it is not possible to view the matrix.

On a private instance, the matrix can be viewed but the color assigned to the test case is either red or green.

### Expected results

a) It should be possible to view the matrix.

b) The color associated with the test run / test case should be something other than the "successful" or "failed" colors. Ideally, a tooltip would provide additional information about the specific reason that the case is in an intermediate state.

### Additional info (Python traceback, logs, etc.)

issues.title: Apostrophes are HTML-escaped in Test Run view when text is inside a YAML code block
issues.body:
### Description of problem
Text containing apostrophes is rendered inconsistently between the Test Case view and the Test Run execution view when the text is contained within a fenced YAML code block.

In the Test Case view, apostrophes are displayed correctly as '. However, when the same test case is executed within a Test Run, apostrophes inside the YAML code block are rendered as HTML entities (').

This causes the content displayed during test execution to differ from the content shown when viewing the test case.

### Version 
Kiwi TCMS 15.3
Kiwi TCMS 16.6-Enterprise DEMO

### Steps to Reproduce
https://public.tenant.kiwitcms.org/plan/16596/ - see the issue here

- Create or edit a test case.
- In the test case text, add a fenced YAML code block containing apostrophes:
```yaml
description: Access the user's profile page by clicking on the user's avatar
```
- Save the test case.
- Open the Test Case view and verify the content is rendered correctly.
- Add the test case to a Test Run or Plan and start execution.
- Observe the content displayed in the Test Run/Plan execution screen.

### Actual results
In the Test Case view:
```yaml
description: Access the user's profile page by clicking on the user's avatar
```
In the Test Run execution view:
```yaml
description: Access the user's profile page by clicking on the user's avatar
```

Apostrophes inside the YAML code block are HTML-escaped and displayed literally.

### Expected results
The content should be rendered identically in both views:
description: Access the user's profile page by clicking on the user's avatar
HTML entities should be decoded before rendering, including content inside fenced YAML code blocks.

### Additional info (Python traceback, logs, etc.)
The issue appears to be specific to fenced code blocks (tested with yaml). Regular text outside a code block renders correctly in both locations. The discrepancy is only observed when the text is displayed during Test Run/Plan execution.

issues.title: docs/mcp.md still says the repo is NVIDIA-internal and needs GitHub credentials, but it is public
issues.body:
## Summary

`docs/mcp.md` lines 47–51 still describe the repository as private:

> [!NOTE]
> Auto Ontology is NVIDIA-internal today, so this install needs GitHub credentials with
> access to the repository (`gh auth login`, or any cached git credential
> helper). It shortens to a plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` once the package is published to
> PyPI; until then `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` alone will not resolve.

The repository is now public (`"visibility": "public"`), so the `uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp"` install no longer needs authenticated GitHub access. The second half of the note is still accurate: the package is not on PyPI, so plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` does not resolve.

The first half now reads as a gate that isn't there. A reader with no `gh` auth configured may reasonably assume the MCP server is unreachable and stop, when the documented command works as-is.

## Evidence

`docs/mcp.md` as of `main` today:

```
$ gh api repos/NVIDIA/auto-ontology/contents/docs/mcp.md --jq '.content' | base64 -d | sed -n '47,51p'
> [!NOTE]
> Auto Ontology is NVIDIA-internal today, so this install needs GitHub credentials with
> access to the repository (`gh auth login`, or any cached git credential
> helper). It shortens to a plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` once the package is published to
> PyPI; until then `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` alone will not resolve.
```

Repository visibility:

```
$ gh api repos/NVIDIA/auto-ontology --jq '{visibility, private}'
{"visibility":"public","private":false}
```

The unauthenticated clone path resolves:

```
$ GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git /tmp/ao-check
Cloning into '/tmp/ao-check'...
remote: Enumerating objects: ...
```

## Suggested wording

The note can be shortened to the part that is still true:

> [!NOTE]
> The MCP package is not published to PyPI yet, so install it from the repository:
> `uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp`.
> It shortens to a plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` once the package is published.

## Impact

Docs only. No code, no behavior change. Affects anyone following the MCP setup instructions from outside NVIDIA — which, with the repository public, is now the default audience.

Happy to leave this to the maintainers given `CONTRIBUTING.md` says external contributions are not being taken; filing it as a note rather than a patch for that reason.
