Completion owner: [#1134](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1134). Gate `CP-05` in program `OPH-EXECUTABLE-COMPLETION-2026-10-29-v2`. [Common hypothesis](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/OPH_EXECUTABLE_HYPOTHESIS.md) · [Dependency DAG and gate contracts](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md) ## Dependencies - [ ] [#1139](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1139): Exhibit a localized native defect and its protecting invariant - [ ] [#1140](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1140): Derive common defect maintenance energy, kinetics and conserved stress Existing component work can proceed provisionally; integrated gate acceptance requires the actual maps to accepted predecessors. The same law, state/reference, observer access, clocks, energy and refinement domain must compose. A similarly named benchmark is not that map. ## Bounded completion tasks Finalize reproducible predictions and derive, implement or explicitly account for every premise consumed by one jointly consistent observer construction. Source: [claims/completion_work_queue.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/claims/completion_work_queue.json). Task completion records a bounded result; it does not accept a physical completion gate, discharge an unproved premise or add an independent physical comparison. Passing software tests alone does not establish a positive scientific outcome. The [execution and premise policies](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#bounded-completion-tasks) apply to every task. | Task | Bounded result | Owner | Status | Prerequisites | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [WQ-08](#work-wq-08) | Determine what the class census can say about species abundances | CP-05 / [#1141](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1141) | completed: positive | none | ### WQ-08: Determine what the class census can say about species abundances Owner: CP-05 / [#1141](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1141). Status: `completed: positive`. A thermal benchmark is a comparison input; class counting alone supplies neither a temperature nor physical species abundances. **Exact prompt** ```text Construct the exact six-class pushforward of the 32 declared occupation patterns, then the typed extension to Higgs and gauge components. Separately apply the PR-59 restriction omitting exterior degrees zero and five: its 30-pattern grammar excludes the right-handed-neutrino pair, so the 32-pattern extension must not silently inherit that premise. Compute rank, nullspace and sharp feasible bounds for selected species aggregates, explicitly exhibiting different nonnegative within-class populations with the same census. Distinguish code quanta from simulated flux faces and list the additional premise needed to apply the decoder to run counts. Test the proposed 75/25 reading and the restricted grammar's 24:6 component count rather than assuming uniform occupation. Define one temperature and neutrino-content convention for a comparison-only thermal benchmark using primary sources. Specify whether the benchmark concerns number density or energy density, its normalization, equilibrium and chemical-potential assumptions, mass approximation and physical helicity counting; use the corresponding fermion/boson statistical weights. State which abundance combinations the actual observable could test. No benchmark is a simulated cosmological history. ``` **Inputs and theorem reuse** - [model/defect_particle_classes/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/defect_particle_classes/PROOF.md) - [model/defect_particle_classes/results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/defect_particle_classes/results.json) - [model/native_abundance_epochs/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_abundance_epochs/PROOF.md) - [model/native_abundance_epochs/results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_abundance_epochs/results.json) - [model/defect_integer_lift/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/defect_integer_lift/PROOF.md) - [model/defect_particle_classes/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/defect_particle_classes/PROOF.md): Whole proof. Use the exact centre-class multiplicities and their known species degeneracies. Canonical premise references: PR-12, PR-47, PR-55, PR-59. **Bounded outputs** - `model/native_abundance_epochs/species_identifiability.py`: Exact class-to-species inverse problem and counterexamples. - `model/native_abundance_epochs/species_identifiability_results.json`: Observable abundance combinations and explicitly unidentifiable fractions. **Validation** ```sh python3 -m pytest -q model/native_abundance_epochs model/defect_particle_classes ``` Indistinguishable class-census controls produce different species fractions as certified. **Task closure** - Pass: Identifiable combinations and ambiguity bounds are exact; a claim about quark/lepton percentages is accepted only if the observable determines it. - Fail: Representation counts are used as dynamical probabilities or a shared centre label is treated as unique species identity. - Inconclusive: Retain the bounded computation, explicit resource limit and smallest unresolved premise. Do not mark a physical gate accepted. **Bounded completion evidence** - [model/native_abundance_epochs/species_identifiability_results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_abundance_epochs/species_identifiability_results.json): Exact 32/30-component maps and boson extensions have explicit nullspaces, sharp aggregate bounds and attaining indistinguishable populations. One extra bit resolves family totals; three labels resolve all selected species aggregates. The ideal 1 TeV comparison distinguishes number/energy weights; no native particle decoder or cosmological abundance match is claimed. Independent check: [model/native_abundance_epochs/test_species_identifiability.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_abundance_epochs/test_species_identifiability.py). ## Acceptance - [ ] Construct actual transport and charge conservation on the native state/process, with leakage and recovery bounds. - [ ] Show the physical accessible current content and matter lift, including extra modes and chirality; do not identify equivalent internal and spatial representations by name alone. - [ ] Distinguish stable defects, metastable/internal excitations and massless collective/transport modes; derive their observable and interaction maps on one law. - [ ] Prove every theorem premise assigned to this gate on the actual model and retained domain; bind the state, algebra, operations, clock and refinement maps in the existing premise ledger before invoking the conclusion. ## Obstruction and stopping Incompatible required charge/spin/statistics/current/transport structures exclude the covered defect realization. A 17-versus-12 response mismatch excludes its grammar, not every admissible current law. issues.title: [Completion CP-06] Obtain one interacting chiral 3+1 field description from native records
issues.body: ## Goal A refining same-process observation law with a nontrivial interacting chiral 3+1-dimensional effective field description and controlled detector/intervention correspondence. Completion owner: [#1134](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1134). Gate `CP-06` in program `OPH-EXECUTABLE-COMPLETION-2026-10-29-v2`. [Common hypothesis](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/OPH_EXECUTABLE_HYPOTHESIS.md) · [Dependency DAG and gate contracts](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md) ## Dependencies - [ ] [#1138](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1138): Construct the continuing regime, faithful reference and local modular clocks - [ ] [#1140](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1140): Derive common defect maintenance energy, kinetics and conserved stress - [ ] [#1141](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1141): Transport the same defects and derive particle identity and currents Existing component work can proceed provisionally; integrated gate acceptance requires the actual maps to accepted predecessors. The same law, state/reference, observer access, clocks, energy and refinement domain must compose. A similarly named benchmark is not that map. ## Next planned work Choose one existing charged-source family and compute the same dressed probe's energy-resolved spatial law at increasing finite capacities. Retain original spectral weight, compensating charge, failures and common clock. Test protection and transport on that law with CP-03/04/05; seek a stable branch with a nonzero interaction record before extending the physical continuum claim. Reuse [centre-class certificates](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/defect_particle_classes/README.md) and [complete charged field records](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/field_record_addenda/README.md). A class match alone does not transfer a state between the coherent register, Wilson sources and classical lattice runs. The joint dependency graph supplies the shared acceptance list. Finite gaps, prepared positive excesses and class labels do not identify rest masses or Lorentz spin. Keep the actual source action and reference fixed across the comparison or prove the transfer. A volume-uniform physical chiral limit requires its own error estimates. This assignment does not change the frozen component campaign or accept this gate. Wider primitives require the shared versioned contract. ## Bounded completion tasks Finalize reproducible predictions and derive, implement or explicitly account for every premise consumed by one jointly consistent observer construction. Source: [claims/completion_work_queue.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/claims/completion_work_queue.json). Task completion records a bounded result; it does not accept a physical completion gate, discharge an unproved premise or add an independent physical comparison. Passing software tests alone does not establish a positive scientific outcome. The [execution and premise policies](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#bounded-completion-tasks) apply to every task. First batch: [WQ-11](#work-wq-11). | Task | Bounded result | Owner | Status | Prerequisites | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [WQ-21](#work-wq-21) | Calibrate native quark spectral bins and test the mass dictionary | CP-06 / [#1142](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1142) | completed: negative | [WQ-01](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#work-wq-01) | | [WQ-11](#work-wq-11) | Calculate the missing odd spectral moment on one common source | CP-06 / [#1142](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1142) | ready | [WQ-01](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#work-wq-01) | | [WQ-12](#work-wq-12) | Resolve one concrete chirality-pairing premise | CP-06 / [#1142](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1142) | ready | [WQ-01](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#work-wq-01) | ### WQ-21: Calibrate native quark spectral bins and test the mass dictionary Owner: CP-06 / [#1142](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1142). Status: `completed: negative`. A calibrated source-energy display is permitted immediately. Physical running quark masses require a renormalization scheme/scale, flavour attachment and source-to-observable map; six empirical Yukawas are six supplied inputs. **Exact prompt** ```text Freeze the actual native_quark_response uc, dc and Q complete spectral bins on their stated Hamiltonian/reference/clock. Calculate scale-free interval ratios before applying any measured anchor. Implement an explicit single-anchor GeV projection of source excitation energies relative to the actual ground, with the reference cost4 subtracted exactly once; retain all other spectral bins and failure probabilities. Keep unnamed source energies separate from physical quark masses. Test the candidate dictionary that assigns the dominant uc/dc bins to up/down: their near-equal energy ratio cannot match the calibrated common-MZ up/down ratio through one multiplicative scale. Certify that bounded obstruction if it survives replay; do not promote exact local measure equality to equality of full interacting spectra. Bind comparison-only pure-MSbar tadpole-free values at mu=MZ=91.1876GeV to the empirical Yukawa/v packet, with all input ancestry and no fabricated joint matching uncertainty. State the smallest propagation/dispersion, three-family and renormalized-observable witnesses needed to replace a calibrated source-energy table by six physical running quark masses. A negative direct-dictionary result is valid completion and motivates a source or observable change, not a fitted offset or six independent claimed predictions. ``` **Inputs and theorem reuse** - [model/native_quark_response/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_quark_response/PROOF.md) - [model/native_quark_response/results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_quark_response/results.json) - [model/native_quark_response/full.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_quark_response/full.py) - [model/native_quark_response/research_reference.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_quark_response/research_reference.json) - [model/common_source/calibrated_matter_parameters.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/common_source/calibrated_matter_parameters.json) - [model/common_source/calibrated_matter_results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/common_source/calibrated_matter_results.json) - [model/particle_joint_reconstruction/dependencies.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_joint_reconstruction/dependencies.json) - [model/native_quark_response/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_quark_response/PROOF.md): Whole proof. Reuse complete native bins, original probabilities, actual-neutral reference subtraction and exact local flavour-degeneracy controls. Canonical premise references: none assigned. **Bounded outputs** - `model/defect_mass_catalogue/calibration.py`: Exact common-clock scale feasibility and signed energy conversion. - `model/defect_mass_catalogue/results.json`: Complete native quark bin conversion, retained original probabilities and excluded record-zero dictionary; all-family target inventory. - `model/defect_mass_catalogue/test_calibration.py`: Exact scale cancellation, incompatible clocks/conventions, unchanged reference subtraction and failure accounting. **Validation** ```sh python3 -m unittest model.defect_mass_catalogue.test_calibration ``` All exact arithmetic and inherited complete-record controls pass. ```sh python3 -m model.defect_mass_catalogue.catalogue --check ``` Frozen comparison, complete bin conversion and negative dictionary verdict reproduce. **Task closure** - Pass: The declared dictionary meets its ratio and source-observable conditions with explicit calibration ancestry, or a sharper bounded constructive map is proved. - Fail: Exact interval separation excludes the proposed common-scale quark dictionary; retain the obstruction and its source scope. - Inconclusive: Record the exact missing spectral or renormalization witness and bounded computations; no physical mass claim follows. **Bounded completion evidence** - [model/defect_mass_catalogue/results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/defect_mass_catalogue/results.json): The proposed dominant uc/dc-bin dictionary fails an exact one-scale feasibility test at the frozen common-MZ calibration. All native bins, reference-subtracted intervals and original failure/outside probabilities are retained. This does not exclude other source dictionaries or derive physical quark masses. Independent check: [model/defect_mass_catalogue/test_calibration.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/defect_mass_catalogue/test_calibration.py). ### WQ-11: Calculate the missing odd spectral moment on one common source Owner: CP-06 / [#1142](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1142). Status: `ready`. The odd-probe preparation and charged endpoint have distinct contracts. A finite moment or interaction witness does not establish a charged physical mass, dispersion relation or interacting continuum. **Exact prompt** ```text Compute or rigorously enclose the actual neighbour expectation m1 for one existing odd probe on the smallest feasible selected primary member. Use the shell-moment reduction and retain the complete original preparation, creation/removal outcomes, common clock and source-bound reference. Compare it with the corresponding energy-resolved spatial record; test whether a nonzero connected interaction on that same source and preparation is available. If the interaction observable belongs to a different preparation, quantify the missing transfer instead of combining their successes. Declare matrix/precision limits before execution. This odd probe has its own declared primary clock and preparation; the lepton-clock conversion and charged-endpoint localization are separate comparisons, not assumed prerequisites or interchangeable probes. ``` **Inputs and theorem reuse** - [model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/PROOF.md) - [model/particle_primary_coherent_odd_response/KERNEL_PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_coherent_odd_response/KERNEL_PROOF.md) - [model/particle_primary_original_shell_moments/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_original_shell_moments/PROOF.md) - [model/particle_primary_composite_transport/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_composite_transport/PROOF.md) - [model/particle_common_contract/contract.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_common_contract/contract.py) - [model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/PROOF.md): Whole proof. Use the exact shell reduction to the unresolved neighbour expectation instead of diagonalizing the full spectrum. - [model/particle_primary_coherent_odd_response/KERNEL_PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_coherent_odd_response/KERNEL_PROOF.md): Whole proof. Reuse the reduced set of component-summed original spectral measures. Canonical premise references: PR-50, PR-53, PR-54, PR-71. **Bounded outputs** - `model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/neighbour_moment.py`: Reduced exact or interval calculation of the actual odd neighbour moment. - `model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/neighbour_moment_results.json`: Moment enclosure and same-source spatial/interaction comparison. **Validation** ```sh python3 -m pytest -q model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules model/particle_primary_coherent_odd_response ``` Original spectral weight and kernel-reduction controls pass. **Task closure** - Pass: The missing finite moment is enclosed with non-vacuous error and its physical-consumer prerequisites are explicit. - Fail: An even-density contrast, supplied mass texture or a different-source contact interaction is reported as the odd probe result. - Inconclusive: Retain the bounded computation, explicit resource limit and smallest unresolved premise. Do not mark a physical gate accepted. ### WQ-12: Resolve one concrete chirality-pairing premise Owner: CP-06 / [#1142](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1142). Status: `ready`. A candidate-level chirality result does not establish an anomaly-free interacting chiral continuum. **Exact prompt** ```text Apply the proved reflected Gamma5 energy-law identity to one explicitly named proposed physical chirality dictionary. Determine whether it can remove the unwanted reflected response while preserving the complete charge/current instrument. If it cannot, prove the finite obstruction and state one minimal symmetry-breaking operator or alternate dictionary whose consequences can be tested without a parameter scan. Any changed action is a separately declared candidate with its own acceptance ancestry; do not silently change the primary program or call native Gamma5 physical Lorentz chirality. ``` **Inputs and theorem reuse** - [model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/PROOF.md) - [model/particle_primary_charge_conjugation/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_charge_conjugation/PROOF.md) - [model/standard_model_source_map/fermion_attachment.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/standard_model_source_map/fermion_attachment.py) - [model/particle_joint_reconstruction/CANDIDATE.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_joint_reconstruction/CANDIDATE.md) - [model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules/PROOF.md): Whole proof. Apply the all-capacity reflected Gamma5-law constraint to the proposed physical handedness map. Canonical premise references: PR-46, PR-47, PR-50. **Bounded outputs** - `model/standard_model_source_map/chirality_admission.py`: One explicit chirality dictionary admission or exclusion test. - `model/standard_model_source_map/chirality_admission_results.json`: Exact parity constraint, candidate domain and minimal unresolved premise. **Validation** ```sh python3 -m pytest -q model/particle_primary_odd_sum_rules model/particle_primary_charge_conjugation ``` Reflected-record equality remains intact and the proposed dictionary is tested against it. **Task closure** - Pass: The tested finite dictionary satisfies the retained charge/current and reflected-record constraints within its stated domain. - Fail: An exact reflected-record argument excludes the tested dictionary; retaining that counterexample narrows the construction without a universal no-go. - Inconclusive: Retain the bounded computation, explicit resource limit and smallest unresolved premise. Do not mark a physical gate accepted. ## Acceptance - [ ] Prove the declared continuum or effective-domain comparison for complete observable laws, with locality, quantum correlations, positivity/unitarity and controlled errors. - [ ] Retain every taste, chirality, dark mode and residue until a derived decoupling/removal map is supplied; obtain kinetic, Higgs and current responses jointly. - [ ] Keep the full photon-containing theory gapless; state separate massive thresholds, confinement observables, infrared and resonance conventions, and any pure Yang--Mills gap domain. - [ ] Prove every theorem premise assigned to this gate on the actual model and retained domain; bind the state, algebra, operations, clock and refinement maps in the existing premise ledger before invoking the conclusion. ## Obstruction and stopping A covered chirality, locality, positivity, continuum or interaction no-go stops the frozen realization class. A supplied scalar product, finite free symbol or pole list alone does not pass this gate. Route every exclusion to CP-12 with target version, mandatory premises, quantified class, evidence/independent checks, coverage, surviving escape routes and consequence. issues.title: [Completion CP-07] Freeze the physical dictionary and derive the matched particle spectrum
issues.body: ## Goal A source-selected spectrum, mixing and interaction packet in compatible physical conventions, using the same defects, energy, kinetics and observer clocks. Completion owner: [#1134](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1134). Gate `CP-07` in program `OPH-EXECUTABLE-COMPLETION-2026-10-29-v2`. [Common hypothesis](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/OPH_EXECUTABLE_HYPOTHESIS.md) · [Dependency DAG and gate contracts](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md) ## Dependencies - [ ] [#1142](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1142): Obtain one interacting chiral 3+1 field description from native records Existing component work can proceed provisionally; integrated gate acceptance requires the actual maps to accepted predecessors. The same law, state/reference, observer access, clocks, energy and refinement domain must compose. A similarly named benchmark is not that map. ## Next planned work Use one admitted interacting source, its actual state, clock and compensating reference to compute a persistent charged branch and the missing odd spectral moment. Test the declared coherent flavour transport in a complete interaction/readout experiment and identify what source data can split its up/down singular values. Carry the solved electric-sector family weights explicitly into a specified preparation and coupling comparison. Retain finite spectroscopy coverage, conditional neutrino inputs and paired hadron-scale covariance as separate domains. Use the [native coherent flavour word](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/native_flavour_transport/PROOF.md), [quantum sector measure](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/quantum_sector_measure/PROOF.md) and [complete neutrino mass instrument](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/neutrino_mass_observables/PROOF.md). A source architecture may be declared; matching its interacting poles and absolute units to observations requires the actual joint calculation. No target-informed scale, phase or beta-function choice counts as an independent prediction. Preserve the hypercharge mismatch, source multiplicities, lepton residual, quenched and one-spacing limits. Quark Yukawas, mixing and neutrino obligations stay in this gate; they are not satisfied by a centre-class dictionary. This assignment does not change the frozen component campaign or accept this gate. Wider primitives require the shared versioned contract. ## Bounded completion tasks Finalize reproducible predictions and derive, implement or explicitly account for every premise consumed by one jointly consistent observer construction. Source: [claims/completion_work_queue.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/claims/completion_work_queue.json). Task completion records a bounded result; it does not accept a physical completion gate, discharge an unproved premise or add an independent physical comparison. Passing software tests alone does not establish a positive scientific outcome. The [execution and premise policies](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#bounded-completion-tasks) apply to every task. | Task | Bounded result | Owner | Status | Prerequisites | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [WQ-04](#work-wq-04) | Freeze a no-fit lepton comparison and residual budget | CP-07 / [#1143](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1143) | completed: positive | none | | [WQ-05](#work-wq-05) | Certify the lepton coefficient bridge and its physical boundary | CP-07 / [#1143](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1143) | completed: positive | none | | [WQ-06](#work-wq-06) | Determine the sector measure consumed by the coupling chain | CP-07 / [#1143](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1143) | completed: positive | none | | [WQ-16](#work-wq-16) | Expose the source constraints on flavour and neutrino parameters | CP-07 / [#1143](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1143) | completed: negative | [WQ-01](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#work-wq-01) | ### WQ-04: Freeze a no-fit lepton comparison and residual budget Owner: CP-07 / [#1143](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1143). Status: `completed: positive`. This finalizes a conditional retrospective comparison, not the physical mass derivation. **Exact prompt** ```text Build a reproducible comparison for both lepton ratios with frozen editions of primary experimental inputs, uncertainties and available covariance. Keep theta=2/9 and balance=sqrt(2); do not tune the finite round count or any parameter to the residual. Separate exact architecture ratios, certified finite implementation error and the unproved physical mass map. Report the muon discrepancy, tau comparison and sensitivity to declared preparation errors without inventing a theory uncertainty. Retain a machine-readable calibration/exposure record and require primary-source citations for all reference values. ``` **Inputs and theorem reuse** - [model/lepton_cycle/sensitivity.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_cycle/sensitivity.py) - [model/lepton_cycle/results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_cycle/results.json) - [model/lepton_register_round/results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_register_round/results.json) - [model/completion/particle_mass_table.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/completion/particle_mass_table.json) - [model/lepton_cycle/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_cycle/PROOF.md): Whole proof. Use the exact shape Jacobian and reference-inclusive finite-round error without adjusting the phase. Canonical premise references: PR-13, PR-15, PR-75. **Bounded outputs** - `model/lepton_cycle/physical_comparison.json`: Two-ratio comparison with editions, covariance availability, exposed inputs and missing physical map. - `model/lepton_cycle/compare.py`: Deterministic comparison and no-fit guards. - `model/lepton_cycle/test_compare.py`: Target perturbation and calibration leakage controls. **Validation** ```sh python3 -m pytest -q model/lepton_cycle ``` Both ratios replay and changing comparison targets leaves model outputs unchanged. **Task closure** - Pass: Both ratios have reproducible residuals and correctly separated experimental, implementation and missing physical uncertainties. - Fail: The residual is removed by fitting, a tau marginal is presented as a joint likelihood, or finite-round error is used as an arbitrary physical correction. - Inconclusive: Retain the bounded computation, explicit resource limit and smallest unresolved premise. Do not mark a physical gate accepted. **Bounded completion evidence** - [model/lepton_cycle/physical_comparison.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_cycle/physical_comparison.json): Fixed theta=2/9 and balance=sqrt(2) give muon residual 9.833581 ppm and tau 30.935835 ppm against frozen primary references. Covariance availability, reference-only discrepancies, independent finite execution design, preparation bounds and empirical exposure are explicit; no physical mass-map or theory-error claim. Independent check: [model/lepton_cycle/test_compare.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_cycle/test_compare.py). ### WQ-05: Certify the lepton coefficient bridge and its physical boundary Owner: CP-07 / [#1143](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1143). Status: `completed: positive`. An exact coefficient bridge does not establish a physical energy generator, pole mass, Lorentz kinematics or absolute unit. **Exact prompt** ```text At fixed theta=2/9, construct the literal family-frame intertwiner between the complete native mass-read effect and the admitted charged-family coefficient C-dagger C/3. Preserve the actual preparation, normalization and charged representation. Prove or refute the coefficient identity and reject extra squaring, native-pair substitution and loss of the 5/4 preparation factor. Then build an admission table for the full state, kinetic normalization, reference, clock and physical mass-pole joins: coefficient equality cannot silently supply them. Give the smallest explicit same-source measurement needed to settle one absent join. Use no measured mass to choose the map. ``` **Inputs and theorem reuse** - [model/lepton_cycle/instrument.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_cycle/instrument.py) - [model/lepton_cycle/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_cycle/PROOF.md) - [model/standard_model_source_map/koide_source.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/standard_model_source_map/koide_source.py) - [model/charged_lepton_response/phase_selection.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/charged_lepton_response/phase_selection.py) - [model/charged_lepton_response/MASS_RESPONSE_BRIDGE.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/charged_lepton_response/MASS_RESPONSE_BRIDGE.md) - [model/charged_lepton_response/mass_response_bridge.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/charged_lepton_response/mass_response_bridge.py) - [model/particle_common_contract/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_common_contract/PROOF.md): Whole proof. Retain one source, state, reference, charge sector and clock through the comparison. Canonical premise references: PR-22, PR-50, PR-71. **Bounded outputs** - `model/lepton_mass_compiler/family_map.py`: Independent configured-action polynomial and literal native-effect Fourier intertwiner, including all normalization controls. - `model/lepton_mass_compiler/results.json`: Exact family map and explicit source/state/kinetic/reference/clock/physical admission table; compiled free-field witness. **Validation** ```sh VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 python3 -m pytest -q model/lepton_mass_compiler ``` All9 independent operator, archive, mass-readout and family-map controls pass. ```sh VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 python3 -m model.lepton_mass_compiler --check ``` Fresh full source reconstruction reproduces the complete receipt. **Task closure** - Pass: The literal coefficient bridge is proved with exact normalization and frame controls; every unmatched physical premise is explicit. - Fail: An exact coefficient or representation counterexample refutes the proposed bridge; defining source energy by the desired formula is invalid methodology, not a bridge. - Inconclusive: Retain the bounded computation, explicit resource limit and smallest unresolved premise. Do not mark a physical gate accepted. **Bounded completion evidence** - [model/lepton_mass_compiler/results.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_mass_compiler/results.json): The independent configured coefficient satisfies F E_native F-dagger=C_ex-dagger C_ex/3 with the exact5/4 preparation factor and geometric family frame. Extra squaring, pair substitution, active normalization and wrong Fourier orientation are rejected. The separately declared full-CAR compiler gives a controlled free rest-mass readout, with physical Standard Model, clock, Higgs vacuum and mirror conditions explicit. Independent check: [model/lepton_mass_compiler/test_compiler.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/lepton_mass_compiler/test_compiler.py). ### WQ-06: Determine the sector measure consumed by the coupling chain Owner: CP-07 / [#1143](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1143). Status: `completed: positive`. A finite sector measure does not by itself establish four-dimensional running or physical renormalization matching. **Exact prompt** ```text Fix one admitted source, operation set, electric-sector projectors and finite cutoff (with any required tail bound) before extraction. Derive sector transitions from the actual quantum channel and branch multiplicities, retaining no-ops and rejected outputs. For arbitrary within-sector states and coherences, prove adjoint preservation E*(P_j)=sum_i K_ij P_i; alternatively declare a restricted dephased or conditional-state family and prove its closure. Classical strong lumpability alone does not establish quantum sector closure. Solve stationary measures and remaining sector freedom exactly, or give a sector-preservation/nonclosure witness. Do not substitute the classical distance quotient for electric SU(2) sectors or identify finite-group and SU(2) labels without a map. issues.title: [Completion CP-10] Compose the realized Einstein response with matter and clock readouts
issues.body: ## Goal A common matter/geometry model that actually instantiates null balance and tensor completion and predicts its coupled coarse-scale gravitational response. Completion owner: [#1134](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1134). Gate `CP-10` in program `OPH-EXECUTABLE-COMPLETION-2026-10-29-v2`. [Common hypothesis](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/OPH_EXECUTABLE_HYPOTHESIS.md) · [Dependency DAG and gate contracts](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md) ## Dependencies - [ ] [#1145](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1145): Realize the joint modular, stress and entropy premises G1--G6 Existing component work can proceed provisionally; integrated gate acceptance requires the actual maps to accepted predecessors. The same law, state/reference, observer access, clocks, energy and refinement domain must compose. A similarly named benchmark is not that map. ## Bounded completion tasks Finalize reproducible predictions and derive, implement or explicitly account for every premise consumed by one jointly consistent observer construction. Source: [claims/completion_work_queue.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/claims/completion_work_queue.json). Task completion records a bounded result; it does not accept a physical completion gate, discharge an unproved premise or add an independent physical comparison. Passing software tests alone does not establish a positive scientific outcome. The [execution and premise policies](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#bounded-completion-tasks) apply to every task. | Task | Bounded result | Owner | Status | Prerequisites | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [WQ-15](#work-wq-15) | Validate source-premise admission to the Einstein composition | CP-10 / [#1146](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1146) | blocked | [WQ-14](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#work-wq-14) (positive/negative/inconclusive) | ### WQ-15: Validate source-premise admission to the Einstein composition Owner: CP-10 / [#1146](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1146). Status: `blocked`. A complete adapter is not a proof that every physical input exists; CP-10 acceptance requires all actual same-source premises. **Exact prompt** ```text Construct a typed adapter from the source gravity-witness receipt to the existing finite Einstein composition. Supply only premises proved on the same state, region map and clock. For each absent geometric or error-scaling premise, keep an explicit parameter in the conditional theorem and reject an unconditional admission. Demonstrate one positive synthetic theorem-instantiation control and one actual-source admission attempt, clearly distinguishing their domains. Do not replace missing source evidence with theorem names or defaults. ``` **Inputs and theorem reuse** - [model/matched_einstein_limit/PROOF.md](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/matched_einstein_limit/PROOF.md) - [Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/QuantitativeSmallBall.lean](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/QuantitativeSmallBall.lean) - [Lean/Geometry/SourceOrderEinsteinComposition.lean](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/Lean/Geometry/SourceOrderEinsteinComposition.lean) - [Lean/Geometry/EinsteinTensorBridge.lean](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/Lean/Geometry/EinsteinTensorBridge.lean) - [Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/Composition.lean](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/Composition.lean) - [Lean/Geometry/SourceOrderEinsteinComposition.lean](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/Lean/Geometry/SourceOrderEinsteinComposition.lean): Whole proof. Reuse the existing composition instead of reproving the abstract Einstein implication. - [Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/QuantitativeSmallBall.lean](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/QuantitativeSmallBall.lean): Whole proof. Propagate the actual matched small-ball errors and required scaling. - [Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/Composition.lean](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/Composition.lean): Anchor: `continuumEinstein_from_explicit_premises`. Instantiate the existing conditional continuum implication only with its full explicit premises. Canonical premise references: PR-23, PR-24, PR-25, PR-26, PR-27, PR-28. **Bounded outputs** - `model/matched_einstein_limit/source_admission.py`: Source-premise adapter with exact missing-input diagnostics. - `model/matched_einstein_limit/source_admission_results.json`: Actual-source admission verdict distinct from synthetic implication tests. **Validation** ```sh python3 -m pytest -q model/matched_einstein_limit ``` Synthetic complete witnesses pass; actual missing premises fail closed. ```sh cd Lean && lake build Geometry.SourceOrderEinsteinComposition ``` Existing finite implication compiles without proof holes. **Task closure** - Pass: A typed adapter correctly validates complete actual witnesses or returns their exact missing-premise set; synthetic controls are labelled and no physical acceptance follows from adapter correctness. - Fail: A concrete counterexample shows that the proposed adapter conflates source domains or admits a missing premise. - Inconclusive: Retain the bounded computation, explicit resource limit and smallest unresolved premise. Do not mark a physical gate accepted. ## Acceptance - [ ] Apply the existing conditional Einstein theorem with a checked map for every premise; do not replace the missing realization by reproving the tensor identity. - [ ] Obtain the Einstein equation up to its cosmological term, one positive Newton constant and universal coupling of the same defect maintenance energy/stress. - [ ] Propagate finite/refinement errors into gravitational observations. Keep a possible quantum spin-two graviton separate from the classical theorem and Standard Model content. - [ ] Prove every theorem premise assigned to this gate on the actual model and retained domain; bind the state, algebra, operations, clock and refinement maps in the existing premise ledger before invoking the conclusion. ## Obstruction and stopping A genuine counterexample satisfying every theorem premise refutes the affected implication. A necessary failure of joint gravitational response can exclude the frozen program only with CP-12 coverage of the admissible class. Route every exclusion to CP-12 with target version, mandatory premises, quantified class, evidence/independent checks, coverage, surviving escape routes and consequence. Candidate failure, class no-go, theorem error, empirical rejection, inconclusive search and resource stop remain distinct. A whole-program verdict requires coverage of every frozen admissible realization; a changed class is a new program version. ## Retained starting evidence - [paper/recovering_observer_spacetime_and_einstein_dynamics_from_overlap_consistency.tex](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/paper/recovering_observer_spacetime_and_einstein_dynamics_from_overlap_consistency.tex) - [flagship/from_observer_consensus_to_standard_physics.tex](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/flagship/from_observer_consensus_to_standard_physics.tex) - [Lean/Geometry/EinsteinTensorBridge.lean](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/Lean/Geometry/EinsteinTensorBridge.lean) - [model/common_source/null_tomography.py](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/common_source/null_tomography.py) Related earlier work: [#1026](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1026), [#1078](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1078). issues.body: ## Goal A continuing obstruction review across every gate, with exact scope, class coverage, independent checks and an explicit stop/continue verdict. The broad obstruction search #1078 is not established and owns that continuing research; this gate applies its scoped evidence to the new program decisions. Completion owner: [#1134](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1134). Gate `CP-12` in program `OPH-EXECUTABLE-COMPLETION-2026-10-29-v2`. [Common hypothesis](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/OPH_EXECUTABLE_HYPOTHESIS.md) · [Dependency DAG and gate contracts](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md) ## Dependencies - [x] [#1135](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1135): Freeze the executable program class and decision contract Existing component work can proceed provisionally; integrated gate acceptance requires the actual maps to accepted predecessors. The same law, state/reference, observer access, clocks, energy and refinement domain must compose. A similarly named benchmark is not that map. ## Bounded completion tasks Finalize reproducible predictions and derive, implement or explicitly account for every premise consumed by one jointly consistent observer construction. Source: [claims/completion_work_queue.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/claims/completion_work_queue.json). Task completion records a bounded result; it does not accept a physical completion gate, discharge an unproved premise or add an independent physical comparison. Passing software tests alone does not establish a positive scientific outcome. The [execution and premise policies](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/docs/COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md#bounded-completion-tasks) apply to every task. First batch: [WQ-17](#work-wq-17). | Task | Bounded result | Owner | Status | Prerequisites | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [WQ-01](#work-wq-01) | Account for every consumed premise and architectural input | CP-12 / [#1148](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1148) | completed: positive | none | | [WQ-17](#work-wq-17) | Instantiate operational observers and expose external resources | CP-12 / [#1148](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1148) | ready | none | ### WQ-01: Account for every consumed premise and architectural input Owner: CP-12 / [#1148](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/issues/1148). Status: `completed: positive`. This inventory supports a complete statement of assumptions. It does not derive all physical assumptions or prove consistency merely by counting rows. **Exact prompt** ```text Reconcile all canonical premise rows and every conditional assumption in the joint field/particle dependency graph with the lepton-cycle, population, charged-source and gravity claim inputs. Produce one current assumption-closure table, preserving canonical IDs. Classify each consumed input as proved on this source, imported theorem with matched hypotheses, declared architectural primitive, empirical calibration, open implementation, open physical map or rejected candidate; mark non-consumption explicitly. Include preparation independence, analyzer, kick/reset/archive, clock, squared-eigenvalue mass assignment, coupling measure, species dictionary and thermal history. Give each unresolved consumed row a completion owner and the smallest witness or counterexample needed. Prove that every source-specific discharge names its state, algebra, operation, reference, clock and domain. Do not turn a declaration or receipt hash into a proof. Bind coverage to a named source/proof/claim manifest at a specific revision; the coverage claim applies to that audited dependency set. Declared physical interpretations close disclosure only and retain their open implementation or physical-map obligation. ``` **Inputs and theorem reuse** - [tracking/premise_register.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/tracking/premise_register.json) - [claims/axiom_registry.yaml](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/claims/axiom_registry.yaml) - [model/completion/finite_attachment_map.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/completion/finite_attachment_map.json) - [model/completion/finite_record_dynamics.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/completion/finite_record_dynamics.json) - [model/particle_joint_reconstruction/dependencies.json](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/model/particle_joint_reconstruction/dependencies.json) - [claims/claim_registry.yaml](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/blob/main/claims/claim_registry.yaml) Canonical premise references: none assigned. **Bounded outputs** - `model/completion/assumption_closure.json`: Complete typed input inventory and ownership; canonical premise statuses retained unless proved. - `model/completion/assumption_closure.py`: Coverage and source-domain validator with missing-input and false-discharge controls. **Validation** ```sh python3 -m model.completion.assumption_closure ``` All canonical rows and joint-graph assumptions covered; missing and misclassified inputs rejected. ```sh python3 tools/check_claim_registry.py ``` Scientific claim dependencies remain valid. **Task closure** - Pass: Every canonical row and consumed unregistered service has an explicit disposition, source domain and owner. - Pass: Each claimed discharge has a mathematical witness; each open input has a bounded next action. - Fail: An input is absent, a calibration is advertised as an independent prediction, or incompatible source domains are pooled. - Inconclusive: Retain the bounded computation, explicit resource limit and smallest unresolved premise. issues.title: [BUG] Docs vs code (round 20): EoRA doc scripts force expandable_segments on ROCm (the documented corrupting config), stale rocm-rdna4 Paro AUTO/BLAS-pin claims, checkpoint.md support list omits qwen2/dynamic/MACaQ/NF12, errors name removed calibration_dataset_concat_size
issues.body:
Found on `main` @ 7b8f12785, AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1) and CPU-only (torch 2.15).

This is a docs-vs-code pass over README, `checkpoint.md` and `docs/`. Each item below was checked against actual behaviour on this host. Excluded: the export docs (being deprecated) and the known stale VPTQ cross-process note in `rocm-rdna4.md`. The AWQ GEMV_FAST/LLM_AWQ ROCm row of `rocm-rdna4.md` is filed separately as #5109.

## 1. The EoRA doc scripts force the allocator config that GPT-QModel avoids on ROCm (most user-impacting)
All four scripts under `docs/eora/` start with
```python
os.environ["PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF"] = "expandable_segments:True"
```
They are `eora_generation.py:21`, `post_quant_eora_generation.py:21`, `evaluation.py:21` and `eora_load_and_inference.py:21`. `docs/rocm-default-environment.md` says that on ROCm `expandable_segments:True` plus `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` "corrupts ordinary Torch results on ROCm 10.1 / gfx1201", which is why ROCm defaults to `max_split_size_mb:256,garbage_collection_threshold:0.7`. GPT-QModel then keeps the caller's value silently. With `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` set before `import gptqmodel` on the R9700, the result is:
```
ENV {'PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF': 'expandable_segments:True', 'PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF': None, 'PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF': None, 'ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT': '0'}
```
No warning is printed. A ROCm user who follows `docs/eora/README.md` therefore runs EoRA generation under the configuration the ROCm doc calls corrupting. Suggested fix: drop the line (`import gptqmodel` already installs the right per-platform default), or set it only when `torch.version.hip` is None.

## 2. `rocm-rdna4.md` Paro Triton row and text are stale since #5053 (#4914)
- Table row (`rocm-rdna4.md:54`): gfx1200 "✅ explicit `PARO_TRITON` only", and "AUTO keeps the Torch `ParoLinear` kernel".
- `rocm-rdna4.md:178`: "`SUPPORTS_FORMATS[FORMAT.PARO] = 0` means `PARO_TRITON` is never chosen by `AUTO`; selecting it explicitly is required on every platform."

In the code, `ParoTritonLinear.SUPPORTS_FORMATS = {FORMAT.PARO: 10}`, and `auto_select_priority()` promotes it on ROCm. Measured result: a Paro checkpoint reloaded with `backend="auto"` on the R9700 gives `{'ParoTritonLinear': 14}`. On CPU it gives `ParoLinear`. The README 7.11.2 notes ("Paro selects Triton on ROCm") are correct; the RDNA4 page contradicts them.

## 3. The ROCm BLAS-pin docs say Paro keeps hipBLASLt, but the code pins rocBLAS for it
- `rocm-default-environment.md:78`: "AWQ, Paro and weight-only (RTN) accumulate none of these and keep hipBLASLt." The same page's flowchart and before/after table say Paro is "pinned rocBLAS" (#4460).
- `rocm-rdna4.md:104-106`: the pin list "GPTQ, QQQ, VPTQ, MACaQ, EXL3, calibrated FP8 GSQ or an EoRA adapter ... now pins rocBLAS, and every other method pins hipBLASLt" omits Paro.

In the code, `_DETERMINISTIC_BLAS_PROCESSOR_STEPS` (`gptqmodel/models/base.py:173-182`) contains `ProcessorStep.PARO`. Both sentences should name Paro as pinned.

## 4. The `checkpoint.md` "Supported configurations" list no longer matches the adapter
`checkpoint.md:204-218` lists model types `llama` and `qwen3_moe`, the methods "GPTQ, RTN, AWQ, QQQ, Paro, EXL3, FP8, GGUF, and bitsandbytes", and says "dynamic per-module quantization/exclusions" is unsupported. The code differs:
- `CHECKPOINT_MODEL_TYPES = {"llama", "qwen2", "qwen3_moe"}` (`looper/gptq_checkpoint.py:290`).
- `MacaqProcessor` declares `CheckpointSupport.PRIMARY` (`looper/macaq_processor.py:74`). The README 7.11.2 notes say "NF12 and MACaQ can resume from checkpoints".
- `validate_checkpoint_support()` does not reject `dynamic`, and `dynamic` (including runtime exclusions) is part of the checkpoint identity.

Measured on CPU with a real 2-layer Qwen2.5-0.5B copy (`model_type=qwen2`). For each case I ran a full checkpointed `quantize()`, then a fresh process with `CheckpointConfig(resume="required")` on the same path, and compared every state-dict tensor:

| config | first run | resume (`required`) | differing tensors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPTQ 4-bit + `dynamic={r"+:.*\.1\..*": {"bits": 8}}` | 30.2 s | 1.1 s | 0 / 83 |
| GPTQ 4-bit + `dynamic={r"-:.*\.1\.mlp\.down_proj": {}}` | 50.1 s | 4.8 s | 0 / 79 |
| `NF12Config()` | 8.0 s | 0.5 s | 0 / 55 |
| `MacaqConfig()` (bf16) | 330.7 s | 20.8 s | 0 / 69 |

All of these work, but the doc tells users that qwen2, `dynamic`, MACaQ and NF12 are not supported.

## 5. Calibration error messages name the removed keyword `calibration_dataset_concat_size`
Since #4724 the user-facing name is `CalibrationConfig.concat_size`. Several messages that reach users still use the old keyword:
- `gptqmodel/utils/calibration.py:195`: "Quantize: `calibration_dataset_concat_size` is token-based and cannot be used ..."
- `:1159`: "Quantize: calibration_dataset_concat_size=... exceeds ..."
- `:1351`: `_require_tokenizer("`calibration_dataset_concat_size` is specified")`
- `:1476`: "`calibration_dataset_concat_size` must be larger than `min_length`."

`quantize(calibration_concat_size=...)` and similar old keywords raise `TypeError`, so a user who follows these messages hits a dead end. They should say `CalibrationConfig.concat_size`. Other messages in the same file already name `CalibrationConfig.min_length`.

## Checked and consistent (no action)
- README quick start: inference (ROCm AUTO -> TorchLinear) and quantize -> save -> reload -> generate with `CalibrationConfig` on Qwen3-0.6B.
- Every `CalibrationConfig` default in README and `calibration-config.md`; `HessianConfig.sink_row_cap_median_multiple=4.0`. With `desc_act=False` the cap is bitwise inert (0/28 tensors differ).
- `CheckpointConfig`, `P2PConfig` and all 68 `KernelConfig`/`RuntimeConfig` defaults in `kernel-config.md`.
- The ROCm allocator and `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT` defaults, caller precedence (incl. `PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF`), and the CUDA `expandable_segments` default. `QuantizeConfig(runtime=RuntimeConfig(rocm_quant_blas="hipblaslt"|""))` skips the pin and warns as documented.
- AUTO kernel selection on ROCm and CPU for GPTQ 4/8, AWQ GEMM/GEMV, RTN, QQQ, GGUF, FP8, NF12, EXL3, Paro, MACaQ, BnB and VPTQ. All match the tables apart from item 2 and #5109.
- The offload run-directory lifecycle (in-session model has no meta tensors and survives deleting the run dir; the run dir is removed on failure). `peft.md` (GPTQ mixed-bit via plain Transformers == native; AWQ `torch_awq` LoRA grads). `reshard()`. EoRA in-quantize and post-quant flows. The rotation opt-in gate. Rejection of `exclude_attention_sinks` by VPTQ and Paro.

issues.title: [BUG] #4706 (fix of #4664) incomplete: default FP8Config checkpoints still write quant_method 'fp8', so plain transformers routes them to FineGrainedFP8: ~15 min of 3.9G-element CPU dequant, then a shape error (no refusal, no save-time warning)
issues.body:
Found on `main` @ 7b8f12785, CPU (transformers 5.22). Checkpoint: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct quantized on this box with the default `FP8Config()`.

## What is wrong
#4706 (fix of #4664) made GPT-QModel-only layouts fail closed in plain transformers, but only for `bitsandbytes`. The FP8 half of #4664, reported in the follow-up comment on that issue, is still open:

- `FP8Config()` (default `weight_scale_method="row"`, `weight_scale_semantics="inverse"`) writes `quant_method: "fp8"` with a per-row `weight_scale_inv`. Transformers registers its own `fp8` quantizer (`FineGrainedFP8`, which expects 128x128 block scales), so `REFUSED_HF_QUANT_METHODS` (`gptqmodel/_quant_methods.py:27-42`) cannot register a refusing quantizer for it (`setdefault` keeps the transformers one, `docs/hf-interop.md:277-279`).
- `hf_compat_warnings` (`models/writer.py:319+`) emits nothing for FP8, so the checkpoint carries no label either. GGUF had the same name collision, and it was solved by publishing `gptqmodel_gguf` instead (`writer.py`, the `METHOD.GGUF` branch).

`docs/support-matrix.md:16` marks FP8 as not loadable by Transformers, and `docs/hf-interop.md`'s failure contract promises that a GPT-QModel-only layout "raises when gptqmodel is imported". What actually happens with `import gptqmodel` and `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(ckpt, device_map="cpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)`:

```
[transformers] Using FP8 quantized models requires a GPU or XPU, we will default to dequantizing the model to bf16
Loading weights: ... 223/290 [12:20<03:51, 3.30s/it]
model.layers.{0...23}.mlp.down_proj.weight | CONVERSION |
  File ".../transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py", line 1172, in _dequantize_one
    return (q * s).to(output_dtype).reshape(original_shape)
RuntimeError: shape '[896, 4864]' is invalid for input of size 3904897024
RuntimeError: We encountered some issues during automatic conversion of the weights. For details look at the `CONVERSION` entries of the above report!
```
Before failing, transformers broadcasts the `[896]` row scale against the `[896, 4864]` codes into a 3.9-billion-element temporary (`896*4864*896`) for every projection. Over ~15 minutes the 290 weight conversions run at 2-6 s each, and the final error never mentions GPT-QModel or FP8 scale layout. The same happens without `import gptqmodel`. For comparison, `GPTQModel.load` of the same checkpoint gives nll 2.896 (`TorchFP8Linear`). The issue body of #4664 recorded the same behaviour at 12c1273c2, so nothing has changed for FP8.

## Suggested fix
Do what was done for GGUF: write non-block FP8 checkpoints under a GPT-QModel-specific `quant_method` (for example `gptqmodel_fp8`), add that name to `REFUSED_HF_QUANT_METHODS`, and teach the GPT-QModel loader to read both names. Keep `quant_method: "fp8"` only for `weight_scale_method="block"` layouts that FineGrainedFP8 can actually read. At minimum, add an FP8 entry to `hf_compat_warnings` so the saved checkpoint is labelled.

## Test that should have caught it
`tests/test_checkpoint_interop_4053.py::test_hf_from_pretrained_refuses_every_gptqmodel_only_method` and `tests/test_checkpoint_compat.py::test_hf_compat_warning_for_every_gptqmodel_only_method` iterate only `REFUSED_HF_QUANT_METHODS`, so FP8 is never exercised.

## Severity
Medium for interop. A default-config FP8 checkpoint is not loadable by plain transformers, and the attempt costs about 15 minutes of CPU and huge temporaries before failing with a misleading error.

issues.title: [MEM] AWQ token_rows copies every calibration token of every module to host and samples ~1% only after the layer forward: peak host RAM grows linearly with calibration size (OLMoE-2L 6.4 -> 17.8 GiB for 128 -> 512 docs, GPTQ 2.7 -> 3.8) and hits 28 GiB/layer with ExpertsRoutingOverride; retained rows stay 906
issues.body:
Found on `main` @ 7b8f12785, RTX 4090 (CUDA 13.2, torch 2.15) and Radeon AI PRO R9700 (ROCm), Python 3.14, glibc.

### What is wrong
With the default `token_rows` aggregation, AWQ keeps only a bounded sample of each module's input: `_token_row_budget` gives one largest-batch equivalent, 906 rows on 128 C4 docs. But `_record_input_feature` (`looper/awq_processor.py:1108`) first copies **every** calibration token of every captured module to host memory, and holds all of it until the end of the layer's forward. Only then does `_layer_input_features` (`:2296-2398`) run `_pack_token_rows` and drop the rest.

The scale search, `x_mean`, the replay loss and the clip search all read only the packed rows (`inp` in `_search_best_scale` is the packed `[1, 906, hidden]` tensor). So 98-99% of the captured host bytes are written and never read. Peak host RAM per layer therefore grows linearly with:
- the number of calibration tokens. The retained sample does not grow: `docs/awq-calibration-aggregation.md` says "the bound does not grow with the number of calibration documents", which holds for the packed tensor but not for the capture;
- the expert fan-out. With `MoEConfig(routing=ExpertsRoutingOverride())`, every expert captures every token.

GPTQ on the same looper folds each batch into a Hessian and stays flat.

### Measurements (peak `RssAnon` sampled every 0.5 s during `quantize()`; default `AWQConfig(bits=4, group_size=128)` vs `GPTQConfig(bits=4, group_size=128)`, bf16, `batch_size=1`, C4 rows of 2500 chars)
OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 truncated to 2 layers (`num_hidden_layers=2` in a config copy), RTX 4090:

| calibration | tokens | AWQ peak RssAnon | GPTQ peak RssAnon | AWQ rows retained per module (logged `raw -> retained`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 docs | 64,652 | **6.39 GiB** | 2.69 GiB | 64652 -> 906 (attention), 7449 -> 128 (an expert) |
| 512 docs | 256,655 | **17.78 GiB** | 3.80 GiB | 256655 -> 906 |

4x the calibration data adds +11.4 GiB of AWQ host RAM, and the scale search still sees the same 906 rows.

OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 truncated to 4 layers, `ExpertsRoutingOverride()` (all 64 experts per token), 128 docs, R9700:
- AWQ: every layer spikes from 3.6 GiB at the layer boundary to **25.9 / 23.6 / 27.8 / 25.4 GiB** RSS (`ru_maxrss` 28.25 GiB). Every expert module logs `raw 64652 -> retained 906`.
- GPTQ with the same override: peak 3.98 GiB.

Full OLMoE-1B-7B (16 layers, native routing, 128 docs), RTX 4090: AWQ quantize peak RSS 7.22 GiB, GPTQ 3.84 GiB.

The size matches a full-token capture. Per OLMoE layer it is about 64652 x 2 B x (2048 q/k/v + 2048 o_proj + 2048 MoE root + 8 x 2048 gate/up + 8 x 1024 down) = 3.9 GiB at top-8, and 26 GiB at 64-expert override. The same formula for Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, 2048/768) with `ExpertsRoutingOverride()` and 128 docs gives ~45 GiB per layer. With a typical 1024-doc x 2048-token calibration set at native top-8, it gives ~90 GiB per layer, all to retain a few thousand rows per module.

### Minimal repro
```python
import json, gzip, torch, threading, time
from gptqmodel import GPTQModel
from gptqmodel.quantization.config import AWQConfig, GPTQConfig, CalibrationConfig
def anon():
    return next(int(l.split()[1]) for l in open("/proc/self/status") if l.startswith("RssAnon")) / 2**20
peak = [0.0]; stop = threading.Event()
def sample():
    while not stop.is_set(): peak[0] = max(peak[0], anon()); time.sleep(0.5)
texts = [t[:2500] for t in (json.loads(l)["text"] for l in gzip.open("c4-train.00000-of-01024.json.gz", "rt")) if len(t) >= 1500][:512]
m = GPTQModel.load("olmoe_2_layers", AWQConfig(bits=4, group_size=128), dtype=torch.bfloat16)   # or GPTQConfig
threading.Thread(target=sample, daemon=True).start()
m.quantize(CalibrationConfig(dataset=texts)); stop.set()
print(f"peak RssAnon {peak[0]:.2f} GiB")
```
```
AWQ  128 docs: 6.39   512 docs: 17.78
GPTQ 128 docs: 2.69   512 docs:  3.80
```

### Suggested fix
Bound the capture, not only the packed result:
- For `token_rows` modules, keep a per-module streaming sample while capturing. The per-batch quota can be derived from the calibration lengths, which the looper knows before the layer forward (`largest_batch_rows` and the batch count are known up front for dense modules). For routed experts, use a deterministic reservoir or a per-batch stride. Then drop the rest of each batch's capture immediately instead of appending it to `entry["inputs"]`.
- Where provenance is needed (`_token_row_replay_kwargs`), record `(batch, row)` for the kept rows at capture time, as `_pack_token_rows` already does.
- If an exact match with the current deterministic sample is required, do a two-pass selection: the row indices depend only on per-batch row counts, so the indices for batch *b* can be fixed as soon as the counts are known.

### Test that should have caught it
No test measures AWQ host memory against calibration size. Two checks would have caught this: a CPU test that captures N vs 4N batches on a tiny MoE and asserts the peak captured host bytes stay within ~2x of `retained * hidden * dtype`, and a check that `entry["inputs"]` never holds more than the budget.

### Severity
Medium ([MEM]). No wrong output, but a large host-RAM waste that scales with calibration size and expert fan-out. AWQ on a large MoE with `ExpertsRoutingOverride` (the documented remedy for starved experts) or with a larger calibration set can run out of host RAM, while the same run with GPTQ stays at a few GiB.

issues.title: [PERF] #4594 (fix of #4545) incomplete: TorchFP8Linear (CUDA AUTO for FP8) still decodes every weight through FP32 plus a transpose copy per forward: bs1 decode 7.6x slower than dense fp16 on sm_120 (Llama-3.1-8B layers)
issues.body:
Found on `main` @ 7b8f12785, RTX 5090 (sm_120), torch 2.15 + CUDA 13.2, transformers 5.22.

### What is wrong
With the default `FP8Config()` (weight-only, `weight_scale_method="row"`, `activation_quant_method="none"`), CUDA AUTO loads `TorchFP8Linear`, and every forward runs `_forward_dequant_matmul` -> `dequantize_weight` -> `_dequantize_native` (`gptqmodel/nn_modules/qlinear/fp8.py:627-669`). That function makes several full-weight passes on every call, for every layer, including each decode step:

1. `deq = weight.to(torch.float32)`: writes 4 B/element.
2. `deq.div_(scale_inv.view(-1, 1))`: reads and writes the fp32 weight.
3. `.to(target_dtype)`: reads fp32, writes fp16.
4. `.transpose(0, 1).contiguous()`: a full transpose copy, only so that `matmul_fp32_reduce` gets an `[in, out]` operand.

That is about 24 B of memory traffic per weight element for a 1 B/element format, before the GEMM. #4594 (fix of #4545) moved the GEMM back to native fp16. It kept this FP32 decode and the transpose copy, so the FP8 kernel is now far slower than the dense fp16 model it replaces. `torch.profiler` for one `mlp.gate_proj` call (4096 -> 14336) at M=1 shows `aten::copy_` 146 us x4, `div_` 308 us, transpose copy 164 us, and the GEMM 48 us.

### Numbers
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct truncated to 8 decoder layers (same layer shapes as the 8B; vocab/lm_head dense in both). `FP8Config()` quantized with GPTQModel, fp16, batch 1, CUDA events, GPU otherwise idle:

| | dense HF fp16 | FP8 AUTO (`TorchFP8Linear`) |
|---|---|---|
| decode step, bs1 (DynamicCache) | 3.62 ms | **27.6 ms (7.6x slower)** |
| decode step, bs8 | 3.95 ms | 27.4 ms (6.9x) |
| prefill 512 / 2048 tokens | 11.1 / 39.6 ms | 35.5 / 66.3 ms (3.2x / 1.7x) |
| `generate()` 128 tokens, bs1 | 254 tok/s | **36 tok/s** |
| `q_proj` / `gate_proj` / `down_proj` at M=1 | 23 / 79 / 83 us | 194 / 959 / 966 us |

For reference, GPTQ 4-bit (Marlin) on the same model decodes at 3.49 ms/step and AWQ Marlin at 3.41 ms.

Emulating a leaner path on the same modules: cast the FP8 codes straight to fp16, run the GEMM on the transposed view with an fp32 output, and apply the per-row inverse scale to the output (`torch.mm(x, w.to(fp16).t(), out_dtype=torch.float32) * (1/scale_inv)`, then round once):

| module, M | current | cast + GEMM + row-scale epilogue | rel diff vs current |
|---|---|---|---|
| gate_proj, 1 | 959 us | 204 us | 3.1e-4 |
| down_proj, 1 | 967 us | 204 us | 2.8e-4 |
| q_proj, 1 | 192 us | 51 us | 2.9e-4 |
| gate_proj, 2048 | 2070 us | 1429 us | 3.0e-4 |

(The fp32 output keeps the unscaled product out of fp16 overflow. Done in fp16 output, `down_proj` at M=2048 overflowed.) The same applies to `"tensor"` scales. For `"block"` scales, the fp32 round trip and the transpose copy could still be dropped by scaling in the target dtype when `_weights_fit_activation_dtype` already says it is range-safe.

### Repro
```python
m = GPTQModel.load("<Llama-3.1-8B FP8Config() ckpt>", backend=BACKEND.AUTO, dtype=torch.float16)
lin = m.model.model.layers[0].mlp.gate_proj          # TorchFP8Linear, row scales
x = torch.randn(1, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
with torch.inference_mode(), torch.profiler.profile(activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as p:
    for _ in range(20): lin(x)
print(p.key_averages().table(sort_by="cuda_time_total", row_limit=8))   # copy_/div_/transpose >> mm
```

### Suggested fix
- Range-safe weights (`_native_gemm_eligible`): decode straight to the activation dtype. Use the `[out, in]` weight as a transposed view (`F.linear`/`mm` on `.t()` needs no copy). For row/tensor scales, apply the scale in an fp32 output epilogue instead of on the full weight.
- Longer term, a fused W8A16 FP8 kernel (for example the Marlin FP8 variant) would make the FP8 format faster than fp16 at decode instead of 7x slower.

### Test that should have caught it
There is no throughput check comparing the FP8 kernel with a dense fp16 `nn.Linear` at M=1. A ratio bound on a 4096x14336 layer would catch both the fp32 round trip and the transpose copy.

### Severity
Medium [PERF]: the default FP8 format is 7.6x slower than fp16 at batch-1 decode on the default CUDA kernel.

issues.title: [BUG] TorchFP8Linear per-token (W8A8) output is silently wrong on sm_121: torch._scaled_mm accepts the row-wise scale layout but does not apply it (rel error ~1e3)
issues.body:
Found while verifying FP8 tests on an NVIDIA GB10 (`sm_121`, torch 2.11.0+cu130, aarch64). `TorchFP8Linear` with per-token activation quantization (W8A8) produces **silently wrong output** on this device: `torch._scaled_mm` accepts the row-wise scale layout but does not apply it.

## What is wrong

`_can_use_scaled_mm` (`gptqmodel/nn_modules/qlinear/fp8.py:713`) enables the native path whenever

```python
self.activation_quant_method == "per_token" and self.weight_scale_method in {"tensor", "row"}
```

That is the row-wise contract: `scale_a` is `(tokens, 1)` and `scale_b` is `(1, out_features)`. On `sm_121` with this torch build, cuBLASLt's rowwise path either refuses or returns a result that does not match `(A@B) * scale_a * scale_b`:

| `scale_a` | `scale_b` | result |
|---|---|---|
| `(1,1)` | `(1,1)` | correct (`rel=0.000`) |
| `(M,1)` | `(1,1)` | `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` |
| `(1,1)` | `(1,N)` | `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` |
| `(M,1)` | `(1,N)` | **runs, `rel=1063` (wrong output)** |
| `(M,)`, `(1,M)` | any | `Invalid scaling configuration` |

Only the exception cases are caught (`forward()` sets `_scaled_mm_hard_disabled` on a raised error). The `(M,1)` + `(1,N)` combination raises nothing and returns wrong values, so the module keeps the path for every later forward.

Probe (CUDA, fp8 e4m3, `M=7, K=N=64`):

```python
xq = (torch.randn(7, 64, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
wq = (torch.randn(64, 64, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
sa = torch.linspace(0.5, 1.5, 7, device="cuda").reshape(7, 1)
sb = torch.linspace(0.5, 1.5, 64, device="cuda").reshape(1, 64)
ref = (xq.float() @ wq.t().float()) * sa * sb
out = torch._scaled_mm(xq, wq.t(), scale_a=sa, scale_b=sb, out_dtype=torch.float16)
print(((out.float() - ref).abs() / ref.abs().clamp_min(1e-6)).max())   # ~1063
```

## Symptom in the suite

Two tests are red on `main` on this host (they pass on the maintainer hosts in the issue tracker):

```
FAILED tests/kernels/test_fp8_kernel.py::test_fp8_scaled_mm_matches_dense_reference[tensor-float8_e4m3fn]
FAILED tests/kernels/test_fp8_kernel.py::test_fp8_scaled_mm_matches_dense_reference[row-float8_e4m3fn]
  Greatest absolute difference: 1.3759765625 at index (2, 48) (up to 0.05 allowed)
```

The test's reference is correct: I checked it against the FP8 operands and both scales directly (`dense vs fp8-ref maxabs = 8e-4`), while `_forward_scaled_mm` is off by 1.375.

## Severity

Medium-high. It is opt-in (`activation_quant_method` defaults to `"none"` = W8A16), but a caller who opts into W8A8 gets plausible-looking, wrong logits with no warning, on the newest NVIDIA hardware. The project's contract is fail-closed for kernels that cannot compute the documented math.

## Suggested fix

Make the row-wise `_scaled_mm` path fail closed on hardware/torch builds that cannot compute it, instead of trusting that it raises:

- Probe once per process (cached next to `_scaled_mm_hard_disabled`): a tiny `16x16` FP8 GEMM with `scale_a=(M,1)`, `scale_b=(1,N)` compared against `(A@B) * scale_a * scale_b` in FP32. Disable the path when the call raises **or** the result is outside a loose tolerance.
- Then `_can_use_scaled_mm` returns `False` for the per-token branch on this host, `forward()` takes the existing dequantize + matmul fallback (correct, slower), and the two tests skip instead of failing.

Note: draft PR #5173 edits the same functions (`_can_use_scaled_mm`, `_forward_scaled_mm`) for W8A16 decode, so this should land after (or inside) that change to avoid a conflict.
