st.data_editor NumberColumn drops not allowed characters without any feedback - a silent data-corruption trap
issues.body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary When typing into a `NumberColumn` cell of `st.data_editor`, any character that the number editor does not accept is silently discarded. The most dangerous case is the decimal separator: in an app using `.` as the decimal separator, a user whose habit or OS locale uses `,` (e.g. Finland, Germany, Poland, Netherlands, Brazil) types `1,23`, the `,` is dropped and the cell commits `123` — a value 100× too large that looks perfectly plausible in the grid. There is no visual feedback at any point: the character simply does not appear, the cell is not marked as invalid, and the wrong value is returned to Python as a valid edit. In data-entry applications this is a silent data-corruption trap that is very easy to overlook. This is not a request to support other locales/separators (that is covered by #11164 / #1353). The point is more general: **the editor should never silently change what the user typed**. Rejected input should be either shown and marked invalid (like other invalid cell values) or at least clearly signalled, so the user is aware the value was not accepted as typed. A very similar silent-drop problem was recently fixed for a leading `.` (#16909, fixed in #16920), which shows the same class of issue is considered a bug. The `,` case (and any other rejected character) still behaves this way. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import pandas as pd import streamlit as st df = pd.DataFrame({"Item": ["I'll enter 1,23 here", "I'll enter 1.23 here"], "Factor": [0.1, 0.1]}) edited = st.data_editor( df, column_config={"Factor": st.column_config.NumberColumn("Factor", format="plain")}, hide_index=True, ) st.write(edited) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Run the app above (browser language: English, so `.` is the decimal separator). 2. Select the `Factor` cell in the first row ("I'll enter 1,23 here"), type `1,23` and press Enter. 3. Select the `Factor` cell in the second row ("I'll enter 1.23 here"), type `1.23` and press Enter. 4. Compare both cells and the values returned by `st.data_editor` (shown by `st.write(edited)` below the editor). ### Expected Behavior - Second row: `1.23` is accepted and returned as `1.23` (this works today). - First row: `1,23` must not be silently turned into another number. One of the following (in order of preference): - The typed text `1,23` stays visible in the cell editor, the cell is marked invalid (same red/invalid treatment used for other values that fail validation) and the value is not committed — the cell keeps `0.1`, or - The input is rejected with a visible message/indicator explaining that `,` is not a valid character / decimal separator. In no case should a different number than what the user typed be committed silently. It may be configurable on the column level (e.g. dropNotAllowedCharacters : bool = True), in case there are users preferring the current way. ### Current Behavior - First row: the `,` keystroke is ignored, the editor shows `123` and on Enter `123.0` is committed and returned by `st.data_editor` as a normal edit. - Second row: `1.23` is committed correctly. - The two rows now show `123` and `1.23` although the user intended the same value; no error, warning or visual indication is shown for the first row. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.52.2 (also verified on 1.67.0) - Python version: 3.11 - Operating System: Windows 11 - Browser: Google Chrome 157.0.8103.38 (Official Build) (64-bit) - Also observed in Streamlit in Snowflake. ### Additional Information - Root cause appears to be the Glide Data Grid number overlay editor (`react-number-format` `NumericFormat`), which strips characters that do not match the configured decimal/thousand separators. Streamlit sets `thousandSeparator: ""` in `NumberColumn`, so the decimal separator is the only non-digit character accepted; everything else is dropped before Streamlit's own `validateInput` sees it. - Related issues: #16909 (same silent-drop symptom for a leading `.`, fixed in #16920), #11164 (pasting localized numbers, kept open as an enhancement), #7702, #1353 (i18n). - Current workaround is to use a `TextColumn` with a `validate` regex and convert in Python, but this loses numeric sorting and right alignment, so it is not a good general solution.
